Case_History_Text: EMS handoff: This is a 65-year-old man brought from home with his spouse for sudden, severe chest pain extending toward the upper back. He reports episodes on and off since yesterday evening, with increased intensity before calling 911. He is short of breath and has a sheen of sweat, lightheadedness, and fatigue that feels excessive for the day. He also noticed a sour taste in his mouth. History includes high blood pressure and type 2 diabetes; his father and older brother had vascular disease. He works as a high school coach and was resting at home when symptoms worsened.

Symptoms: sudden severe chest pain; upper-back pain; dyspnea; fatigue out of proportion to the day; dry cough; occasional indigestion
Case_History_Text: A 75-year-old retired accountant presents to the emergency department alone for sudden severe pain in the center of her chest with discomfort extending into the upper back. She reports that it began earlier today while she was at home sorting through household papers and has persisted for most of the day, with periods of increased intensity. She describes associated shortness of breath and says she feels unusually fatigued compared with what she accomplished today. She has also noticed a dry cough without sputum. She denies recalling a fall, unusual exertion, or recent respiratory illness. She reports occasional indigestion over the past several months but says today’s symptoms feel more substantial and have not resolved as they sometimes do after resting. She has been able to walk but feels less steady because of the discomfort and breathlessness. She drove herself partway before asking a neighbor to bring her to the hospital, and she is currently concerned because the pain remains present.

Symptoms: sudden severe chest and upper-back pain; shortness of breath; lightheadedness; mild nausea
Case_History_Text: I’m 65 and work on a farm. About two hours ago, while I was finishing chores, I suddenly developed very severe pain across my chest and upper back. It came on quickly and has stayed intense. I feel short of breath and somewhat lightheaded, and I have mild nausea but have not vomited. I called EMS because I was worried, and they brought me here; I came alone. I’ve had occasional indigestion over the years, though this feels more severe than that. I was treated for anxiety several years ago, but I have not needed medication recently. I don’t remember injuring myself or doing anything unusual before the pain started.

Symptoms: sudden severe chest pain; upper-back pain; shortness of breath; diaphoresis; unusual fatigue; uneasy stomach
Case_History_Text: 57F librarian brought to ED by adult daughter for approx 6 hrs of sudden severe central chest and upper-back pain with SOB. Reports a sheen of sweat, fatigue out of proportion to her day, and an uneasy feeling in her stomach. Pain began abruptly while finishing paperwork at the library and has persisted with fluctuating intensity. Denies recent injury. Long smoking history, now reduced to several cigarettes/day; known high cholesterol and family history of vascular disease. Appears uncomfortable and mildly anxious at triage, speaking in short but complete sentences.

Symptoms: sudden severe chest pain; upper-back pain; shortness of breath; unusual fatigue; mild nausea
Case_History_Text: I am his wife, and I brought my 53-year-old husband to the emergency department after calling EMS. He had been shelving books at the library earlier and said he felt unusually exhausted, far more than the day seemed to warrant. About three hours ago, he suddenly developed intense pain in the center of his chest that also reached into his upper back. He became short of breath and looked uncomfortable, though he was able to answer questions. He mentioned mild nausea but has not vomited. The pain has continued despite resting at home, so I called for help. He has type 2 diabetes and usually manages his daily activities independently. He has not described anything similar recently.

Symptoms: sudden severe chest pain; upper-back pain; shortness of breath; sour taste in mouth; unusual fatigue; dry cough
Case_History_Text: Hello, I am a 48-year-old woman who arrived at the emergency department with my spouse. About 45 minutes ago, while I was sitting after finishing part of my security shift, I suddenly developed severe pain in the middle of my chest that also involves my upper back. I feel short of breath and unusually exhausted, more than would make sense for the day. I have noticed a sour taste in my mouth and have had a dry cough, but no fever. The pain has remained intense and has made it difficult to get comfortable. My medical history includes type 2 diabetes and longstanding high blood pressure. I do not know what is causing this and would appreciate urgent evaluation.

Symptoms: sudden severe chest pain; upper-back pain; shortness of breath; lightheadedness; mild nausea; dry cough
Case_History_Text: EMS handoff: This is a 50-year-old man, a librarian, brought in by his adult daughter after we were called for sudden severe chest and upper-back pain that began earlier today. He describes the pain as intense and persistent, with shortness of breath and lightheadedness. He also reports mild nausea and a dry cough over the past day. He was able to walk to the stretcher but appeared uncomfortable and anxious. History includes longstanding high blood pressure, and he reports that a parent had heart disease at an early age. No other history was available during transport.

Symptoms: sudden severe chest pain; upper-back pain; shortness of breath; mild nausea; uneasy stomach sensation
Case_History_Text: A 42-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with a coworker for sudden severe pain in the center of her chest and upper back that began last night while she was at home. She describes the discomfort as intense and persistent, with periods of worsening, and says it has made it difficult to take a satisfying breath. She reports mild nausea and an uneasy sensation in her stomach but has not vomited. She denies recent injury or unusual exertion. The symptoms have caused considerable concern, and she came directly from work with a nurse colleague after deciding they were not improving. Her medical history is notable for high blood pressure; she is unsure whether she took her usual medication this morning. She reports no prior similar episode and no known heart or lung condition. On arrival, she remains uncomfortable and short of breath but is able to answer questions clearly.

Symptoms: sudden severe chest pain; upper-back pain; shortness of breath; intermittent episodes since yesterday evening; sweating; unusual fatigue; sour taste in mouth
Case_History_Text: I’m 68 and work as a restaurant cook. Yesterday evening, I suddenly developed severe pain in my chest that seemed to reach into my upper back. It eased after a while, then returned several times overnight and again today without a clear pattern. When it comes on, I feel short of breath and get a sheen of sweat, even when I’m sitting still. I’m more exhausted than I should be after the kind of day I had. I’ve also noticed a sour taste in my mouth. I have type 2 diabetes and smoked for many years, though I’ve cut down a lot. My neighbor called EMS and came with me to the emergency department because the pain became intense again.

Symptoms: sudden severe chest and upper-back pain; dyspnea; dry cough; lightheadedness; marked fatigue; sour taste in mouth
Case_History_Text: 46-year-old woman, home health aide, arrives to ED with coworker after sudden onset of severe central chest and upper-back pain earlier today. Pain has persisted for most of the day; reports shortness of breath, dry cough, lightheadedness, and fatigue out of proportion to her activity. Notes a sour taste in her mouth but no clear food trigger. PMH includes type 2 diabetes and obesity; spends much of the workday seated between visits. States her parent had heart disease at an early age. Appears uncomfortable and speaks in full sentences.

Symptoms: sudden severe chest pain; upper-back pain; shortness of breath; lightheadedness; uneasy feeling in the stomach
Case_History_Text: I am his daughter, and I met my 81-year-old father in the emergency department after his neighbor brought him in by EMS. He is a retired nurse who had been sitting at home when he suddenly developed intense pain across his chest and into his upper back about two hours ago. He says the discomfort came on abruptly and has remained severe. Since then, he has felt short of breath, lightheaded, and unusually uneasy in his stomach. He looks frightened and keeps shifting in the bed, saying he cannot get comfortable. He has smoked for much of his life, although he has cut down considerably in recent years. He denies any recent injury, and neither he nor the neighbor can identify a clear trigger.

Symptoms: sudden severe chest and upper-back pain; shortness of breath; lightheadedness; dry cough; uneasy stomach sensation
Case_History_Text: Hello, I am a 52-year-old woman and a rideshare driver. About six hours ago, while finishing an afternoon shift, I suddenly developed very strong pain across my chest and upper back. It has stayed intense and makes it hard to breathe normally. I have also felt lightheaded, noticed a dry cough, and had an uneasy feeling in my stomach. The pain has made me anxious, but it does not feel like my usual worry. A coworker met me nearby and drove me to the emergency department because I did not feel safe continuing. I had anxiety treated several years ago and have had high blood pressure for a long time. I have not had an injury or similar episode before.

Symptoms: sudden severe chest and upper-back pain; shortness of breath; fatigue out of proportion to activity; lightheadedness; mild nausea; sour taste in mouth
Case_History_Text: EMS handoff: This is a 76-year-old man, a security guard, brought in by his adult daughter after we were called for sudden severe pain across the chest and upper back that began about three hours ago while he was resting at home. He reports shortness of breath, unusual fatigue beyond what he would expect from his day, lightheadedness, and mild nausea. He also noticed a sour taste in his mouth. He has occasional indigestion, obesity, and a largely sedentary work routine. His family reports a history of vascular disease. He remained awake and able to answer questions during transport.

Symptoms: sudden severe chest pain; upper-back pain; shortness of breath; diaphoresis
Case_History_Text: A 67-year-old woman was brought to the emergency department by her spouse for abrupt onset of severe central chest and upper-back pain beginning approximately 45 minutes before arrival. She had been sitting at home after returning from a morning shift as a home health aide when the discomfort started without a clear preceding exertion or injury. She describes the pain as intense and persistent, with pressure-like discomfort in the chest and aching across the upper back. She has felt short of breath since the onset and appears to have a sheen of sweat on her forehead. Her spouse reports that she looked frightened and briefly needed to sit forward while walking to the car. She denies recent falls, heavy lifting, or a known respiratory illness. Her medical history includes high blood pressure; she is unsure of the names of all her medications. She has not had similar symptoms of this severity previously.

Symptoms: chest pain; palpitations; dyspnea; dizziness; lightheadedness; shortness of breath
Case_History_Text: A 75-year-old woman, retired from nursing, presents to the emergency department with her neighbor for 45 minutes of chest discomfort, palpitations, shortness of breath, and dizziness. She describes the chest sensation as a pressure-like discomfort across the upper chest that began while she was seated at home, without a clear precipitating event. The palpitations feel like intermittent rapid or uneven beats and have occurred alongside lightheadedness. She denies fainting. Her breathing feels more difficult than usual, though she has been able to speak in full sentences and walk with assistance. She reports no recent fever, cough, vomiting, or known injury. The neighbor states that she appeared pale and uneasy but remained alert throughout the trip. She has a long history of cigarette use and says she has cut down substantially in recent years. She is unsure whether similar symptoms have occurred previously and provides no additional details about established heart conditions.

Symptoms: Chest pain; palpitations; dyspnea; dizziness; lightheadedness; sour taste in mouth; uneasy stomach feeling
Case_History_Text: I’m a 58-year-old librarian, and my adult daughter came with me after we called EMS. Since yesterday, I’ve had episodes of pressure-like discomfort in the middle of my chest, along with a fluttering or pounding feeling in my heartbeat. I get short of breath walking across the room and feel dizzy or lightheaded, though I have not fainted. There’s also been a sour taste in my mouth and an uneasy feeling in my stomach. The symptoms come and go, without a clear pattern, and I feel more tired than usual. I smoked for many years and have cut down substantially. A doctor once mentioned that my heartbeat was irregular, but I was not given a clear explanation. I have no other details to add.

Symptoms: chest pain; palpitations; dyspnea; dizziness; mild nausea; dry cough; sour taste; sweating
Case_History_Text: 64-year-old woman, retail manager, arrived alone to ED with chest pressure beginning last night, intermittent and unchanged in position. Reports episodes of palpitations, shortness of breath, and lightheadedness, with mild nausea and a sheen of sweat. Also notes a dry cough and sour taste in her mouth. She says her heart does not feel persistently rapid. Long smoking history, now reduced; high cholesterol. She recalls being told once that her heartbeat was irregular but has no further details. No recent illness or injury reported. Appears worried and is speaking in full sentences.

Symptoms: intermittent chest pain; palpitations; shortness of breath; dizziness; sour taste in mouth; mild nausea
Case_History_Text: I brought my 83-year-old father to the emergency department after calling EMS because he had been having episodes of chest discomfort since yesterday evening. He is a retired mechanic and usually manages on his own. The discomfort has come and gone, sometimes with a feeling that his heart is beating unusually or unevenly. During the episodes he says it is harder to catch his breath and that he feels lightheaded, though he has not fainted or fallen. He mentioned a sour taste in his mouth and mild nausea but has not vomited. He cannot identify a clear trigger, and resting has not consistently stopped it. He had anxiety treated several years ago, but this seems different to me.

Symptoms: chest pain; palpitations; shortness of breath; dizziness; mild nausea; uneasy stomach feeling; unusual fatigue
Case_History_Text: Hello emergency team, I am a 77-year-old retired postal worker. Since late this morning, I have had intermittent chest discomfort along with a fluttering or pounding feeling in my chest. I have also felt short of breath, lightheaded, and unusually tired for what has otherwise been a quiet day. There is a mild nauseated, uneasy feeling in my stomach, but I have not vomited. My husband brought me to the emergency department because the symptoms have kept returning and I do not feel like myself. My mother had heart problems at a relatively young age. I was treated for anxiety years ago, though this feels different enough that I wanted to be checked.

Symptoms: chest pain; palpitations; dyspnea; dizziness; dry cough; uneasy stomach sensation; sweating; lightheadedness
Case_History_Text: EMS brings a 68-year-old man from home after his spouse called for about two hours of intermittent chest pressure with a noticeable racing or irregular heartbeat, shortness of breath, dizziness, and lightheadedness. He reports a dry cough, an uneasy feeling in his stomach, and a sheen of sweat but denies fainting. He is a retail manager with occasional indigestion, untreated sleep apnea, and a parent who developed heart disease at an early age. His spouse says he appeared pale and uncomfortable while resting in a chair. He arrives alert, speaking clearly, and accompanied by his spouse.

Symptoms: chest pain; palpitations; shortness of breath; dizziness; sour taste in mouth
Case_History_Text: A 56-year-old woman was brought to the emergency department by a neighbor after developing approximately six hours of intermittent chest discomfort while taking a break from driving for a rideshare service. She describes the discomfort as a pressure and tightness in the center of her chest, occurring in episodes lasting several minutes, without a clear positional or exertional pattern. During the episodes, she notices a pounding or fluttering sensation in her chest, shortness of breath, and lightheadedness but has not fainted. She reports a sour taste in her mouth and mild nausea but denies vomiting. The symptoms have waxed and waned, with incomplete relief during rest. She denies fever, cough, recent illness, leg swelling, or focal weakness. She has smoked for many years and recently reduced the number of cigarettes per day. She reports no recent surgery or prolonged immobilization. Her neighbor states that she appeared pale and anxious before coming in, though she remained able to walk to the car.

Symptoms: Chest pain; palpitations; shortness of breath; dizziness; fatigue
Case_History_Text: I’m 58 and work as a restaurant cook. About three hours ago, while I was getting ready for the evening shift, I started feeling a pressure-like ache in the middle of my chest. My heart began fluttering or skipping, and I became short of breath and lightheaded. I had to sit down because I felt unsteady, though I did not pass out. I’m unusually wiped out for how little I’ve done today. There’s also been a sour taste in my mouth, which made me wonder about indigestion, but the chest discomfort has continued. My spouse called EMS and came with me to the emergency department. I had anxiety years ago and was treated for it, and a doctor once mentioned that my heartbeat seemed irregular, but I never had a clear explanation.

Symptoms: chest pain; palpitations; dyspnea; dizziness; diaphoresis; mild nausea; sour taste; lightheadedness
Case_History_Text: 56-year-old woman, librarian, arrived to ED with spouse for 45 min of central chest pressure and intermittent racing/irregular heartbeat. Reports shortness of breath, dizziness, and feeling faint without syncope. Spouse notes a sheen of sweat. Mild nausea and sour taste in mouth; denies vomiting. History includes type 2 diabetes, obesity, and sedentary work. Reports parent with early heart disease. No additional history available at triage. Appears anxious but conversant and able to walk from waiting area. No obvious respiratory distress noted.

Symptoms: chest pain; palpitations; dyspnea; dizziness; sour taste in mouth; marked fatigue
Case_History_Text: I am his daughter, and I came to the emergency department after he called EMS from home. My father is 68 and works as a software engineer. He arrived by ambulance alone because I live across town. Since yesterday, he has had intermittent chest discomfort, describing it as pressure that comes and goes, along with a sensation that his heart is fluttering or beating irregularly. He has also felt short of breath and dizzy, especially when walking across the room. He mentioned a sour taste in his mouth but no clear meal-related pattern. What worries me most is that he seems unusually exhausted, far more than expected after a normal day. He has a history of high blood pressure and takes medication for it.

Symptoms: chest pain; palpitations; dyspnea; dizziness; mild nausea; sweating; uneasy stomach sensation
Case_History_Text: Hello, I am a 72-year-old woman who came to the emergency department with my daughter because I have felt unwell since last night. I have had pressure-like discomfort in my chest that comes and goes, along with a fluttering or uneven feeling in my heartbeat. I get short of breath walking across the room and feel lightheaded, though I have not fainted. There is mild nausea, a clammy sheen of sweat, and an uneasy sensation in my stomach. I worked as a postal worker until recently. I have untreated sleep apnea, and a clinician once mentioned that my heartbeat sounded irregular, but I have not had this combination of symptoms before. Please let me know what information you need.

Symptoms: chest pain; palpitations; dyspnea; dizziness; dry cough; mild nausea; fatigue
Case_History_Text: EMS brings a 74-year-old retired teacher to the ED with his neighbor after a call from his apartment this morning. He reports episodes of central chest discomfort and a sensation of his heart fluttering or racing, occurring on and off since yesterday evening. During episodes he becomes short of breath, dizzy, and unusually fatigued, with mild nausea but no vomiting. He has also noticed a dry cough. He denies fainting or recent injury. His history includes anxiety treated years ago, untreated sleep apnea, and one prior comment that his heartbeat was irregular. He was conversational and able to walk to the stretcher.
Model_Diagnosis: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response

Symptoms: chest pain; palpitations; dyspnea; dizziness; diaphoresis; mild nausea
Case_History_Text: A 77-year-old retired nurse arrives at the emergency department with her neighbor after experiencing intermittent chest discomfort for most of today. She describes a pressure-like sensation across the upper chest, occasionally accompanied by awareness of her heartbeat and mild shortness of breath. She has felt lightheaded when standing or walking but has not fainted. A sheen of sweat developed during one episode, and she reports mild nausea without vomiting. The discomfort has fluctuated in intensity and is present again on arrival, though she is able to speak in full sentences. She denies recent fever, cough, leg injury, or prolonged travel. She has a history of episodic irregular heartbeats treated with a daily rate-controlling medication and says her pulse sometimes feels uneven at home. She also reports anxiety treated several years ago but feels today’s symptoms are different from her usual anxious episodes. Her neighbor states she appeared pale and uncomfortable before coming in.

Symptoms: chest pain; palpitations; shortness of breath; dizziness; mild nausea; unusual fatigue
Case_History_Text: I am a 71-year-old man and work as a librarian. About two hours ago, while shelving books, I noticed a pressure-like discomfort in the middle of my chest along with my heart feeling as though it was beating unevenly. I became short of breath and lightheaded, so I sat down. The discomfort has continued off and on, and I feel more tired than seems reasonable for the day. I have had mild nausea but have not vomited. A coworker stayed with me and called EMS, who brought me to the emergency department. I have high cholesterol. I was treated for anxiety several years ago, but this feels different from my usual anxious episodes. I do not recall any recent illness or injury.

Symptoms: chest pain; palpitations; dyspnea; dizziness; lightheadedness; mild nausea; uneasy stomach feeling; fatigue
Case_History_Text: 84-year-old woman, unemployed, brought to ED by adult daughter for ~6 hrs of intermittent chest pressure with awareness of a racing or irregular heartbeat, SOB, dizziness, and lightheadedness. Reports an uneasy feeling in her stomach, mild nausea, and fatigue out of proportion to activity. No reported fainting. History includes HTN, high cholesterol, and one prior mention of an irregular heartbeat; details unclear. Symptoms began while resting at home and have fluctuated, with no clear trigger. Patient appears worried but is able to speak in full sentences. Triage evaluation initiated.

Symptoms: chest pain; palpitations; shortness of breath; dizziness; unusual fatigue
Case_History_Text: I brought my 74-year-old father to the emergency department after calling EMS from his home. He has felt unwell for about three hours, beginning with a pressure-like discomfort in the center of his chest and a sensation that his heart was beating irregularly or forcefully. He became short of breath while walking from the kitchen and said he felt lightheaded, though he did not faint. The fatigue seemed far greater than what would be expected after an ordinary day. He usually works as a postal worker and is normally active. He has not mentioned a recent illness or injury. He has untreated sleep apnea and does not use his prescribed nighttime equipment consistently. EMS brought him in, and I stayed with him because he seemed anxious and unusually tired.
Model_Diagnosis: New-onset atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response

Symptoms: chest pain; palpitations; shortness of breath; dizziness; mild nausea; sweating; unusual fatigue
Case_History_Text: I am a 67-year-old woman who arrived at the emergency department with my spouse after symptoms began about 45 minutes ago. I was sitting during a break from my security-guard shift when I noticed pressure across the middle of my chest and a fluttering, uneven feeling in my heartbeat. I became short of breath and dizzy when I stood, with mild nausea and a cool sheen of sweat. I feel much more exhausted than seems reasonable for the day, although I have not done anything strenuous. I sometimes have indigestion, but this feels different enough to worry me. I am obese and spend most of my workday seated at a desk. My spouse drove me in, and the symptoms are still present but have not rapidly worsened.

Symptoms: chest pain; palpitations; dyspnea; dizziness; lightheadedness; diaphoresis; dry cough; shortness of breath
Case_History_Text: EMS brings a 75-year-old man to the emergency department with his adult daughter after he developed intermittent central chest discomfort and a sensation of his heart fluttering over the past day. He reports increasing shortness of breath, a dry cough, dizziness, and episodes of feeling lightheaded, with a sheen of sweat during the latest episode. He is a retired mechanic who describes years of limited activity and has a history of high blood pressure and obesity. His father had heart disease at a young age. On arrival he is awake, speaking clearly, and not in obvious distress; his pulse is not markedly rapid.

Symptoms: chest pain; palpitations; shortness of breath; dizziness; mild nausea
Case_History_Text: A 71-year-old woman was brought to the emergency department by a neighbor for chest discomfort that began last night while she was resting at home. She describes intermittent pressure across the upper chest with episodes of a fluttering or irregular heartbeat. The discomfort has recurred several times today and is accompanied by shortness of breath, lightheadedness, and mild nausea. She denies fainting, coughing, fever, or recent illness. She has not noticed leg swelling and reports no recent travel or prolonged immobility. The patient works as a nurse and initially hoped the symptoms would pass, but contacted her neighbor after feeling dizzy while walking from the kitchen. She has a history of high blood pressure and states that she takes her prescribed medication, though she cannot recall the name. She reports no known prior heart problems. On arrival, she is speaking in full sentences and appears mildly anxious but not acutely distressed.

Symptoms: intermittent chest pain; palpitations; shortness of breath; dizziness; uneasy stomach feeling; sour taste; mild nausea
Case_History_Text: I’m 76 and retired from nursing. Since yesterday evening, I’ve had episodes of pressure-like discomfort in the middle of my chest that come and go. During them, my heart feels as though it is fluttering or beating unevenly, and I get short of breath and lightheaded. I’ve also noticed an uneasy feeling in my stomach, a sour taste in my mouth, and mild nausea. I can’t identify one clear trigger; resting helps somewhat, but the symptoms return. I was treated for anxiety years ago, though this feels different enough to worry me. My parent had heart disease at an early age. My neighbor stayed with me and called EMS, and they brought me to the emergency department.

Symptoms: chest pain; palpitations; dyspnea; dizziness; lightheadedness; mild nausea; uneasy stomach sensation
Case_History_Text: 60F, welder, presents to ED with spouse for chest discomfort and intermittent palpitations present most of today. Reports SOB, dizziness, and feeling lightheaded, with an uneasy sensation in her stomach and mild nausea. Symptoms began while doing routine activities and have waxed and waned; denies collapse. Appears mildly anxious but conversant. Hx anxiety treated several years ago, untreated sleep apnea, and long smoking history, now reduced. No acute distress noted at triage. Awaiting further evaluation.

Symptoms: chest pain; palpitations; shortness of breath; dizziness; lightheadedness; dry cough
Case_History_Text: I brought my 64-year-old uncle to the emergency department after calling EMS because he had been feeling unwell for about two hours. He is a janitor and was alone at home when the symptoms began. He described a pressure-like discomfort across the front of his chest, along with a sensation that his heart was beating irregularly. He became short of breath while walking from the kitchen and said he felt lightheaded, though he did not faint or fall. He has also had a dry cough without bringing anything up. By the time we arrived, he was awake, speaking clearly, and still uncomfortable but not visibly distressed. His medical history includes type 2 diabetes, and he takes daily prescribed medication. He has no family with him besides me.

Symptoms: chest pain; palpitations; shortness of breath; dizziness; sweating; uneasy stomach feeling
Case_History_Text: I am 68 and work as a high school coach. About six hours ago, while getting ready to leave for an evening practice, I noticed a pressure-like discomfort in the center of my chest along with a fluttering, uneven-feeling heartbeat. I became short of breath and lightheaded, especially when walking across the room. I have also had a sheen of sweat and an uneasy feeling in my stomach, but no vomiting. The discomfort has eased and returned rather than fully going away. A neighbor drove me to the emergency department and is waiting with me. I have high blood pressure and smoked for many years, though I have cut down substantially. I have not had this combination of symptoms before.

Symptoms: chest pain; palpitations; shortness of breath; dizziness; lightheadedness; uneasy stomach sensation; sweating
Case_History_Text: EMS brings a 62-year-old man, a city bus driver, to the emergency department with his spouse after a call from home. He reports three hours of intermittent chest discomfort with awareness of his heartbeat, shortness of breath, and lightheadedness. He describes an uneasy sensation in his stomach and says his wife noticed a sheen of sweat. He denies fainting. He has had occasional indigestion, smoked for many years but has cut down, and was treated for anxiety several years ago. During transport he remained alert and able to speak in full sentences; symptoms persisted without a clear trigger.

Symptoms: chest pain; palpitations; dyspnea; dizziness; diaphoresis; sour taste in mouth
Case_History_Text: A 53-year-old woman, a construction foreman, presented to the emergency department with her spouse for 45 minutes of intermittent chest discomfort, palpitations, shortness of breath, and dizziness. She describes the chest sensation as pressure with occasional sharper twinges, centered behind the breastbone and not clearly related to movement or breathing. The discomfort began while she was reviewing plans at home after work and has fluctuated without fully resolving. She noticed a sheen of sweat, felt mildly lightheaded when standing, and reported a sour taste in her mouth without vomiting. Her spouse says she appeared anxious but remained able to speak in full sentences. She recalls being told once that her heartbeat was “irregular,” though she has not pursued regular follow-up and is unsure of the circumstances. She denies fainting, recent illness, leg swelling, or known injury. She arrived ambulatory, accompanied by her spouse, and remained concerned that the sensations were becoming more frequent.

Symptoms: sudden dyspnea; pleuritic chest pain; cough; chest tightness; wheezing; lightheadedness
Case_History_Text: A 28-year-old woman was brought to the emergency department by a coworker after developing sudden shortness of breath at her graphic design studio approximately 45 minutes earlier. She describes a tight sensation across the chest with sharper discomfort when taking a deep breath or coughing. She has had repeated bouts of cough and notices a faint wheeze, which she says began around the same time as the breathing difficulty. She reports feeling lightheaded but has not fainted. The discomfort is not clearly related to movement, and she is unsure whether it changes with eating or position. She denies fever, chills, vomiting, or known recent respiratory illness. Her coworker says she appeared anxious and briefly had to sit on the floor. The patient has a history of high blood pressure and takes a daily prescribed medication, though she is uncertain of the name. She reports no prior similar episode and is not aware of any medication allergies. She is speaking in full sentences on arrival but remains visibly uncomfortable.

Symptoms: sudden shortness of breath; sharp chest pain worse with breathing; cough with occasional wheeze; chest tightness; heavy-feeling legs; low-grade feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: I am 69 and work as a high school coach. Yesterday, while sitting at home after dinner, I suddenly became short of breath and felt a sharp pain on the right side of my chest when I took a deep breath. I have been coughing since then, sometimes with a wheezy sound, and my chest feels tight. My legs have felt unusually heavy, though I do not recall injuring them. I have also felt mildly feverish but did not check my temperature. EMS was called when breathing became harder this morning, and my adult daughter came with me to the emergency department. I am obese and take medication for high blood pressure. I have noticed occasional burning or sour discomfort after meals in the past, but this episode feels different.

Symptoms: sudden dyspnea; pleuritic chest pain; dry cough; chest tightness; intermittent wheeze; sweating; low-grade feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: 68-year-old woman brought to ED by her adult daughter for sudden SOB beginning last night. Reports sharp chest pain worse with deep inspiration, chest tightness, and persistent dry cough with intermittent wheeze. Felt sweaty overnight and “feverish” but did not check temperature. Denies known sick contacts. PMH includes seasonal allergies, HTN, and obesity. She works at a daycare and was independent before this episode. No home treatment taken other than usual allergy medicine. Speaking in full sentences at triage, anxious and uncomfortable.

Symptoms: sudden shortness of breath; pleuritic chest pain; cough; intermittent wheezing; sweating; lightheadedness
Case_History_Text: I brought my 29-year-old husband to the emergency department after calling EMS because his breathing suddenly became difficult again this morning. He has had episodes on and off since yesterday evening, with a sharp pain that worsens when he takes a deep breath and a dry cough. At times he sounds wheezy, and once he said the discomfort felt like burning after dinner, but he has never had this combination before. During the worst episode he became sweaty, pale, and lightheaded, so I did not want him driving. He works nights as a janitor and has been more tired than usual. He is obese but takes no regular medicines and has no known heart or lung condition. EMS brought us in while he remained awake and able to speak.

Symptoms: sudden shortness of breath; sharp chest pain worse with deep breathing; persistent cough; intermittent wheezing; sweating; leg heaviness; lightheadedness; burning upper-chest discomfort
Case_History_Text: I am a 69-year-old woman and work as a retail manager. My neighbor brought me to the emergency department because I suddenly became short of breath while sitting at home, and it has continued for most of today. I have a sharp pain across the chest that gets worse when I take a deep breath, along with a persistent cough and occasional wheezing. I have felt sweaty and lightheaded, and both legs seem unusually heavy, though I have not noticed a clear injury or one-sided swelling. I also sometimes feel a burning sensation behind my breastbone, especially after eating. I have high blood pressure and recently recovered from a respiratory infection. I am worried because this feels different from my usual symptoms.

Symptoms: sudden dyspnea; pleuritic chest pain; productive cough; wheeze; low-grade feverish feeling; leg heaviness; lightheadedness
Case_History_Text: EMS handoff: This 35-year-old man, a librarian, developed sudden shortness of breath and sharp chest discomfort that worsens with breathing about two hours ago while at home. His spouse called EMS after he became lightheaded and complained that both legs felt heavy. He reports a productive cough, intermittent wheezing, and feeling mildly feverish. He describes no known recent illness but says his blood pressure control has been poor. History includes obesity and a close relative with a prior blood clot. He arrived in the emergency department with his spouse after remaining alert and speaking in full sentences during transport.

Symptoms: sudden dyspnea; pleuritic chest pain; chest tightness; dry cough; intermittent wheeze
Case_History_Text: A 46-year-old woman was brought to the emergency department by her spouse for approximately six hours of sudden shortness of breath and chest discomfort. She reports that the symptoms began while she was finishing paperwork during her shift as a warehouse supervisor, without a clear exertional trigger. The pain is described as a sharp sensation along the right side of the chest that becomes more noticeable with deep inspiration. She also feels a bandlike tightness across the chest and has had a persistent dry cough with occasional wheezing. She denies producing sputum, coughing blood, fainting, or vomiting. She noticed mild fatigue earlier in the day but was otherwise well. Her spouse says she appeared anxious after the breathing difficulty began. The patient has seasonal allergies, which have previously caused intermittent nasal congestion and mild cough, but she says this episode feels more abrupt and intense than usual. She reports no known heart or lung disease and takes no daily prescription medicines.

Symptoms: sudden shortness of breath; sharp chest pain worse with breathing; productive cough; wheezing; lightheadedness
Case_History_Text: I’m 37 and a college student. About three hours ago, while I was studying at home, I suddenly became short of breath and developed a sharp pain on the left side of my chest that gets worse when I take a deep breath. I’ve been coughing up small amounts of clear mucus, and my sister said she could hear me wheezing. I also feel lightheaded when I stand. I sprained my ankle recently, so I’ve barely been walking around, and I took a long bus trip last week. The chest discomfort sometimes has a burning quality, with an unpleasant taste in my mouth after coughing. My neighbor called EMS and came with me to the emergency department.

Symptoms: sudden dyspnea; pleuritic chest pain; chest tightness; productive cough; wheeze; leg heaviness; sweating
Case_History_Text: 46F brought to ED by neighbor for sudden onset SOB beginning ~45 min ago. Reports sharp chest pain worse with deep inspiration, chest tightness, and productive cough with intermittent wheeze. Feels unusually heavy in both legs and became sweaty during the episode. Denies known injury. PMH notable for seasonal allergies and obesity; takes oral contraceptives. Works as a welder. Neighbor states she appeared anxious and paused frequently to catch her breath on the way in. No further history available at triage.

Symptoms: sudden shortness of breath; pleuritic chest pain; cough; intermittent wheezing; leg heaviness; low-grade feverish feeling

He also mentioned a sour taste and burning behind the breastbone after eating dinner, which seemed to worsen when lying down. He has seasonal allergies and sometimes coughs during pollen season, but this breathing trouble is much more abrupt and frightening than usual.

Symptoms: sudden shortness of breath; sharp chest pain worse with deep breathing; dry cough; wheezing; feverish feeling; reduced activity after ankle sprain
Case_History_Text: Hello, I am writing about my coworker, a 70-year-old retired teacher who came with me to the emergency department. She became suddenly short of breath last night and has had a sharp pain in the side of her chest that worsens when she takes a deep breath or coughs. Her cough is dry, and I noticed wheezing when we were speaking this morning. She says she has felt mildly feverish but has not measured her temperature. She recently had a respiratory infection that seemed to be improving. About two weeks ago she sprained her ankle and has been walking much less because of soreness. She has no known injury to her chest and is normally independent.

Symptoms: sudden intermittent dyspnea; pleuritic chest pain; dry cough; occasional wheeze; lightheadedness; sweating; low-grade feverish feeling

Symptoms: sudden shortness of breath; pleuritic chest pain; dry cough; intermittent wheeze; bilateral leg heaviness
Case_History_Text: A 59-year-old woman presents to the emergency department alone with sudden shortness of breath that began earlier today while she was at work as a janitor. She describes sharp left-sided chest discomfort that worsens with deep breathing and coughing, along with a persistent dry cough. She has noticed intermittent wheezing and says the discomfort is sometimes accompanied by a sour sensation rising into her throat, particularly after eating. She denies vomiting or fainting. Since yesterday, both legs have felt unusually heavy, though she has not noticed clear swelling, redness, or focal tenderness. She reports a respiratory infection approximately two weeks ago, with congestion and a lingering cough that had been gradually improving before today’s change. She has no known recent injury and denies coughing up blood. She is visibly concerned because the breathing difficulty came on abruptly and has persisted for most of the day.

Symptoms: sudden shortness of breath; sharp chest pain worse with breathing; cough; wheezing; lightheadedness; feeling feverish
Case_History_Text: I’m 57 and work as a construction foreman. About two hours ago, while I was resting after work, I suddenly felt like I couldn’t get a full breath. I developed a sharp pain on the right side of my chest that gets worse when I take a deep breath, along with a persistent cough. My daughter said she heard me wheezing before EMS arrived. I’ve also felt lightheaded and a little feverish, but I haven’t measured my temperature. A neighbor came with me after calling EMS. My blood pressure has been poorly controlled lately, and I sometimes miss my medication. My older brother had a blood clot years ago. I have not had symptoms like this before, though I occasionally get coughing or burning discomfort after meals.

Symptoms: sudden dyspnea; pleuritic chest pain; cough; productive sputum; intermittent dry cough; wheezing reported by family; bilateral leg heaviness
Case_History_Text: 43-y/o woman, unemployed, presents to ED with adult daughter for ~6 hrs of abrupt SOB and sharp chest discomfort worse with deep inspiration. Hx obesity and HTN with poor medication adherence/control. No prior similar episode reported. Awake, speaking in brief full sentences, appears uncomfortable. No home oxygen use. Arrived ambulatory with daughter; triage assessment initiated.

Symptoms: sudden dyspnea; pleuritic chest pain; dry cough; intermittent wheeze; lightheadedness
Case_History_Text: I am his sister, and I came to the emergency department after my brother called EMS. He arrived alone by ambulance. He returned yesterday from a long flight and spent much of the trip sitting. He has not mentioned fever, vomiting, or injury. He was anxious and speaking in short sentences when I saw him.

Symptoms: sudden shortness of breath; pleuritic chest pain; cough; chest tightness; lightheadedness; wheezing

I am worried because the breathing difficulty came on so abruptly and has not fully eased.

Symptoms: sudden dyspnea; pleuritic chest pain; dry cough; chest tightness; wheezing; lightheadedness

Symptoms: sudden dyspnea; pleuritic chest pain; cough; intermittent wheeze; lightheadedness; bilateral leg heaviness

She denies fever, vomiting, or known recent illness. Her medical history includes poorly controlled blood pressure, and she acknowledges missing some routine doses. She works mainly at a computer and has had little activity during a recent deadline.

Symptoms: sudden shortness of breath; sharp chest pain worse with deep breaths; cough; intermittent wheezing; sweating; feverish feeling; lightheadedness
Case_History_Text: I’m 47 and nonbinary, and I work as a welder. Since yesterday evening, I’ve had episodes that come on suddenly where I feel like I can’t get a full breath. I also get a sharp pain in my chest when I inhale deeply and have been coughing, sometimes with a wheezy sound. The episodes have come and gone, but they feel worse today. I’ve broken out in sweats and felt mildly feverish and lightheaded, though I haven’t checked my temperature. I noticed a sour taste and burning in my throat after dinner, but that doesn’t explain how breathless I feel. EMS was called, and I came here with a coworker. I have high blood pressure and take oral contraceptives; I haven’t had this happen before.

Symptoms: sudden dyspnea; pleuritic chest pain; cough; intermittent wheeze; chest tightness; sweating; bilateral leg heaviness; feverish feeling

Symptoms: sudden shortness of breath; sharp chest pain worse with deep breaths; productive cough; chest tightness; intermittent wheezing

He says the discomfort feels different from ordinary heartburn, though he has had indigestion before. He has seasonal allergies but no other significant medical history that I know of. He appeared frightened and was breathing faster than usual while EMS transported us.

Case_History_Text: Hello, I’m a 43-year-old woman and a construction foreman. I came to the emergency department alone because about six hours ago I suddenly became short of breath. My sister spoke with me by phone and thought she could hear wheezing, although I do not usually notice it myself. I have felt lightheaded when walking and have had to stop to catch my breath. Symptoms: sudden shortness of breath; pleuritic chest pain; dry cough; chest tightness; intermittent wheeze; sweating; low-grade feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: EMS handoff: This is a 60-year-old man, a retail manager, brought from home after three hours of sudden shortness of breath and sharp chest pain that worsens with deep breathing. He mentions intermittent burning in his upper chest after meals but says this episode feels more intense. He arrived alone and denies recent injury. His sister previously had a blood clot. Symptoms: sudden shortness of breath; sharp chest pain worse with deep breathing; dry cough; intermittent wheeze; heaviness in both legs
Case_History_Text: A 65-year-old unemployed woman was brought to the emergency department by a former coworker after developing sudden shortness of breath approximately 45 minutes before arrival. She describes a sharp discomfort across the left side of her chest that becomes more noticeable with deep inspiration and coughing. Since the episode began, she has had a persistent dry cough and reports occasional wheezing, which she says is unusual for her. She also feels that both legs are heavy, without describing a clear injury or focal weakness. She denies fainting, vomiting, or recent fever. She has a history of high blood pressure and reports taking her prescribed medication inconsistently when her routine changes. She has not identified a specific trigger and says the symptoms began while she was sitting at home speaking with her coworker by phone. On arrival, she is anxious but able to answer questions in complete sentences. Her coworker reports no preceding collapse or confusion.

Symptoms: dyspnea; chest tightness; cough; wheeze; bilateral leg heaviness
Case_History_Text: An 81-year-old woman, a retired nurse, presents to the emergency department alone for 45 minutes of shortness of breath, chest tightness, cough, and audible wheezing. She reports that the symptoms began fairly suddenly while she was preparing tea at home and have persisted despite sitting upright. The cough is mild and nonproductive. A family member speaking with her by phone noticed wheezing during the call and encouraged her to seek care. She also describes both legs as feeling unusually heavy, without a clear injury or focal pain. She denies fever, chills, fainting, or recent vomiting. Her history includes chronic obstructive lung disease and high blood pressure; she states that her breathing is usually manageable with her routine medications. She has not identified a specific trigger and does not recall choking or a new exposure. She is able to speak in full sentences but appears concerned by the persistent tightness and breathlessness.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease

Symptoms: dyspnea; chest tightness; dry cough; wheeze; leg heaviness
Case_History_Text: I’m 79 and a retired teacher. I came to the emergency department after EMS was called because my breathing became noticeably harder over the past day. I feel tight across my chest and have had a dry cough with wheezing. My legs feel unusually heavy, though I have not noticed a specific injury. I have smoked for many years and have a history of breathing problems that sometimes flare up, but this episode feels concerning to me. Last week I took a long bus trip to visit family and spent many hours sitting. I arrived alone; my neighbor stayed with me until the ambulance came. I have not had this much trouble catching my breath since yesterday, and it has persisted even while resting.

Symptoms: dyspnea; chest tightness; productive cough; wheezing; low-grade feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: 78-year-old woman, retired accountant, presents to ED with adult daughter for dyspnea since last night. Reports chest tightness, productive cough, and feeling feverish without measured temperature. Daughter heard wheezing at home. Long history of cigarette use and longstanding smoking-related lung disease managed with inhalers. Recently returned from prolonged air travel. A close relative previously had a blood clot. No additional details available at triage. Patient is speaking in full sentences and appears uncomfortable with breathing but remains able to walk with assistance.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease

He has been short of breath on and off since yesterday evening, with a tight feeling across his chest and wheezing that seems worse when he walks. He has smoked for many years and has a history of chronic breathing problems, but this episode seems more noticeable than usual. He works as a postal worker and was still trying to finish his usual errands yesterday. He denies fainting, and I have not noticed confusion.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)

I work as a construction foreman and was able to start my day, but climbing stairs and walking across the site became increasingly difficult. I have a long history of smoking and a chronic breathing problem that sometimes flares, along with seasonal allergies. I have not noticed anything else unusual and did not want to drive myself.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)

Symptoms: dyspnea; chest tightness; cough; wheeze; leg heaviness
Case_History_Text: A 71-year-old woman was brought to the emergency department by her adult daughter for approximately six hours of worsening shortness of breath. She has had an intermittent cough with scant clear sputum and reports that her daughter noticed audible wheezing while they were at home. She denies known fever, chills, fainting, or recent chest injury. The patient also mentions a heavy, tired feeling in both legs that began earlier today, without describing a specific injury. Her medical history includes chronic obstructive lung disease and high blood pressure. She is a retired mechanic who lives independently and usually manages household activities without assistance. She has not identified a clear trigger for the current symptoms and says they came on gradually after an otherwise routine morning. Her daughter reports no recent confusion or change in speech.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease

The tightness and breathlessness continued, so my family called EMS. I came to the emergency department alone and am speaking for myself in triage.

Coworker reports audible wheezing; patient has frequent dry coughing with occasional scant sputum and feels sweaty. Awake, speaking in short phrases, and visibly uncomfortable. No additional history available at triage.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)

Symptoms: Shortness of breath; chest tightness; cough with sputum; wheezing; sweating

He has been increasingly short of breath since yesterday, with a tight feeling across his chest and wheezing that is louder than usual. His cough has become productive, though he has not noticed blood. He was sweating while sitting in his recliner and said he felt unusually tired. At home, he tried several treatments with his nebulizer, which seemed to help only briefly. He has a history of breathing problems and usually manages them at home. He is a retired postal worker and normally walks around the house without much trouble. He has not complained of fainting or severe chest pain, and EMS brought us in for further evaluation.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)

I can hear myself wheezing more than usual, and I’ve had spells of sweating when the breathing gets worse. Both legs feel unusually heavy, though I don’t recall an injury. I have a chronic lung condition and use nebulizer treatments at home, especially when seasonal allergies flare up. My spouse became concerned this morning and called EMS, who brought me to the emergency department. I’m not sure what triggered this episode. I can speak in full sentences, but walking from room to room has made the breathlessness and chest tightness return.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease

History includes chronic breathing problems managed with inhalers, obesity, seasonal allergies, and a respiratory infection several weeks ago. Denies known injury. Speaking in short but complete phrases, appears anxious, and reports no clear trigger. Neighbor says symptoms worsened after lunch and brought her in when breathing became more uncomfortable.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)

Symptoms: dyspnea; chest tightness; cough; wheeze; feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: My father is 59 and works as a construction foreman. About two hours ago, while resting at home after work, he suddenly became noticeably short of breath and complained that his chest felt tight. I could hear him wheezing when he spoke, and his cough became more frequent. He said he felt slightly feverish but denied shaking chills. He has had chronic breathing problems for years and uses inhalers, though he does not always use them as prescribed. His blood pressure has also been poorly controlled. He had not mentioned any recent illness or injury before this started. When his breathing did not improve after sitting upright, I called EMS and rode with him to the emergency department.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)

Symptoms: dyspnea; chest tightness; dry cough; wheeze; leg heaviness; low-grade feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: I am a 67-year-old woman who came to the emergency department with my daughter because I have been increasingly short of breath for about six hours. My chest feels tight, and I have a dry cough with wheezing that has not eased after using my home nebulizer treatments. I also feel mildly feverish and have noticed heaviness in both legs, though I do not recall injuring them. I work as an office administrator and have been sitting more than usual during a busy week. My blood pressure has not been well controlled recently. I have a history of chronic breathing problems and usually manage them at home, but this episode feels more persistent than usual.

Symptoms: dyspnea; chest tightness; cough; wheeze; leg heaviness; sweating; low-grade feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: EMS handoff: This is a 70-year-old man, a city bus driver, brought in with a coworker after we were called for worsening breathing over the last three hours. On arrival he is awake, answering appropriately, and able to speak with mild pauses between phrases.

Symptoms: dyspnea; chest tightness; cough; wheeze
Case_History_Text: A 54-year-old woman was brought to the emergency department by her adult daughter after developing increasing shortness of breath approximately 45 minutes before arrival. She describes a sensation of tightness across the chest and difficulty getting a satisfying breath, accompanied by a mostly dry cough. Her daughter noticed audible wheezing while they were walking from the parking area. The patient works as a security guard and says the symptoms began during a routine shift without a clearly identified trigger. She denies choking, recent illness, or known injury. She has experienced similar breathing difficulty in the past and has prescribed inhalers, though she acknowledges inconsistent use. Her medical history also includes poorly controlled blood pressure. She reports no recent medication changes. She is able to speak in full sentences but appears uncomfortable and pauses occasionally to catch her breath. Her daughter remains at the bedside and provides additional history.

Symptoms: acute dyspnea; audible wheeze; nocturnal cough; dry cough; intermittent productive cough; chest tightness; poorly controlled blood pressure
Case_History_Text: A 59-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with a coworker for 45 minutes of worsening shortness of breath and audible wheezing. She reports that her breathing became noticeably difficult while walking across campus after an evening class, with a sensation of chest tightness but no focal chest pain. For several nights, she has been waking with bouts of coughing and breathlessness. The cough is usually dry, although she occasionally brings up a small amount of clear sputum. Her coworker says she appeared more winded than usual and needed to pause while speaking. She denies fever, chills, recent travel, or known sick contacts. She has a history of poorly controlled blood pressure and acknowledges missing some doses of her medication during a busy week. She is currently enrolled as a college student and has no documented prior episodes requiring emergency care. She is able to speak in short sentences on arrival and appears anxious about the sudden worsening of her breathing.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute decompensated heart failure with pulmonary edema (cardiac asthma)

Symptoms: Shortness of breath for one day; wheezing; chest tightness; cough worse at night; feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: I am 43 and work as a home health aide. Since yesterday, I have been getting increasingly short of breath, especially when walking across a room or lying down to sleep. My adult daughter noticed a wheezing sound and called EMS when I seemed to be working harder to breathe. I have had a tight feeling across my chest but no sharp pain. Last night I kept waking up coughing and had to sit up for a while before settling down. I feel slightly feverish, though I have not checked my temperature. I had wheezing episodes as a child, but they became rare as I grew older. My blood pressure has been poorly controlled lately, and I sometimes miss my medication when work is busy.

Symptoms: Dyspnea since last night; wheezing; nocturnal cough; dry cough; leg heaviness; sweating
Case_History_Text: 47-year-old woman, unemployed, brought to ED by adult daughter for worsening SOB since last night. Daughter reports audible wheezing, especially when pt lies down, with repeated episodes of dry cough overnight and poor sleep. Pt describes chest tightness, leg heaviness, and sweating but denies fever, sputum, or known recent exposure. Had a respiratory infection several weeks ago and reports wheezing during childhood. PMH notable for poorly controlled blood pressure; medication adherence unclear. Speaking in short phrases but alert and cooperative. No similar severe episode reported recently.

Symptoms: Shortness of breath; wheezing; nocturnal cough; productive cough; sweating; intermittent chest tightness
Case_History_Text: I brought my husband to the emergency department after calling EMS because his breathing became harder again this morning. He is 23 and works as a restaurant cook. This morning he was sweaty, seemed anxious, and said he could not get a satisfying breath. His cough has brought up a small amount of clear mucus. He has seasonal allergies but no other major medical problems that I know of. He has not mentioned fainting or severe chest pain. EMS helped him sit upright during the ride, and he remained awake and able to answer questions.

Symptoms: Shortness of breath; wheezing; nocturnal cough; chest tightness; sweating; low-grade feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: I’m a 28-year-old woman and came to the emergency department with my neighbor because I’ve been struggling to breathe for most of today. Today I became sweaty and felt slightly feverish, though I have not checked my temperature. I have seasonal allergies and a history of high blood pressure. I work as a graphic designer and have not had this much trouble breathing before. The symptoms seem worse when I lie down, so I have been sitting upright and trying to stay calm.

Symptoms: dyspnea; wheeze; nocturnal cough; chest tightness; dry cough; lightheadedness; leg heaviness

On arrival, she is anxious about the breathing difficulty but remains able to answer questions in complete sentences. Her spouse provides additional history and says the nighttime cough has become more frequent over the past week.

Symptoms: shortness of breath; wheezing; nocturnal cough; productive cough; low-grade feverish feeling; lightheadedness
Case_History_Text: I’m a 63-year-old high school coach, and for the past three hours I’ve been getting increasingly short of breath and wheezy. She recently returned from a long-distance bus trip lasting approximately nine hours, during which she had limited opportunities to get up and move around. She denies recent sick contacts and has not taken any new medications. No additional acute complaints are reported.

Symptoms: Cough with sputum; shortness of breath; wheezing; chest tightness; lightheadedness; recent respiratory infection

I also get seasonal allergies, especially this time of year, but this feels more intense than my usual congestion. I’m not sure if I’ve had a fever, but I’ve felt warm and tired since last night.
