Symptoms: cough; productive sputum; dyspnea; wheeze; sweating; lightheadedness; recent cold symptoms
Case_History_Text: EMS brought a 32-year-old man from home after his spouse called for increasing shortness of breath. He reports symptoms occurring on and off since yesterday evening, beginning with a dry cough that became productive of yellowish sputum. He noticed audible wheezing, sweating, and intermittent lightheadedness but denies fainting. He has had a lingering cold for about a week. He has smoked for several years and works as a pharmacist. His spouse reports no unusual confusion. He mentions that a relative previously had a blood clot. On arrival, he is alert and speaking in full sentences.

Symptoms: cough; sputum production; shortness of breath; wheezing; low-grade feverish feeling; lingering cold
Case_History_Text: A 29-year-old woman presents to the emergency department alone for worsening breathing symptoms that began earlier today. She reports a lingering cold for approximately one week, with nasal congestion and an intermittent cough that became more frequent this morning. The cough is now bringing up small amounts of thick, pale sputum. She feels mildly feverish and fatigued but has not measured her temperature at home. She describes shortness of breath with walking between rooms and while doing light chores, without sudden onset or a clearly positional pattern. A family member noticed a high-pitched wheeze when she was breathing this afternoon, prompting her visit. She denies coughing blood, fainting, chest injury, or leg swelling. She has continued drinking fluids and has not had vomiting or diarrhea. She works as a farmer and reports recent exposure to dust while tending a shed, though she cannot identify a specific new chemical or animal exposure. She arrived without assistance and has no known history of chronic lung disease.

Symptoms: cough; sputum; shortness of breath; wheezing; sweating; lightheadedness; leg heaviness
Case_History_Text: I’m 42 and coach at a high school. I’ve had a cough with yellowish sputum for a few days, but over the last two hours my breathing became noticeably harder and I started wheezing. I feel sweaty and a little lightheaded, especially when I stand or walk. Both legs feel unusually heavy, though they are not painful. A coworker called EMS and came with me to the emergency department. I have not noticed anything else unusual, and I can still speak in full sentences, although I need to pause more than usual. I’m obese and get seasonal allergies, but I do not normally have breathing trouble like this. I’m unsure whether I’ve had a fever.

Symptoms: cough; scant sputum; shortness of breath; wheezing; chest tightness; leg heaviness; recent respiratory infection
Case_History_Text: 27-y/o woman, security guard, arrives to ED with coworker for ~6 hrs of worsening SOB and chest tightness. Reports a mostly dry cough with small amounts of sputum and intermittent wheeze, which her sister noticed by phone during a recent call. Feels both legs are heavy but denies focal pain or swelling. Had a respiratory infection last week with lingering congestion. Hx seasonal allergies. States a relative previously had a blood clot. No known chronic lung disease reported. Speaking in full sentences at triage; appears uncomfortable but alert and ambulatory.

Symptoms: Cough; scant sputum; shortness of breath; wheezing; low-grade feverish feeling; several years of smoking
Case_History_Text: I am his sister, and I met him at the emergency department after his coworker called EMS from the garage. He had been working normally earlier today, but over the last three hours his cough became more frequent and he said it felt harder to catch his breath. He describes the cough as mostly dry, though he has brought up a small amount of thin yellowish sputum. His coworker noticed a whistling sound when he breathed. He says he feels feverish but has not checked his temperature. He denies choking or any known recent injury. He has smoked for years and gets occasional morning cough, but this episode is much more sudden and uncomfortable than usual. He is awake, worried, and speaking with brief pauses.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)

Symptoms: cough; scant sputum; shortness of breath; wheezing; low-grade feverish feeling; sweating
Case_History_Text: Hello, I’m a 21-year-old woman who came to the emergency department with my neighbor because my breathing became noticeably harder about 45 minutes ago. I have had a mostly dry cough with a small amount of clear sputum, wheezing, and a tight feeling in my chest. I feel mildly feverish and sweaty but have not measured my temperature. I work at a daycare and have been around several children with recent colds. I am obese and have smoked for several years. I do not usually need help with breathing, and I have not noticed anything else unusual. The wheezing and breathlessness are making it difficult to talk comfortably, so I wanted to be checked.

Symptoms: cough; productive sputum; dyspnea; wheeze; chest tightness; possible fever; leg heaviness
Case_History_Text: EMS handoff: This is a 53-year-old man, a software engineer, brought in with his neighbor after EMS was called for worsening breathing over the past day. He reports the cough started dry and became productive with small amounts of sputum, along with wheezing, chest tightness, and a feeling of heaviness in both legs. He felt feverish at home but did not measure his temperature. He recently returned from long-distance travel and has a history of high blood pressure. He mentions a relative with a prior blood clot. On arrival he is alert, speaking in full sentences, and mildly uncomfortable.

Symptoms: cough; sputum production; shortness of breath; wheezing; low-grade feverish feeling; leg heaviness
Case_History_Text: A 40-year-old woman who works as a farmer presents to the emergency department with her adult daughter for evaluation of respiratory symptoms that began last night. She reports a frequent cough producing small amounts of thick, pale sputum, accompanied by a sensation of chest tightness, audible wheezing, and shortness of breath that is more noticeable when walking across the room. She has felt mildly feverish but has not recorded a temperature at home. She also describes both legs as feeling unusually heavy since returning from a recent long trip, without reporting focal injury. She denies vomiting, fainting, or a known exposure to anyone with a similar illness. She has continued drinking fluids but slept poorly because of coughing. Her daughter notes that the patient appeared more tired than usual this morning. No similar episode is reported recently, and the patient is seeking assessment because the breathing discomfort has persisted.

Symptoms: Cough; sputum; shortness of breath; wheezing; intermittent feverish feeling; leg heaviness; lightheadedness
Case_History_Text: I’m 33 and work as a home health aide. Since yesterday evening, I’ve had coughing spells that come and go, bringing up thick sputum. I feel short of breath when I walk across a room, and my family member noticed a whistling sound when I was breathing last night. I’ve felt warm and had some chills, though I didn’t check my temperature. Both legs feel unusually heavy, and I’ve been lightheaded at times without passing out. EMS was called after I became winded while getting ready for work, and I came to the emergency department with a coworker. I have seasonal allergies but no known lung disease. One of my relatives had a blood clot before. I don’t smoke.

Symptoms: productive cough; shortness of breath; wheezing; lightheadedness; sweating
Case_History_Text: 53-y/o woman, software engineer, arrived alone to ED after symptoms worsened over most of today. Reports productive cough with increasing dyspnea and intermittent wheeze; her sister noticed noisy breathing at home. Feels lightheaded and has had episodes of sweating, with possible subjective fever but no measured temperature. Denies fainting or chest injury. Recently returned from a long trip. She is obese and reports a relative with a prior blood clot. No known chronic lung disease reported. Speaking in full sentences at triage; breathing appears mildly labored. Further evaluation pending.

Symptoms: productive cough; sputum; shortness of breath; wheezing; lightheadedness; feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: I’m his older sister, and I came to the emergency department after his neighbor called EMS. He is 21 and manages a retail store. He said he had been coughing on and off, but over about two hours it became much harder for him to catch his breath. The cough is bringing up thick sputum, and I could hear a whistling sound when he breathed. He also complained of feeling lightheaded when he stood up and said he felt feverish, though we did not check his temperature at home. He has seasonal allergies but no other major medical problems that I know of. His neighbor stayed with him and rode along because I was at work when the symptoms suddenly worsened.

Symptoms: cough; sputum production; shortness of breath; wheezing; low-grade feverish feeling; lightheadedness
Case_History_Text: I am 55 and came to the emergency department with my spouse after about six hours of worsening breathing symptoms. I drive for a rideshare service and started coughing during an afternoon shift, bringing up small amounts of yellowish sputum. Since then I have felt feverish, mildly lightheaded, and short of breath, especially when walking from room to room. My spouse noticed a whistling sound when I breathed. I have not fainted or had chest pain. My blood pressure has been poorly controlled because I sometimes miss doses, though I do not know today’s reading. A relative had a blood clot in the past. I do not use tobacco, and this feels more intense than my usual seasonal cough.

Symptoms: cough; scant sputum; shortness of breath; wheezing; low-grade feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: EMS reports a 62-year-old man brought to the emergency department after his spouse called for help. He is a mechanic with a history of high blood pressure and obesity and had a respiratory infection about a week ago. Over the last three hours, his cough became more frequent, initially dry and now producing small amounts of sputum. He describes feeling feverish and increasingly short of breath, while his spouse noticed audible wheezing. He remained able to speak in full sentences during transport and was breathing room air on arrival. No chest injury or choking event was reported.

Symptoms: cough; scant sputum; dyspnea; wheeze; sweating; chest tightness
Case_History_Text: A 67-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by her adult daughter for worsening breathing that began about 45 minutes before arrival. She reports a dry cough earlier in the day that has become intermittently productive of scant clear-to-yellow sputum. During the episode, she noticed audible wheezing, chest tightness, and shortness of breath with minimal activity. She became sweaty while sitting in her parked car and felt too uncomfortable to continue driving for her rideshare shift. She denies choking, recent travel, or known exposure to fumes. She has not measured a temperature and is unsure whether she has had chills. Her daughter says the patient appeared tired but remained alert and able to speak in full sentences. The patient has a history of obesity and no reported chronic lung condition. She has used no inhaler or other breathing treatment today and reports no similar emergency visit recently.

Symptoms: productive cough; sputum production; shortness of breath; wheezing
Case_History_Text: A 70-year-old woman was brought to the emergency department by her adult daughter for 45 minutes of worsening shortness of breath. She is a retired nurse and reports several days of cough with increased sputum, described as thicker than usual but without a clear change in color. Her daughter noticed prominent wheezing while the patient was resting at home. The patient has a home nebulizer and used it once before arrival with only partial, temporary relief. She is able to speak in short sentences and feels more breathless with walking. She reports feeling warm earlier but did not check her temperature and denies shaking chills. She has not identified a specific sick contact. She denies sharp, localized chest pain, fainting, vomiting, or leg swelling. Her daughter says the cough has sounded “deeper” today, although neither can identify a consistently localized area of discomfort. The patient is concerned because this episode feels more severe than her usual breathing flares.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)

Symptoms: cough; scant sputum; shortness of breath; wheezing; chest tightness; lightheadedness
Case_History_Text: I’m 84 and a retired nurse. Since yesterday I’ve been more short of breath than usual, with a mostly dry cough that has brought up a little clear sputum and some wheezing. My chest feels tight, especially when I walk across the room, and I’ve felt lightheaded but haven’t passed out. I had a respiratory infection recently and never felt completely back to normal. I’m not sure whether I’ve had a fever; I felt warm overnight but did not check it. My blood pressure has been poorly controlled lately. My daughter became concerned when I was breathing harder this morning and called EMS, who brought me to the emergency department. I can speak in full sentences, though it takes more effort than usual.

Symptoms: Cough; occasional scant sputum; dyspnea; wheeze; chest tightness; leg heaviness
Case_History_Text: 71-y/o woman, retail manager, arrived alone to ED for SOB since last night. Reports mostly dry cough with occasional scant sputum, chest tightness, wheezing, and a heavy feeling in both legs. States she felt warm overnight but did not check her temperature; denies chills. Hx years of smoking, obesity, and HTN. No known recent sick contacts reported. At triage, breathing appears mildly labored while speaking in full sentences. Brief lung exam notes scattered wheeze with generally diminished sounds and no definite focal finding. Symptoms began after an otherwise routine workday.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease

Symptoms: Productive cough; shortness of breath; wheezing; intermittent chest tightness; leg heaviness
Case_History_Text: I brought my 81-year-old father to the emergency department after EMS was called this morning. He has been having episodes of shortness of breath since yesterday evening, along with a cough bringing up small amounts of yellowish sputum and noticeable wheezing. He says his legs feel heavy, especially when he walks, but he denies a sharp or severe chest pain. He recently returned from a long trip and has seemed more tired than usual since then. He felt warm overnight, though I did not measure a clear fever, and he has not had shaking chills. A former coworker who was visiting helped him get ready and came with us. He is a retired nurse and initially thought the breathing trouble would pass, but it became more persistent this morning.

Symptoms: Cough; productive sputum; shortness of breath; wheezing; low-grade feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: I’m a 51-year-old high school coach writing from the ED with my spouse. Since this morning, I’ve become increasingly short of breath and have had wheezing that is worse when I walk or talk. I started with a mostly dry cough, but I’m now bringing up small amounts of thick, pale-yellow sputum. I feel mildly feverish and chilled, though I have not measured a high temperature. My chest feels tight and irritated rather than sharply painful. I have seasonal allergies and use a home nebulizer occasionally when breathing gets difficult. I have not noticed a clear side of my chest hurting, and my spouse says my breathing sounds noisy. This is more intense than my usual symptoms.

Symptoms: cough; sputum production; dyspnea; wheeze; chest tightness; leg heaviness; lightheadedness; low-grade feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: EMS handoff: This 60-year-old man, a college student, was brought to the emergency department after his coworker called EMS for roughly two hours of worsening shortness of breath. He reports cough with sputum, audible wheezing, chest tightness, and a heavy feeling in both legs. He also felt lightheaded and intermittently feverish but did not measure a temperature. He has seasonal allergies, high blood pressure, and a home nebulizer; he used it before we arrived with uncertain benefit. Breath sounds were generally noisy with scattered wheeze and no clearly localized abnormality. His coworker accompanied him to the department.

Symptoms: cough; sputum production; shortness of breath; wheezing; leg heaviness; sweating
Case_History_Text: A 71-year-old woman was brought to the emergency department by her spouse for approximately six hours of worsening shortness of breath. She reports a cough producing small amounts of yellow-gray sputum and describes audible wheezing that became more noticeable while doing household chores. She has felt intermittently warm but has not measured her temperature and denies shaking chills. She also mentions a heavy sensation in both legs and several episodes of sweating during the afternoon. She had a respiratory infection about two weeks ago, with partial improvement before these symptoms began. She denies chest pain, fainting, or recent travel. Her spouse says she seemed more tired than usual but remained able to speak in full sentences. On initial assessment, her breathing is mildly labored, with wheezing and generally coarse breath sounds heard on both sides; no clearly localized abnormality is appreciated. She works as a janitor and had planned to finish her shift before coming in.

Symptoms: Cough; scant sputum; shortness of breath; wheezing; lightheadedness; sweating
Case_History_Text: I’m 58 and work on a farm. About three hours ago, while doing chores, I suddenly felt more short of breath than usual and started wheezing. I had been fighting a respiratory infection recently, with a mostly dry cough, but today I’m bringing up a small amount of clear to pale sputum. I feel lightheaded and sweaty, though I haven’t checked my temperature and don’t know if I’ve had a fever. My chest feels tight when I breathe, but I wouldn’t call it sharp pain. My adult daughter called EMS and came with me. My blood pressure has been poorly controlled lately, and I sometimes miss doses. I’m not sure whether the breathing sounds are worse on one side.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute cardiogenic pulmonary edema (acute decompensated heart failure)

Symptoms: productive cough; sputum; dyspnea; wheeze; chest tightness; lightheadedness; leg heaviness
Case_History_Text: 81-year-old woman, retired pharmacist, brought to ED by spouse for 45 min of worsening SOB with chest tightness and audible wheeze. Reports several days of cough producing small amounts of pale sputum, now harder to clear. Feels lightheaded and notes both legs feel heavy, without reported unilateral swelling or pain. Seasonal allergies and uses a home nebulizer intermittently. No known measured fever; spouse says she felt warm earlier. Triage exam: mildly tachypneic, scattered wheeze with generally coarse breath sounds, no definite focal finding appreciated. Family history notable for a prior blood clot in a relative.

Symptoms: Cough; sputum production; shortness of breath; wheezing; lightheadedness
Case_History_Text: I am his sister, and I came to the emergency department after his coworker called EMS from the warehouse. He is 54 and supervises shipping there. Over the past day, he has developed a frequent cough bringing up thicker-than-usual sputum and increasing trouble catching his breath. His coworker said he heard him wheezing while they were walking between storage areas. He also felt lightheaded when standing, though he did not faint. He has smoked for many years and occasionally gets winded, but this episode seemed more sudden and limiting than usual. He denies chest pain. He felt warm to me earlier, but he was unsure whether he had a fever and has had no clear shaking chills. He has not reported vomiting or recent travel.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)

Symptoms: Cough; productive sputum; shortness of breath; wheezing; low-grade feverish feeling; heavy legs
Case_History_Text: I am a 74-year-old retired postal worker, brought to the emergency department by my daughter because my breathing became noticeably harder overnight. I have had a productive cough with pale yellow sputum and a wheezing, tight feeling in my chest since last night. I feel mildly feverish, although I have not measured a high temperature. My legs feel unusually heavy, but I have not noticed one-sided swelling or sharp chest pain. I had a respiratory infection a few weeks ago and seemed mostly recovered before this started. I have high blood pressure and take my usual prescribed medicine. I am able to speak in full sentences but become short of breath walking from the waiting area.

Symptoms: productive cough; sputum; intermittent dyspnea; wheezing; lightheadedness; leg heaviness
Case_History_Text: EMS handoff: We were called to the home for an 84-year-old man brought in with his adult daughter. He reports episodes of shortness of breath beginning yesterday evening, along with a productive cough and increased sputum. His daughter noticed wheezing while he was resting. He also describes feeling lightheaded and says both legs feel heavy. He recently recovered from a respiratory infection, typically needs steroid bursts about twice a year, and returned from a long trip several weeks ago. He denies knowing of a measured fever; the daughter says he seemed warm overnight. Lung sounds were variably noisy and somewhat difficult to localize in the field.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)

Symptoms: cough; sputum production; dyspnea; wheeze; sweating; lightheadedness
Case_History_Text: A 70-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with her adult daughter for shortness of breath that began earlier today and has gradually worsened. She reports a frequent cough producing small amounts of thick, pale-yellow sputum, along with audible wheezing and a feeling that she cannot take a full breath. She has been sweating intermittently and felt lightheaded when walking from room to room, but has not fainted. She is unsure whether she had a fever, saying that she felt warm briefly but did not check her temperature. She denies sharp chest pain, though describes mild chest tightness during coughing. Her daughter noticed that she seemed more tired than usual this afternoon. The patient is a retired postal worker and lives independently. She has seasonal allergies that often cause nasal congestion and intermittent cough. She reports no recent travel and no clearly known sick contact. She came in because the breathing difficulty persisted despite resting and drinking fluids.

Symptoms: Cough; sputum production; shortness of breath; wheezing; lightheadedness; feeling feverish; sweating
Case_History_Text: I’m a 67-year-old man and work as a nurse. I had a respiratory infection recently, and although I was starting to feel better, my breathing became noticeably harder over the last two hours. I’ve been coughing up more sputum than usual and hearing a wheeze when I breathe. I feel mildly feverish and sweaty, and I got lightheaded walking across the room. My adult daughter called EMS and came with me to the emergency department. I’m obese but usually manage my daily activities without help. I can’t tell whether the cough feels deeper than before, and I haven’t noticed one specific painful spot when I breathe. I’m worried because the breathlessness came on quickly and feels worse than it did earlier today.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)

Symptoms: cough; scant sputum; dyspnea; wheeze; low-grade feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: 59F bus driver, arrived to ED with neighbor for ~6 hrs worsening SOB. Cough began dry, now bringing up small amounts of sputum. Reports feeling mildly feverish but denies measured temperature. Neighbor heard wheezing at home. No clear focal chest discomfort reported; triage exam notes diffuse noisy breathing without a definite localized finding. PMH includes poorly controlled HTN and recurrent episodes treated with steroid bursts about twice yearly. States a relative had a prior blood clot. No medication list available at triage. Speaking in short phrases but cooperative; symptoms started while resting after work.

Symptoms: cough; scant sputum; shortness of breath; wheezing; sweating
Case_History_Text: I brought my 69-year-old father to the emergency department after calling EMS this evening. He had been sitting in his apartment watching television when, over about three hours, his breathing became noticeably harder and he started sweating. He has had a mostly dry cough, though he brought up a small amount of pale sputum once or twice. I could hear him wheezing when he spoke and walked from the bedroom. He has not checked his temperature; he felt warm to me, but he denied chills and said he was unsure whether he had a fever. He has needed steroid bursts about twice a year for similar breathing trouble. He is unemployed and lives alone. He denies chest pain, vomiting, or leg swelling.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)

Symptoms: cough; sputum production; shortness of breath; wheezing; sweating; low-grade feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: Hello, I’m writing about my mother, a 75-year-old retired mechanic, who arrived in the emergency department with me tonight. For about 45 minutes she has felt increasingly short of breath, sweaty, and unable to get a comfortable breath. She has been coughing up a small amount of thicker-than-usual sputum and says she feels slightly feverish, though we have not checked a temperature at home. I could hear wheezing when she spoke and walked from the car. She has smoked for many years, although she has cut down recently. Her symptoms seem worse with activity, and she is tired but answering questions normally. A close relative once had a blood clot. She has not reported sharp chest pain or fainting.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease

Symptoms: cough; productive sputum; dyspnea; wheeze; lightheadedness; low-grade feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: EMS handoff: This is a 78-year-old man, a retired accountant, brought from home with his spouse after one day of worsening shortness of breath, productive cough, and wheezing noticed by family. He reports feeling mildly feverish and intermittently lightheaded but denies fainting. On assessment, he is speaking in short phrases, with audible wheeze and generally coarse breath sounds without a clearly localized abnormality. His spouse says they recently returned from a long trip. History includes high blood pressure; a relative previously had a blood clot. No other acute concerns were reported before transport.

Symptoms: Cough; scant sputum; dyspnea; wheeze; low-grade feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: A 67-year-old woman presents to the emergency department alone for worsening breathing difficulty that began last night. She works as a home health aide and reports that the symptoms started with an irritating, mostly dry cough, followed by a small amount of clear-to-yellow sputum this morning. She feels mildly feverish but has not measured her temperature and denies shaking chills. She describes a sense of chest tightness and audible wheezing, with shortness of breath more noticeable when walking from room to room. She has not identified a definite sick contact, although several of her clients have had recent respiratory symptoms. She denies choking, leg swelling, fainting, or sustained chest pain. Her history includes poorly controlled blood pressure, and she admits she has missed several doses of her medication this week because of a changing work schedule. She has tried warm tea at home without meaningful relief. On arrival, she appears tired but is able to speak in complete sentences; breath sounds are generally reduced with scattered coarse sounds and intermittent wheeze, without a clearly localized abnormality.

Symptoms: cough; sputum production; shortness of breath; wheezing; feverish feeling; lightheadedness
Case_History_Text: I’m an 80-year-old nonbinary nurse, and my spouse brought me in after EMS was called because my breathing seemed worse. Since yesterday evening, I’ve had episodes of shortness of breath that come and go, along with a cough bringing up more sputum than usual. My spouse noticed wheezing when I was resting. I’ve felt mildly feverish but have not checked my temperature, and I’ve been lightheaded when standing. I recently returned from a long trip, with several hours of sitting during travel. I smoked for many years but stopped a while ago. I don’t have sharp chest pain. I’m tired and breathing feels tight, though the discomfort is not clearly in one spot. I’m worried because this feels different from an ordinary cough.

Symptoms: productive cough; sputum; dyspnea; wheeze; chest tightness; sweating; lightheadedness
Case_History_Text: 79-y/o woman, retired accountant, arrives to ED with neighbor for worsening SOB most of today. Reports frequent cough now productive of yellowish sputum, audible wheeze, chest tightness, sweating, and intermittent lightheadedness. Says she may have felt warm but did not check temperature. No clear focal chest discomfort reported. History of similar breathing flares treated with steroid bursts about twice yearly; also obese. Neighbor notes she seemed more tired this afternoon. Family history includes a relative with a prior blood clot. Speaking in short phrases but remains cooperative; breath sounds described as diffusely noisy without a definite focal finding.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)

Symptoms: cough; productive sputum; dyspnea; wheeze; feeling feverish; chest congestion
Case_History_Text: I brought my 61-year-old husband to the emergency department after calling EMS because his breathing became noticeably harder over about two hours. He has been coughing up yellowish sputum and says his chest feels congested, with a whistling sound when he breathes. He has felt mildly feverish, though we did not check his temperature at home. He is a construction foreman and has continued working despite feeling run-down since returning from a long trip several days ago. He has not mentioned sharp chest pain, fainting, or vomiting. The breathing trouble worsened while he was resting at home, and I became worried when he had to pause between sentences. EMS brought us in, and he is sitting upright and using extra pillows to breathe more comfortably.

Symptoms: Cough with sputum; shortness of breath; wheezing; chest tightness; sweating
Case_History_Text: I am a 67-year-old woman and came to the emergency department by myself. About six hours ago, I began feeling unusually short of breath, with a tight feeling across my chest and a cough bringing up small amounts of yellow-gray sputum. My daughter spoke with me by phone and said she could hear me wheezing. I have also been sweating, though I have not checked my temperature and do not clearly feel feverish. I work as a welder and sometimes get winded after a long shift, but this feels worse than usual. I recently spent many hours traveling by bus. A close relative once had a blood clot. I have not fainted or noticed sharp pain with breathing.

Symptoms: cough; sputum production; shortness of breath; wheezing; chest tightness; feverish feeling; sweating; lightheadedness
Case_History_Text: EMS handoff: This is a 63-year-old man, a software engineer, brought from home with his neighbor after EMS was called for three hours of worsening shortness of breath. He reports increased coughing with sputum, chest tightness, and audible wheezing. He feels mildly feverish, has been sweating, and became lightheaded while walking to the door, but denies passing out. He has seasonal allergies, poorly controlled blood pressure, and says he needs steroid bursts about twice a year for similar breathing problems. On scene he was speaking in short phrases and coughing frequently; wheezing was heard throughout, with the lower lung sounds difficult to assess during coughing.

Symptoms: Cough; sputum production; dyspnea; wheeze; sweating; subjective low-grade feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: A 70-year-old woman was brought to the emergency department by her spouse for worsening shortness of breath that became markedly more noticeable over the past 45 minutes. She reports several days of cough with increased sputum production and describes the sputum as thicker than usual, without noting a clear change in color. She has heard herself wheezing and feels unable to take a satisfying breath. While getting ready to leave home, she became sweaty and said she felt mildly feverish, though no temperature was measured. Her spouse reports that she appeared more tired than usual but remained conversational. She denies syncope and has not described definite chest pain. She is a retired mechanic with a remote history of workplace exposure to dust and fumes. Her blood pressure has been poorly controlled, and she acknowledges inconsistent use of her prescribed medication. On arrival, she is anxious but cooperative, with frequent coughing and diffuse-sounding wheeze; breath sounds are somewhat variable without a clearly localized abnormality.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease

Symptoms: dyspnea for 45 minutes; tachypnea; dry cough; crackles; low-grade feverish feeling; recent respiratory infection
Case_History_Text: A 71-year-old woman presents to the emergency department alone with abrupt worsening of shortness of breath that began approximately 45 minutes ago while she was at home. She reports feeling unable to take a satisfying breath and has been breathing faster than usual. She describes a dry, irritating cough and a subjective low-grade feverish feeling but has not measured her temperature. She denies choking, aspiration, or a known recent exposure. She works as a nurse and says she had a respiratory infection about a week ago, with lingering fatigue and occasional cough since then. She is unsure whether her symptoms are worse when lying down and has not tried any medication before arrival. She denies chest pain, fainting, or coughing up blood. On examination, she appears uncomfortable and tachypneic, speaking in short phrases. Breath sounds are diminished at the bases with fine crackles bilaterally. No focal neurologic symptoms are reported.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute decompensated heart failure with cardiogenic pulmonary edema

Symptoms: shortness of breath; dry cough; rapid breathing; sweating; lightheadedness; crackles heard on lung examination
Case_History_Text: I’m a 71-year-old retired postal worker, and my wife brought me in after the ambulance was called this evening. I’ve been increasingly short of breath since yesterday, even when walking from one room to another, and I feel like I cannot get a satisfying breath. I have a dry cough without bringing anything up.
