Symptoms: Dyspnea for one day; dry cough; low-grade feverish feeling; tachypnea; crackles; chest tightness; leg heaviness
Case_History_Text: EMS brings an 84-year-old man to the emergency department with his daughter after she noticed worsening shortness of breath over the past day. He reports a dry cough, feeling mildly feverish, chest tightness, and heaviness in both legs. He is breathing rapidly and has crackles on auscultation. He denies a sharp, localized chest pain. He is a retired postal worker with a history of seasonal allergies and a productive cough last winter. His daughter adds that he recently completed a long trip. He is alert, speaking in short sentences, and has no reported recent medication changes.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute decompensated heart failure with pulmonary edema

Symptoms: dyspnea; dry cough; tachypnea; crackles; low-grade feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: A 77-year-old woman was brought to the emergency department by her adult daughter for shortness of breath that began last night and has gradually become more noticeable this morning. She describes a dry, irritating cough and says she has felt mildly feverish but has not measured her temperature at home. Her daughter noticed that she was breathing faster while walking from the bedroom to the kitchen and encouraged her to seek care. The patient denies choking or a known aspiration event. She reports seasonal allergies but no recent medication changes and no prior similar episode recalled. She has continued to drink fluids but has had little appetite today. On arrival, she is alert and speaking in complete sentences, though with visibly increased respiratory effort and a rapid breathing rate. Auscultation reveals crackles at both lung bases. She is a retired librarian who lives independently, with her daughter nearby and available to assist.

Symptoms: shortness of breath; cough; rapid breathing; crackling sounds with breathing; wheezing; chest tightness; low-grade feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: I am 71 and retired from working for the postal service. Since yesterday evening, my breathing has been coming and going, but it became harder this morning, so EMS was called. I feel short of breath even while sitting and have been breathing faster than usual. I have a cough and some tightness across my chest. A family member noticed wheezing last night, and I have felt mildly feverish, though I have not checked my temperature. I was told my breathing sounds crackly. I have smoked for many years and am also obese. My neighbor came with me to the emergency department because I was worried about getting here alone.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)

Symptoms: Dyspnea; dry cough; tachypnea; bibasilar crackles; wheezing reported by spouse; leg heaviness; sweating; possible low-grade fever
Case_History_Text: 75-y/o woman, software engineer, arrived to ED with spouse for SOB beginning earlier today and worsening over several hours. Reports dry cough, chest heaviness with breathing, sweaty episodes, and both legs feeling heavy. Spouse noticed wheezing at home. Denies known sick contacts. Hx HTN and seasonal allergies; returned recently from a long trip. Triage: mildly tachypneic, speaking in short sentences, afebrile to low-grade temp, BP elevated, pulse regular. Auscultation notable for bibasilar crackles with occasional wheeze. No acute distress at rest, but symptoms increase with walking.

Symptoms: shortness of breath; rapid breathing; dry cough; sweating; crackling breath sounds; possible fever
Case_History_Text: I brought my 86-year-old husband to the emergency department after calling EMS from our apartment this evening. He had been sitting in his recliner when he suddenly became much more short of breath over about two hours. He was breathing quickly and said he could not get comfortable, even after sitting upright. He has a dry cough and was sweating more than usual. At home he felt warm, although we did not check his temperature. The paramedic mentioned hearing crackling sounds when listening to his lungs. He works part-time as a retail manager and is usually active around the house. His only ongoing issue that I know of is seasonal allergies. He has not described chest pain, and I have not noticed any recent choking or injury.

Symptoms: shortness of breath; rapid breathing; cough with sputum; chest tightness; sweating; crackles on examination; possible fever
Case_History_Text: I am writing about my 78-year-old wife, who arrived at the emergency department with me after about six hours of worsening shortness of breath. She has been breathing quickly and says her chest feels tight, especially when walking from room to room. She is coughing up small amounts of yellowish sputum and has felt sweaty and warm, though we did not measure her temperature at home. Staff noted crackling sounds when listening to her lungs. She is an obese woman who farms part-time and has a history of poorly controlled blood pressure. Until this morning she was doing her usual chores. She has no known recent injury, and I brought her medication list with us.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute decompensated heart failure with pulmonary edema

Symptoms: dyspnea; tachypnea; cough; crackles; leg heaviness; lightheadedness; possible fever
Case_History_Text: EMS handoff: This is a 64-year-old man, a security guard, brought in with his spouse after we were called for worsening shortness of breath over the last three hours. He reports a mostly dry cough but says he brought up a small amount of sputum earlier today. He feels both legs are heavy and became lightheaded while walking from his post. His spouse says he seemed warm at home. Respirations were rapid on arrival, with crackles heard in both lower lung fields. He is obese, had a productive cough last winter, and returned recently from a long trip. No chest discomfort reported.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute decompensated heart failure with pulmonary edema

Symptoms: Dyspnea; cough; tachypnea; crackles; sweating; low-grade feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: A 78-year-old woman was brought to the emergency department by a former coworker after developing worsening shortness of breath over the past 45 minutes. She had been sitting at home when she noticed that breathing required more effort, followed by a persistent cough and a sensation of chest congestion. Her coworker reports that she appeared sweaty and was breathing rapidly during the drive. The patient describes feeling mildly feverish but denies shaking chills. She has not clearly identified a trigger and denies recent choking or known exposure to irritants. On arrival, she remains uncomfortable with exertion and speaks in short phrases, though she is able to answer questions appropriately. Lung examination reveals rapid respirations and fine crackles at both bases. She reports no prior similar episode that she can recall. Her history includes poorly controlled blood pressure, and she is a retired nurse. Medication adherence has been inconsistent recently. She has no additional history available from the accompanying coworker.

Symptoms: sudden shortness of breath; sharp pleuritic chest pain; rapid breathing; racing heartbeat; fever; productive cough; sweating
Case_History_Text: A 46-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by a coworker after developing abrupt shortness of breath approximately 45 minutes ago while working in an auto repair shop. She describes a sharp pain along the right side of her chest that worsens with deep inspiration and coughing. Her coworker noticed that she became sweaty, pale-appearing, and unable to finish a sentence without pausing to breathe. She reports several days of cough producing small amounts of yellow sputum and feeling feverish, though she had continued working. Since the episode began, she has felt her heart racing and has been breathing much faster than usual. She denies fainting and has not reported vomiting. Her medical history includes poorly controlled blood pressure, with inconsistent use of a prescribed medication. She is a mechanic and reports no recent medication changes. The coworker provides additional history because the patient remains visibly short of breath and anxious during questioning.

Symptoms: sudden shortness of breath; sharp pain with breathing; rapid breathing; racing heartbeat; fever; chest tightness; sweating; heaviness in both legs
Case_History_Text: I’m 61 and work as a postal worker. Since yesterday, I’ve felt feverish and worn out after getting over a respiratory infection. This afternoon, while walking from the mailbox to my truck, I suddenly became very short of breath. My chest feels tight, and I have a sharp pain on the right side whenever I take a deep breath. My heart has been racing, I’m breathing fast, and I broke out in a sweat. Both legs have felt unusually heavy tonight, though I haven’t noticed a specific injury. I returned several days ago from a long trip where I was sitting most of the time. My spouse called EMS, and they brought me to the emergency department. I’m frightened because the breathing trouble came on so abruptly.

Symptoms: sudden dyspnea since last night; pleuritic chest pain; chest tightness; tachypnea; tachycardia; fever; productive cough; lightheadedness; bilateral leg heaviness
Case_History_Text: 56F daycare worker arrives alone to ED, reporting abrupt onset SOB and sharp pain with inspiration beginning last night. Also notes chest tightness, lightheadedness, feverishness, productive cough, and heaviness in both legs. Appears anxious and mildly breathless while speaking. Triage: tachypneic and tachycardic; temperature mildly elevated, BP stable, oxygen saturation acceptable on room air. Reports recent prolonged travel with many hours seated. Takes oral contraceptives. States a relative previously had a blood clot. No reported injury. Awaiting further evaluation.

Symptoms: sudden shortness of breath; sharp pain with breathing; rapid breathing; racing heartbeat; fever; intermittent cough with occasional sputum
Case_History_Text: I brought my husband to the emergency department after calling EMS this morning. He is 47 and works as a high school coach. He had been feeling unwell on and off since yesterday evening, with a cough that was mostly dry but produced a little sputum later in the night. This morning, his breathing suddenly became much harder, and he complained of a sharp pain on the right side of his chest whenever he took a deep breath. He felt hot and had chills, though we did not measure his temperature. EMS said he was breathing quickly and his heart was beating fast. His only known medical problem is high blood pressure, and he takes medication for it. I rode with him and stayed beside him during triage.

Symptoms: sudden shortness of breath; sharp pain with breathing; rapid breathing; racing heartbeat; low-grade feverish feeling; wheezing; chest tightness
Case_History_Text: I am a 58-year-old woman and work as an office administrator. Most of today I have felt increasingly unwell, and the shortness of breath came on quite suddenly while I was doing light activities at home. Taking a deep breath causes a sharp pain on the side of my chest, and I also feel tightness across my chest. My neighbor noticed that I was breathing quickly and said she could hear wheezing, so she brought me to the emergency department. My heart feels like it is racing. I have felt feverish, though I have not checked my temperature. My medical history includes high blood pressure and obesity. I have not had this combination of symptoms before.

Symptoms: sudden dyspnea; pleuritic chest pain; tachypnea; tachycardia; chest tightness; sweating; low-grade feverish feeling; wheezing
Case_History_Text: EMS handoff: This 60-year-old man was brought to the emergency department after a coworker called EMS for abrupt shortness of breath that began about two hours ago while he was at home. He reports sharp chest discomfort worsened by deep breathing, a sense of chest tightness, sweating, and feeling mildly feverish. A family member noticed wheezing before arrival. He recently underwent orthopedic surgery. History includes poorly controlled blood pressure and seasonal allergies. On assessment he is tachypneic and tachycardic but awake and able to answer questions; he arrived with his coworker, who provided additional history.

Symptoms: sudden dyspnea; pleuritic chest pain; tachypnea; tachycardia; fever; dry cough; chest tightness
Case_History_Text: A 53-year-old woman, currently enrolled as a college student, arrives alone to the emergency department for approximately six hours of worsening shortness of breath. She reports that the symptoms began suddenly while she was walking across campus and have persisted despite resting. She describes a sharp discomfort along the right side of her chest that increases with deep inspiration and coughing, along with a sensation of chest tightness. She has noticed a dry cough and felt warm at home but denies producing sputum. On arrival, she appears uncomfortable and is breathing rapidly with a fast pulse. She denies fainting, vomiting, or recent trauma. She has seasonal allergies but no other significant medical history that she volunteers. She takes an over-the-counter allergy medication intermittently and reports no recent medication changes. She came directly to the department after a friend advised her to seek evaluation, but the friend did not accompany her.

Symptoms: sudden shortness of breath; sharp pain with breathing; rapid breathing; racing heartbeat; fever; sweating; chest tightness; lightheadedness
Case_History_Text: I’m 66 and work as a mechanic. About three hours ago, while I was finishing up in the shop, I suddenly became short of breath and started breathing very fast. I felt a sharp pain on the right side of my chest whenever I took a deep breath, along with tightness across my chest. My heart seemed to be pounding, and I got sweaty and lightheaded, so a coworker called EMS and came with me. I’ve also felt feverish today. I had a bad respiratory infection a couple of weeks ago that mostly improved. Last week, I spent nearly ten hours traveling by bus for a family visit, with only brief stops to stretch.

Symptoms: sudden dyspnea; pleuritic chest pain; chest tightness; tachypnea; tachycardia; fever; productive cough; reported wheezing; leg heaviness
Case_History_Text: 63-year-old woman, graphic designer, arrived to ED with spouse for 45 min of sudden shortness of breath and sharp pain worse with inspiration. Appears anxious and is tachypneic with a rapid pulse. Reports chest tightness, feverishness, and a productive cough; spouse noticed wheezing at home. She also describes heaviness in both legs without reported injury. History includes poorly controlled hypertension and recent orthopedic surgery. She mentions a relative with a prior blood clot. No additional history available during triage. Placed in a treatment area for prompt evaluation.

Symptoms: sudden shortness of breath; sharp pain with breathing; rapid breathing; racing heartbeat; fever; wheezing; lightheadedness
Case_History_Text: I brought my 24-year-old brother to the emergency department after EMS was called from his campus job. He is a college student and had been working with a coworker when, over the past day, he developed a sudden worsening of shortness of breath and a sharp pain that became worse whenever he took a deep breath. He has been breathing quickly and says his heart feels like it is pounding. Earlier, I heard a wheezing sound when he was resting, and he became lightheaded while walking to the car. He felt warm at home and had a fever. He has a history of high blood pressure but is usually active and independent. His coworker accompanied us and provided some of the timeline.

Symptoms: sudden shortness of breath; sharp pain worse with breathing; rapid breathing; racing heartbeat; fever; sweating; lightheadedness; dry cough
Case_History_Text: Hello, I am a 49-year-old librarian who came to the emergency department with my adult daughter. Since last night, I have become suddenly short of breath, and I feel a sharp pain on the right side of my chest whenever I take a deep breath or cough. I am breathing quickly and can feel my heart racing. I have also been sweaty and lightheaded, though I have not fainted. I developed a dry cough and fever today. I had what seemed like a respiratory infection about two weeks ago, with congestion and fatigue that mostly improved. Five days ago, I returned from a long trip involving many hours of sitting. I have no known injury.

Symptoms: sudden intermittent dyspnea; pleuritic chest pain; tachypnea; tachycardia; fever; chest tightness; dry cough; subjective wheezing; leg heaviness
Case_History_Text: EMS handoff: A 31-year-old man, a postal worker, was brought from home to the emergency department after his adult child called EMS. He reports episodes of sudden shortness of breath and sharp pain with breathing beginning yesterday evening, recurring overnight and becoming more noticeable today. His child heard wheezing, and he also describes chest tightness, a dry cough, and heaviness in both legs. He feels feverish. History includes recent orthopedic surgery and high blood pressure; his medication list reportedly includes an oral contraceptive. On arrival he is alert, speaking in short phrases, temperature 38.1°C, heart rate 112, respiratory rate 28, and blood pressure 148/92.

Symptoms: sudden shortness of breath; pleuritic chest pain; chest tightness; rapid breathing; racing heartbeat; sweating; fever
Case_History_Text: A 66-year-old woman presents to the emergency department alone after developing sudden shortness of breath while preparing for an afternoon practice at the high school where she works as a coach. She reports that the breathing difficulty began earlier today and has persisted, making it uncomfortable to walk or speak in full sentences. She describes a sharp pain along the right side of her chest that worsens with deep inspiration, accompanied by a sense of chest tightness, a racing heartbeat, and sweating. She has felt feverish since last night but has not measured her temperature at home. She denies any known injury or recent respiratory illness. She has smoked cigarettes for many years and says she has occasionally had a morning cough, though today’s breathlessness is distinctly different from her usual symptoms. She has no one with her and provides the history clearly, pausing frequently because of dyspnea. On arrival, she is visibly uncomfortable with rapid breathing and a fast pulse.

Symptoms: sudden shortness of breath; sharp pain with breathing; rapid breathing; racing heartbeat; heavy-feeling legs; low-grade feverish feeling; wheezing reported by family
Case_History_Text: I’m 64 and usually get around without help. About two hours ago, while I was at home, I suddenly became very short of breath and started breathing fast. I have a sharp pain on the side of my chest that gets worse when I take a deep breath. My heart feels like it is racing, and both legs feel unusually heavy. I’ve felt a little feverish today, though I did not check my temperature. A family member thought they heard me wheezing. I had a respiratory infection recently and have high blood pressure. EMS was called, and I came to the emergency department with a former coworker who was nearby. I’m unemployed right now and have not had symptoms like this before.

Symptoms: sudden dyspnea; pleuritic chest pain; tachypnea; tachycardia; productive cough; low-grade feverish feeling; leg heaviness; lightheadedness
Case_History_Text: 57F accountant arrived to ED with adult daughter, reporting abrupt onset SOB and sharp pain worse with inspiration about 6 hrs ago. Also notes productive cough, feeling feverish, bilateral leg heaviness, and intermittent lightheadedness. Hx poorly controlled HTN/high BP and years of cigarette smoking. Triage: visibly tachypneic, speaking in short sentences; HR 112, RR 28, BP 168/94, T 37.8°C, SpO2 95% on room air. No recent evaluation documented. Daughter provides additional history; pt appears anxious but alert.

Symptoms: sudden shortness of breath; sharp pain worsened by breathing; rapid breathing; fast heartbeat; fever; leg heaviness; wheezing
Case_History_Text: I brought my 24-year-old brother to the emergency department after EMS was called from the farm. He had been working with a coworker when, about three hours ago, he suddenly became short of breath and complained of a sharp pain on the side of his chest that worsened whenever he took a deep breath. His breathing has stayed very fast, and his heart seemed to be racing when I felt his wrist. He felt hot at home and said both legs felt unusually heavy, though he did not describe a fall or injury. Our mother noticed wheezing while he was resting. He has had trouble keeping his blood pressure under control but takes no regular medicines that I know of. He arrived with his coworker and was still visibly breathing hard.

Symptoms: sudden shortness of breath; sharp pain worse with breathing; rapid breathing; racing heartbeat; fever; chest tightness; wheezing; sweating
Case_History_Text: Hello, I am a 52-year-old woman and my neighbor brought me to the emergency department because I suddenly became very short of breath about 45 minutes ago. I have a sharp pain on the right side of my chest that worsens when I take a deep breath, along with chest tightness, fast breathing, and a pounding heartbeat. My daughter noticed wheezing when she called me earlier. I also feel hot and have been sweating, although I have not checked my temperature. I take medication for high blood pressure and had orthopedic surgery recently. I work as an office administrator and was feeling normal earlier today. I am frightened because the breathing difficulty came on so abruptly.

Symptoms: sudden dyspnea; pleuritic chest pain; chest tightness; tachypnea; tachycardia; fever; lightheadedness; sweating; productive cough
Case_History_Text: EMS handoff: This is a 78-year-old man, a retired nurse, brought in with a former coworker after EMS was called for sudden worsening shortness of breath over the past day. He reports sharp pain with breathing, chest tightness, lightheadedness, and an episode of sweating. He has had a fever and productive cough. He is breathing rapidly with a fast pulse on arrival. His history includes years of smoking, recent orthopedic surgery, and a long-distance trip several weeks ago. His coworker says he became visibly distressed while resting at home.

Symptoms: sudden dyspnea; pleuritic chest pain; tachypnea; tachycardia; fever; productive cough; leg heaviness
Case_History_Text: A 56-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by her adult daughter for sudden shortness of breath that began last night while she was resting at home. She describes sharp right-sided chest pain that worsens with deep inspiration and reports feeling unable to take a full breath. Since yesterday afternoon, she has also had a productive cough with yellowish sputum, chills, and a subjective fever. Her daughter noticed that she was breathing rapidly this morning and urged her to come in. The patient reports a heavy, uncomfortable sensation in both legs, somewhat greater on the left, without a clear injury or new swelling. She recently underwent orthopedic surgery and has been spending more time seated during recovery. At triage, she is anxious, tachypneic, and tachycardic, with a temperature of 38.1°C and blood pressure of 132/78 mmHg. She works as a librarian and has no known recent sick contacts. She denies fainting but feels markedly fatigued.

Symptoms: sudden shortness of breath; sharp pain with breathing; rapid breathing; racing heartbeat; feverish feeling; wheezing; sweating; chest tightness
Case_History_Text: I’m a 51-year-old nonbinary software engineer. Since yesterday evening, I’ve had episodes where I suddenly can’t catch my breath, and today they became more intense. I have a sharp pain on the side of my chest that worsens when I take a deep breath, along with chest tightness and sweating. My sister noticed a wheezing sound when I was resting, and I’ve felt feverish on and off. EMS was called when my breathing became very fast and my heart felt like it was pounding. I’m here in the emergency department with a coworker. I’m overweight and take an oral contraceptive; otherwise, I have not noticed anything unusual recently.

Symptoms: sudden dyspnea; pleuritic chest pain; tachypnea; tachycardia; fever; dry cough; chest tightness; wheezing; leg heaviness
Case_History_Text: 69-y/o woman brought to ED by coworker from her security job for sudden worsening SOB beginning earlier today. Reports sharp L-sided chest pain with inspiration, chest tightness, dry cough, and feeling feverish. Coworker says she heard wheezing; pt notes both legs have felt heavy since yesterday. She is breathing rapidly and appears uncomfortable on arrival, with a fast pulse. Smoked for many years and had a respiratory infection recently, treated outside the hospital. States a close relative previously had a blood clot. No medications or allergies available at triage.

Symptoms: sudden shortness of breath; sharp pain worse with deep breathing; rapid breathing; fast heartbeat; fever; dry cough with occasional sputum; obesity
Case_History_Text: I brought my 54-year-old father to the emergency department after calling EMS when his breathing suddenly became difficult at home about two hours ago. He is a warehouse supervisor and had been resting after work when he complained of a sharp pain on the side of his chest that worsened whenever he took a deep breath. Since then, he has been breathing quickly and says his heart feels like it is racing. He has felt feverish and has alternated between a dry cough and bringing up a small amount of sputum. He was able to walk earlier today but became too winded to continue. He is obese but usually manages his daily activities without assistance. No similar episode has happened recently.

Symptoms: sudden shortness of breath; sharp pain worsened by breathing; rapid breathing; racing heartbeat; chest tightness; heavy-feeling legs; low-grade feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: I am a 64-year-old librarian who came to the emergency department with my neighbor because I suddenly became short of breath about six hours ago. I have a sharp pain along the side of my chest that gets worse when I take a deep breath, along with chest tightness and a racing heartbeat. I am breathing faster than usual and feel generally feverish, though I have not measured my temperature. Both legs feel unusually heavy. I had orthopedic surgery recently and spent many hours traveling by car shortly afterward. I had been recovering fairly well until today and did not have this breathing problem before the sudden onset. My neighbor noticed I looked uncomfortable and insisted on bringing me in.

Symptoms: sudden shortness of breath; pleuritic chest pain; rapid breathing; fast heart rate; fever; chest tightness; wheezing; leg heaviness; sweating
Case_History_Text: EMS handoff: This is a 38-year-old man, a postal worker, brought from home with his adult daughter after three hours of sudden shortness of breath and sharp pain that worsens when he breathes in. His daughter noticed wheezing, and he reports chest tightness, heavy-feeling legs, sweating, and feeling feverish. He has been breathing rapidly and remains tachycardic but is awake and speaking in short sentences. History includes high blood pressure, recent orthopedic surgery, and use of an oral contraceptive. No fainting was reported. He received supportive care during transport and arrived in the emergency department for evaluation.

Symptoms: sudden dyspnea; pleuritic chest pain; tachypnea; tachycardia; fever; productive cough; leg heaviness
Case_History_Text: A 30-year-old woman presents to the emergency department alone after developing abrupt shortness of breath approximately 45 minutes ago while sorting mail during her postal route. She describes sharp left-sided chest discomfort that worsens with deep inspiration and coughing, along with rapid breathing and a pounding heartbeat. She reports feeling feverish since earlier today and has had a productive cough with small amounts of yellow sputum since yesterday. Over the same period, both legs have felt unusually heavy, though she denies a fall or recent injury. She has a history of high blood pressure and says she takes a daily medication, but she is unsure of its name. She denies known heart or lung disease and has not experienced similar symptoms previously. On arrival, she is anxious, speaking in complete sentences, and appears mildly flushed. Her breathing is visibly rapid, and her pulse is elevated; initial blood pressure is mildly high. She arrived without family or friends and provides the history herself.

Symptoms: dyspnea; chest tightness; cough; wheeze; leg heaviness
Case_History_Text: A 31-year-old woman was brought to the emergency department by her adult daughter for sudden worsening shortness of breath that began approximately 45 minutes before arrival. She describes a sensation of chest tightness and difficulty getting a full breath, accompanied by a persistent dry cough and audible wheezing. She reports that both legs feel unusually heavy, without describing focal pain or a visible change in one leg compared with the other. She denies fainting, confusion, or severe chest pain, and says the discomfort has remained fairly constant since it began. She has noticed intermittent breathing difficulty in the past but has not sought regular care for it recently. Her medical history includes poorly controlled blood pressure, and she acknowledges inconsistent follow-up. She works as an accountant and was at home reviewing paperwork when the symptoms started. Her daughter says the patient appeared anxious and was speaking in shorter phrases during the drive. No clear provoking event is identified.

Symptoms: shortness of breath; chest tightness; cough; wheezing; lightheadedness
Case_History_Text: I’m 48 and work as a graphic designer. Over the past day, I’ve become increasingly short of breath, with a tight feeling across my chest and a whistling sound when I breathe. I’ve been coughing too—mostly dry, though I brought up a small amount of clear mucus a few times. I feel lightheaded when I walk across the room, but I have not passed out. The symptoms seemed worse this evening, so my neighbor called EMS and came with me to the emergency department. I’m overweight and smoked for many years, although I quit several years ago. I don’t usually get this winded, and the breathing discomfort has made it difficult to relax.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)

Symptoms: dyspnea since last night; chest tightness; productive cough; wheezing; feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: 44-year-old woman, restaurant cook, presents to ED with adult daughter for shortness of breath beginning last night. Reports chest tightness, productive cough, and feeling feverish without a measured temperature. Daughter noticed audible wheezing at home. Symptoms followed a recent respiratory infection. Patient also reports recent prolonged travel and has obesity. No additional history provided at triage. Speaking in short phrases but remains alert and cooperative. Denies other concerns at this time. Triage note: respiratory symptoms ongoing overnight, cough bringing up small amounts of sputum, wheeze worse with activity.

Symptoms: dyspnea; chest tightness; dry cough; wheeze; lightheadedness
Case_History_Text: I am his older sister, and I met him in the emergency department after his neighbor called EMS and accompanied him. He is a 29-year-old man who works as a pharmacist. Since yesterday evening, his breathing has been coming and going, with a feeling of tightness across his chest. He has been coughing without bringing anything up and says he can hear himself wheezing. This afternoon he became lightheaded while walking across his apartment, which worried his neighbor. He recently returned from a long trip and seemed tired afterward, but he had been functioning normally until last night. He has not described fever or vomiting. He is usually active, and this episode appears more uncomfortable than anything I have seen from him before.

Symptoms: shortness of breath; chest tightness; dry cough; wheezing; leg heaviness
Case_History_Text: Hello, I’m a 37-year-old woman and work as an auto mechanic. I came to the emergency department with a coworker because I’ve been short of breath for most of today. My chest feels tight, and I have a dry cough with noticeable wheezing, especially when I walk or try to talk for long. Both legs feel unusually heavy, though I have not noticed a specific injury. I recently took a long trip with several hours of sitting, but felt well afterward until today. I sometimes use an inhaler as needed, although these symptoms feel more persistent than usual. I do not remember choking or inhaling anything at work. Please let me know what information you need.

Symptoms: dyspnea; chest tightness; productive cough; wheeze; leg heaviness; low-grade feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: EMS handoff: We brought in a 44-year-old man who works as a mechanic and arrived alone after calling for help at home. He reports about two hours of progressively difficult breathing with chest tightness, frequent coughing that brings up a small amount of sputum, and audible wheezing. He describes both legs as feeling heavy but denies any recent injury. He says he has felt mildly feverish and tired today. History includes poorly controlled blood pressure and seasonal allergies; he also reports that a close relative previously had a blood clot. No 12-lead interpretation available.

Symptoms: dyspnea; chest tightness; productive cough; wheeze; bilateral leg heaviness
Case_History_Text: A 38-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with a coworker for approximately six hours of gradually worsening shortness of breath, chest tightness, cough, and wheezing. She works as a janitor and reports that symptoms began during an evening shift, initially as an irritating cough that became productive of small amounts of pale sputum. She describes the chest sensation as pressure-like and more noticeable when taking a deeper breath, without a clearly identified trigger. She also reports a heavy, tired feeling in both legs since returning from a long trip several days ago, but denies focal leg pain or visible swelling. She has not measured a fever and denies fainting, coughing blood, or vomiting. She reports no recent illness besides mild nasal congestion and has not experienced symptoms this intense before. Her coworker states that she appeared increasingly winded while walking between work areas and brought her directly to the ED.

Symptoms: shortness of breath; chest tightness; productive cough; wheezing; feeling feverish
Case_History_Text: I’m a 24-year-old man who works as a mechanic. About three hours ago, I started getting short of breath, and it has gradually become harder to take a full breath. My chest feels tight, and I’ve been coughing up small amounts of mucus. I can hear myself wheezing when I breathe, especially when I try to walk or talk. I’ve felt feverish but haven’t checked my temperature. My neighbor called EMS and came with me to the emergency department. I’m overweight and have been told my blood pressure is poorly controlled, though I don’t always keep up with it. This came on during an ordinary day at home after work, and I’m feeling anxious because the breathing discomfort has not eased.

Symptoms: dyspnea; chest tightness; dry cough; wheeze; sweating; lightheadedness
Case_History_Text: 40-year-old woman, accountant, brought to ED by adult daughter for sudden worsening dyspnea over 45 min. Reports chest tightness, dry cough, audible wheeze, sweating, and feeling lightheaded. Recently recovering from a respiratory infection; reports seasonal allergies. No additional history obtained at triage. Patient speaking in short phrases but remains alert and cooperative. Daughter states a close relative previously had a blood clot. No medication list available. Triage note: increased work of breathing and intermittent wheeze noted; placed in treatment area for prompt evaluation.

Symptoms: shortness of breath; chest tightness; cough; wheezing
Case_History_Text: I brought my neighbor to the emergency department after EMS was called this evening. He is 40 and works as a high school coach. He had a respiratory infection about a week ago and seemed to be improving, but over the past day his breathing has become noticeably harder. He first developed a dry cough, which later became occasional and productive of a small amount of clear mucus. He says his chest feels tight and that he cannot get a satisfying breath. I can hear wheezing when he talks and walks, and he has needed to pause frequently to catch his breath. He has not mentioned fainting or severe chest pain. Before today, he was active and managing his usual work and household activities.

Symptoms: dyspnea; chest tightness; dry cough; wheeze
Case_History_Text: Hello, I am a 37-year-old woman and work as an office administrator. I came to the emergency department with a coworker because I have felt short of breath since last night. My chest feels tight, and I have had a dry cough with episodes of wheezing. My sister noticed the wheeze while we were talking on the phone this morning. I have felt mildly feverish but have not measured a temperature. About two weeks ago, I had what seemed like a respiratory infection that was improving until these symptoms began. I have not had this degree of breathing difficulty before. A relative has had a blood clot in the past, which makes me concerned and is worth mentioning.

Symptoms: dyspnea; chest tightness; cough; wheeze; sweating; lightheadedness
Case_History_Text: EMS handoff: We were called to the patient’s home for a 48-year-old man with intermittent shortness of breath since yesterday evening. His spouse reports hearing him wheeze and says he has had a dry cough, chest tightness, sweating, and episodes of lightheadedness. He appeared uncomfortable while walking to the stretcher but remained able to speak in full sentences. The patient reports a history of obesity and poorly controlled high blood pressure; he works as a home health aide. No additional history was available during transport. He arrives in the emergency department with his spouse for further evaluation.

Symptoms: dyspnea; chest tightness; productive cough; wheeze; lightheadedness
Case_History_Text: A 24-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by her spouse for shortness of breath that began earlier today and has gradually become more noticeable. She describes a tight feeling across the chest and says breathing feels harder when walking or talking for extended periods. She has had intermittent wheezing and a cough producing small amounts of yellowish sputum. She also reports feeling lightheaded during several coughing episodes but has not fainted. About a week ago, she had what she considered a respiratory infection with nasal congestion and a scratchy throat; most of those symptoms improved before today. She works at a daycare and has noticed several children there with recent coughs. She denies known chronic lung disease and has not experienced this exact combination of symptoms previously. Her spouse says she appeared more uncomfortable over the past two hours, prompting them to seek emergency care.

Symptoms: shortness of breath; chest tightness; cough; wheezing; lightheadedness; feeling feverish
Case_History_Text: I’m 28 and work as a pharmacist. About two hours ago, while finishing my shift, I suddenly started feeling short of breath and noticed a tight sensation across my chest. I began coughing and could hear myself wheezing, which made it harder to speak comfortably. I also feel lightheaded and somewhat feverish, although I haven’t checked my temperature. A coworker stayed with me and called EMS, then came with me to the emergency department. I’ve had seasonal allergies for years, especially during this time of year, but this feels more intense than usual. My father had a blood clot when he was older. I haven’t had anything like this recently and was feeling normal earlier today.

Symptoms: Dyspnea; chest tightness; dry cough; wheeze; lightheadedness; low-grade feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: 41-year-old woman presents alone to ED with ~6 hrs of worsening shortness of breath, chest tightness, dry cough, and audible wheeze. Reports feeling mildly feverish and lightheaded, without fainting. Symptoms began after returning from recent long-distance travel. She is a software engineer with obesity and a several-year smoking history. No home treatment documented. Speaking in full sentences but appears uncomfortable. Denies other concerns at triage. No prior similar episode details available.

Symptoms: dyspnea; chest tightness; dry cough; wheeze; sweating
Case_History_Text: I am his older sister, and I brought my 29-year-old brother to the emergency department after EMS was called. He works as an accountant and had been feeling well until about three hours ago, when he developed increasing shortness of breath and a tight sensation across his chest. He began coughing without bringing anything up and said he was wheezing. By the time we left home, he was sweaty and speaking in shorter phrases, though he remained awake and able to walk. He had recently returned from a long bus trip, but he had not complained of anything during the journey. He normally lives independently and came into the department alone while I spoke with the triage staff.

Symptoms: shortness of breath; chest tightness; cough with sputum; wheezing; bilateral leg heaviness; low-grade feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: I’m a 27-year-old nurse and arrived in the emergency department with my spouse because I suddenly became short of breath about 45 minutes ago. My chest feels tight, and I’m wheezing more when I try to take a deep breath. I’ve also had a cough producing a small amount of mucus and feel mildly feverish, though I have not checked my temperature. Both legs feel unusually heavy, without a clear injury. My blood pressure has been running high lately, and I have not been consistent about follow-up. A close relative previously had a blood clot. I was feeling normal earlier today and have not had this combination of symptoms before.

Symptoms: Dyspnea; chest tightness; cough with sputum; wheeze; lightheadedness; sweating
Case_History_Text: EMS brought a 29-year-old man to the emergency department after he called for increasing shortness of breath over the past day. He reports chest tightness, frequent cough producing small amounts of sputum, and audible wheezing. He became lightheaded and sweaty while walking from his apartment and called for help. He arrived alone and works as a home health aide. He reports smoking for several years, poorly controlled blood pressure, and use of an inhaler as needed, though he has not been using it consistently. He denies other concerns during handoff.

Symptoms: dyspnea; chest tightness; dry cough; wheezing
Case_History_Text: A 19-year-old woman who works as a retail manager presents to the emergency department with a coworker for shortness of breath that began last night and became more noticeable this morning. She describes a sensation of tightness across the chest and difficulty getting a satisfying breath. Her cough has been dry, without sputum, and a family member noticed audible wheezing during a telephone conversation earlier today. She reports a recent respiratory infection with several days of nasal congestion and throat irritation, now mostly improved. She denies having similar symptoms this severe before, though she recalls occasional mild breathing difficulty during past colds. She has been able to walk but feels winded more quickly than usual. She denies fainting, severe chest pain, or known exposure to smoke or other strong irritants. Her coworker states that she appeared uncomfortable during the drive but remained alert and able to speak in complete sentences.

Symptoms: dyspnea; chest tightness; cough; wheeze; sweating; lightheadedness
Case_History_Text: I’m 49 and nonbinary, and my spouse called EMS because my breathing became harder tonight. This has been coming and going since yesterday evening. I feel tight across my chest and have been coughing, with a noticeable wheeze when I breathe out. At times I get sweaty and lightheaded, especially when I walk across the room, though sitting still helps somewhat. I had what seemed like a respiratory infection recently, with congestion and a sore throat that mostly improved. I use an inhaler as needed but have not needed it this often before. I’m unemployed right now and have been staying home a lot. I did not faint, and I have not noticed anything else unusual besides feeling short of breath and anxious.

Symptoms: dyspnea; chest tightness; cough with sputum; wheezing; sweating; leg heaviness
Case_History_Text: Triage note: 37-year-old woman, farmer, brought to ED by a neighbor for dyspnea and chest tightness beginning earlier today and worsening over the afternoon. Reports productive cough, audible wheezing noticed by family, and episodes of sweating. Also describes a vague heavy feeling in both legs without reported injury. Hx seasonal allergies, uses an inhaler PRN, and states BP has been poorly controlled. No additional history available at triage. Speaking in short but complete sentences, anxious but cooperative.

Symptoms: shortness of breath; chest tightness; dry cough; wheezing
Case_History_Text: I brought my husband to the emergency department after calling EMS because his breathing suddenly became difficult at home about two hours ago. He is 28 and works as a welder. He said his chest felt tight and that he could not get a satisfying breath. I could hear a whistling sound when he breathed, and he has had a persistent dry cough without bringing anything up. He used his usual inhaler, which he keeps for occasional breathing trouble, but it did not help as much as expected. He has not complained of fainting or severe chest pain. Until this episode he had been doing his normal activities. He was alert and speaking to us when EMS arrived, though he appeared frightened and was breathing faster than usual.

Symptoms: shortness of breath; chest tightness; dry cough; wheezing; leg heaviness; low-grade feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: Hello, I am writing about my breathing symptoms before I arrived at the emergency department. For about six hours, I have felt increasingly short of breath with a tight feeling across my chest. I have also had a dry cough and noticed wheezing, especially when walking or talking. My legs feel unusually heavy, although I have not noticed a specific injury. I have felt mildly feverish but have not checked my temperature. I am a 45-year-old woman and work as a home health aide. I am overweight and usually have seasonal allergies, but this feels more intense than my typical allergy symptoms. My neighbor brought me in because I seemed to be working harder to breathe.

Symptoms: dyspnea; chest tightness; cough; wheeze; sweating
Case_History_Text: EMS handoff: We were called for a 21-year-old man with three hours of worsening shortness of breath, chest tightness, cough, and audible wheeze. He is a college student who arrived alone after contacting emergency services from his apartment. He initially described a dry cough but later produced a small amount of clear sputum. He reports sweating during the episodes but denies fainting. He mentions poorly controlled blood pressure, a long bus trip several days ago, and a relative with a prior blood clot. He has had no known similar evaluation recently. He was alert and speaking in short phrases on arrival.

Symptoms: dyspnea; chest tightness; cough; wheeze; lightheadedness
Case_History_Text: A 40-year-old woman was brought to the emergency department by a coworker after developing abrupt shortness of breath while repairing equipment at work approximately 45 minutes earlier. She describes a bandlike tightness across the front of her chest and says she cannot take a satisfying deep breath. Her cough has been dry, and her coworker noticed audible wheezing during the drive. She reports feeling lightheaded but has not fainted. She denies fever, chills, productive sputum, or sharp pain with breathing. About a week ago, she had a respiratory illness with nasal congestion and a scratchy throat that was improving before today’s episode. She has continued working and states that the area where the symptoms began was dusty, though she does not recall a specific chemical exposure. She has had occasional breathing problems during prior colds but has never required emergency care for them. She arrived alert, speaking in short but complete sentences, and appears anxious about the sudden change in her breathing.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute asthma exacerbation (likely triggered by dust exposure following viral upper respiratory infection)

Symptoms: acute dyspnea; tachycardia; dizziness with near-syncope; chest tightness; dry cough
Case_History_Text: An 81-year-old woman was brought to the emergency department by her spouse after developing sudden worsening shortness of breath approximately 45 minutes before arrival. Her spouse reports that she became visibly breathless while walking from the kitchen to the living room and then had to sit down because of marked dizziness and a sensation that she might faint. She describes a vague, nonradiating chest tightness and a persistent dry cough but denies sharp, positional chest pain. She has felt more easily winded with routine activity over the past several days, though she had attributed this to poor sleep and age. She denies fever, chills, or recent respiratory illness. Her medical history includes poorly controlled blood pressure, and she acknowledges occasionally missing medications. She is a retired teacher and remains generally independent at home. Her spouse reports no witnessed loss of consciousness, confusion, or recent fall. On arrival, she appears anxious and breathless, with a rapid pulse and difficulty speaking in long sentences.

Symptoms: shortness of breath; racing heartbeat; dizziness and near-fainting; productive cough; sweating; low-grade feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: I am an 83-year-old retired accountant, and I came to the emergency department alone after someone called EMS for me. Since yesterday, I have become increasingly short of breath, even with small movements, and my heart feels like it is beating quickly. I have felt dizzy several times, including one episode when I thought I might pass out while walking to the kitchen. I have also been sweating more than usual and feel mildly feverish. I am coughing up a small amount of phlegm. I usually sleep with two pillows because lying flat is uncomfortable. My only regular health issue is seasonal allergies, and this feels different from them. I did not have chest pain, but I was worried when my breathing suddenly worsened this evening.

Symptoms: Dyspnea since last night; tachycardia; dizziness/near-syncope; sweating; feverish feeling; productive cough; wheezing reported by family
Case_History_Text: 63-year-old woman, accountant, brought to the ED by a coworker for worsening SOB since last night. Reports intermittent lightheadedness with near-fainting, rapid heartbeat, sweating, and feeling mildly feverish. Productive cough; family member noticed wheezing at home. Denies recent injury. States she has needed two pillows to sleep for several months. PMH notable for poorly controlled high blood pressure; medication adherence unclear. No known recent travel or sick contacts reported. Appears uncomfortable and mildly breathless while speaking, with tachycardia noted at triage.

Symptoms: shortness of breath; rapid heartbeat; dizziness and near-fainting; productive cough; sweating; intermittent episodes since yesterday evening
Case_History_Text: I am his daughter, and I brought my 86-year-old father to the emergency department after EMS was called by a coworker. He still drives a city bus and said he began feeling short of breath on and off yesterday evening. Today, while getting ready for work, he became sweaty, lightheaded, and felt as though he might pass out. His coworker noticed that his heart seemed to be racing and that he was breathing harder than usual, so they had him sit down and called for help. He has also had a cough bringing up a small amount of phlegm. He denies falling or losing consciousness. He has no known recent injury, and our family history includes a relative who previously had a blood clot.

Symptoms: Dyspnea; tachycardia; dizziness/near-syncope; productive cough; lightheadedness; low-grade feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: Hello, I’m a 60-year-old college student who came to the emergency department alone because I’ve been short of breath for most of today. My heart feels like it is racing, and I became lightheaded while walking across campus, nearly fainting but never fully losing consciousness. I have also had a cough bringing up a small amount of clear-yellow mucus and have felt feverish, though I did not check my temperature. I returned several days ago from a long trip with many hours of sitting. I have high blood pressure and take my prescribed medication, with no recent changes. I noticed my breathing was worse when climbing stairs this afternoon and wanted to be checked promptly.

Symptoms: Shortness of breath; rapid heartbeat; dizziness with near-fainting; leg heaviness; dry cough; sweating; chest tightness
Case_History_Text: EMS brings an 83-year-old man to the emergency department after he called for help from home, where he was alone. He reports about two hours of worsening shortness of breath, a racing heartbeat, sweating, chest tightness, and dizziness that nearly caused him to faint while walking across the room. He also describes both legs as unusually heavy and has had a dry cough. He is a retired accountant with high blood pressure, sleeps with two pillows, and recently recovered from a respiratory infection. He denies known injury and arrives awake, speaking in brief but clear sentences.

Symptoms: dyspnea; tachycardia; dizziness with near-syncope; productive cough; sweating
Case_History_Text: A 70-year-old woman was brought to the emergency department by a coworker after becoming increasingly short of breath during her afternoon bus route. She reports roughly six hours of worsening breathing difficulty, initially with activity and now present while sitting still. During the final route, she became lightheaded and had to pull over after feeling that she might faint, though she did not lose consciousness or fall. She describes a rapid, uncomfortable heartbeat and intermittent sweating. She has also had a productive cough since earlier today, with small amounts of clear-to-pale sputum. She denies a sharp focal pain but says her chest feels tight when she tries to take a deep breath. Her coworker notes that she appeared pale and unusually tired. The patient has a history of poorly controlled blood pressure and acknowledges missing several recent doses because of an irregular work schedule. She reports no recent illness requiring medical care and arrived walking with assistance.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute decompensated heart failure with pulmonary edema

Symptoms: Shortness of breath; rapid heartbeat; dizziness and near-fainting; chest tightness; wheezing; leg heaviness
Case_History_Text: I’m 62 and work as a welder. About three hours ago, while I was finishing up at home, I suddenly became short of breath and felt my heart racing. I got dizzy and had to sit down because I thought I might pass out. There is a tight feeling across my chest, but it does not feel sharply painful. My daughter said she could hear me wheezing when I tried to speak, and my legs feel unusually heavy. Both legs have been swelling toward the end of the day lately. I have high blood pressure, though I sometimes miss my pills. I live alone and came in after EMS was called; no one came with me.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute decompensated heart failure with pulmonary edema

Symptoms: dyspnea; tachycardia; dizziness/near-syncope; productive cough; wheezing; diaphoresis; lightheadedness
Case_History_Text: Triage note: 86-year-old woman, college student, brought to ED by spouse for abrupt worsening shortness of breath over 45 min. Family member heard wheezing before arrival. Reports productive cough, sweating, racing heartbeat, dizziness, and feeling nearly faint without loss of consciousness. Had a respiratory infection recently and normally sleeps on two pillows. Spouse reports recent prolonged travel. No further history available at triage. Patient is awake, speaking in short phrases, and appears uncomfortable. Symptoms began while resting at home. Denies recent fall or injury.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute decompensated heart failure with pulmonary edema

Symptoms: Shortness of breath; rapid heartbeat; dizziness and near-fainting; productive cough; low-grade feverish feeling; evening leg swelling
Case_History_Text: I brought my 87-year-old father to the emergency department after calling EMS because his breathing became noticeably worse over the past day. He said his heart was racing, and when he stood up from his chair this afternoon, he became dizzy and nearly fainted. He has been coughing up small amounts of phlegm and has felt feverish, though we did not check his temperature at home. I have also noticed that his legs have been swelling toward the evenings recently. He was a construction foreman for many years and usually insists on staying active, but today he was too short of breath to walk across the room without stopping. He is awake and answering questions, and I came with him in the ambulance.

Symptoms: Shortness of breath since last night; racing heartbeat; dizziness with near-fainting; sweating; low-grade feverish feeling; wheezing reported by family; difficulty lying flat
Case_History_Text: Hello, I am a 77-year-old woman and came to the emergency department alone. Since last night I have been unusually short of breath, even with small movements, and my heart feels like it is racing. I became dizzy this morning and nearly fainted while walking from the kitchen, though I did not fall. I have also been sweaty and felt mildly feverish. My daughter noticed wheezing when she called me, and I could hear it too while resting. I usually sleep with two pillows because lying flat is uncomfortable. I worked as a postal worker for many years. My blood pressure has not been well controlled lately, and I have missed some routine appointments.

Symptoms: Dyspnea; tachycardia; dizziness; near-syncope; intermittent cough; wheezing; diaphoresis
Case_History_Text: EMS brings an 81-year-old man, a retired librarian, from home after his neighbor called for increasing shortness of breath. He reports episodes beginning yesterday evening, with dizziness and feeling as though he might pass out, accompanied by sweating and a cough that is sometimes dry and sometimes brings up scant mucus. His neighbor noticed wheezing while he was resting. He recently recovered from a respiratory infection. He normally sleeps with two pillows and denies known personal clotting history, though a sibling had a blood clot. He is alert, speaking in short phrases, and tachycardic on arrival.

Symptoms: shortness of breath; rapid heartbeat; dizziness/near-syncope; sweating; low-grade feverish feeling; two-pillow sleeping
Case_History_Text: An 80-year-old woman who works part-time as a librarian was brought to the emergency department by a neighbor after becoming increasingly short of breath over most of today. She reports that her heart has felt unusually fast and that she became lightheaded while walking from the reading room to the staff area, needing to sit down because she thought she might faint. She describes intermittent sweating and a vague feverish feeling but has not measured her temperature. She denies complete loss of consciousness, significant chest pain, coughing up blood, or recent illness. For several weeks she has preferred sleeping on two pillows because breathing flat feels uncomfortable, though she cannot clearly say whether this has changed recently. She has noticed reduced stamina today but was able to walk independently before this episode. Her neighbor says she appeared pale and anxious but remained alert and conversant. She reports no recent travel or injury and arrived without supplemental oxygen.

Symptoms: shortness of breath; rapid heartbeat; dizziness; near-fainting; dry cough; wheezing; feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: I’m an 83-year-old retired accountant, and my neighbor came with me after EMS was called this afternoon. About two hours ago, I suddenly became much more short of breath while walking from the kitchen to the living room. My heart felt like it was racing, and I became dizzy enough that I had to sit down because I thought I might faint. I’ve had a dry cough since a respiratory infection last week, and my daughter said she heard me wheezing earlier. I’ve felt mildly feverish but have not checked my temperature. I usually sleep with two pillows, which has been my routine for some time. I have not had this degree of breathlessness before.

Symptoms: Dyspnea; tachycardia; dizziness/near-syncope; dry cough; chest tightness; diaphoresis; lightheadedness
Case_History_Text: 83-year-old woman, former bus driver, brought to ED by her daughter for ~6 hrs of worsening shortness of breath. Reports dry cough, chest tightness, sweating, and episodes of lightheadedness with near-fainting when standing. Feels her heart racing. States she has recently needed two pillows to sleep. History notable for poorly controlled hypertension and many years of cigarette use. No additional history available at triage. Patient appears anxious and mildly winded while speaking, but is able to answer questions appropriately. Daughter reports symptoms began while the patient was resting at home.

Symptoms: shortness of breath; rapid heartbeat; dizziness; near-fainting; productive cough; sweating
Case_History_Text: I brought my neighbor, an 83-year-old retired mechanic, to the emergency department after calling EMS because he became unusually short of breath about three hours ago. He said his heart was racing and that he felt lightheaded, nearly passing out when he stood up from his chair. He has also been coughing up small amounts of phlegm and was sweating despite the room being cool. He looked frightened and had to pause between sentences while walking to the ambulance. He has smoked for many years, though he quit briefly several times and still occasionally smokes. I do not know of any recent injury or illness. Until today, he had been managing his usual activities independently.

Symptoms: shortness of breath; rapid heartbeat; dizziness and near-fainting; chest tightness; heavy legs; feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: I am a 71-year-old woman and came to the emergency department with my spouse because I suddenly became short of breath about 45 minutes ago while sitting after work. My heart has been racing, and I felt dizzy enough that I had to hold onto the counter and nearly passed out. There is a tight sensation across my chest, along with a low-grade feverish feeling and heaviness in both legs. I work as a mechanic and was on my feet earlier today, but I do not recall an injury or unusual exertion. I have high blood pressure. For several months, my ankles and lower legs have tended to swell by evening, usually improving overnight. I have not had this combination of symptoms before.

Symptoms: dyspnea; tachycardia; dizziness with near-syncope; cough; leg heaviness; lightheadedness
Case_History_Text: EMS brings an 80-year-old man to the emergency department after his coworker called for help at work. He is a retired nurse with obesity and reports worsening shortness of breath over the past day. He felt lightheaded while standing and nearly fainted, with a rapid heartbeat noted by responders. He describes a recent respiratory infection; his cough was initially dry but has become mildly productive. He says both legs feel heavy and that he has needed two pillows to sleep recently. On arrival he is alert, speaking in short sentences, and remains tachycardic, without reported chest discomfort.

Symptoms: dyspnea; tachycardia; dizziness; near-syncope; lightheadedness; leg heaviness
Case_History_Text: A 64-year-old woman presents to the emergency department alone for shortness of breath that began last night and has persisted into today. She describes the breathing difficulty as a feeling that she cannot get a satisfying breath, occurring with walking through her home and intermittently while sitting. She became lightheaded while standing at the kitchen counter this morning and briefly felt as though she might pass out, though she did not lose consciousness or fall. She reports a racing heartbeat during these episodes. Both legs have felt unusually heavy since yesterday, without a clearly localized area of pain. She denies fever, productive cough, wheezing, or recent illness and is unsure whether she has noticed any swelling. She has seasonal allergies but says this feels different from her usual symptoms. She works as a retail manager and has remained active at work until yesterday. She reports no known prior heart or lung condition and arrived without family or friends.

Symptoms: Shortness of breath; racing heartbeat; dizziness and near-fainting; intermittent wheezing; heavy legs; sweating
Case_History_Text: I’m 67 and use they/them pronouns. Since yesterday evening, I’ve had episodes where I suddenly can’t catch my breath and my heart starts racing. I get dizzy and feel as if I might pass out, especially when I stand or walk. My legs have felt unusually heavy, and I’ve been sweating during the spells. A family member noticed a wheezing sound when I was breathing, though I mostly notice tightness and rapid breathing. The episodes ease somewhat and then return. EMS was called after I nearly collapsed at home, and my neighbor came with me to the emergency department. I smoked for many years, although I no longer smoke regularly. I also have seasonal allergies. I’m currently taking college classes, which has been difficult with these symptoms.

Symptoms: dyspnea; tachycardia; dizziness/near-syncope; leg heaviness; productive cough; wheezing; feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: 85-year-old woman, retired nurse, arrived alone to the ED for shortness of breath that began earlier today and has persisted. Reports a racing heartbeat with intermittent dizziness and one near-fainting episode while walking. Both legs feel heavy. She has had a productive cough and says she has felt mildly feverish; a family member noticed wheezing before she left home. She normally sleeps on two pillows. History includes hypertension with recent poor control. Denies recent injury. Appears anxious but is able to speak in short complete sentences.

Symptoms: shortness of breath; rapid heartbeat; dizziness; near-fainting; dry cough; heavy legs
Case_History_Text: I am the patient’s daughter and came to the emergency department after EMS brought him in. He is a 57-year-old farmer who had been working around the property earlier today when, about two hours ago, he suddenly became short of breath and complained that his heart was racing. He felt lightheaded while standing and had to sit down because he thought he might pass out. He has also mentioned a dry cough and that both legs feel unusually heavy. He arrived without family because I was away when EMS was called. He has seasonal allergies but no other recent concerns that I know of. He has not described fever, vomiting, or a recent injury.

Symptoms: shortness of breath; rapid heartbeat; dizziness with near-fainting; chest tightness; dry cough; heavy-feeling legs
Case_History_Text: Hello, I’m a 56-year-old woman and I came to the emergency department with my coworker because I have felt increasingly short of breath for about six hours. My heart feels like it is racing, and twice I became dizzy enough that I thought I might pass out, though I did not lose consciousness. I also have mild chest tightness, a dry cough, and both legs feel unusually heavy. I had what seemed like a respiratory infection a couple of weeks ago, with congestion and fatigue, but had started feeling better. I have smoked for many years. I drive for a rideshare service and have been sitting more than usual lately. I have no known heart or lung diagnosis and take no daily medicines.

Symptoms: dyspnea; tachycardia; dizziness; near-syncope; cough; intermittent productive cough; sweating; wheezing; seasonal allergies
Case_History_Text: EMS handoff: We were called for a 65-year-old man with three hours of worsening shortness of breath. He was found sitting upright at home, pale and sweaty, reporting lightheadedness and feeling as though he might pass out but no loss of consciousness. His daughter noticed wheezing and says he had been coughing, occasionally bringing up clear sputum; he describes the cough as mostly dry during transport. He denies known chest injury. He is an obese office administrator who arrived alone after family contacted EMS. History includes seasonal allergies, and he reports a relative previously had a blood clot. Heart rate remained elevated en route; he was able to speak in full sentences.

Symptoms: dyspnea; tachycardia; dizziness; near-syncope; productive cough; sweating
Case_History_Text: An 84-year-old woman was brought to the emergency department by a coworker after developing sudden worsening shortness of breath approximately 45 minutes earlier while helping a client transfer from bed to a chair. She became aware of a rapid heartbeat, felt lightheaded, and had to sit down because she thought she might faint, though she did not lose consciousness or fall. Her coworker reports that she appeared sweaty and pale and was breathing quickly. The patient describes a cough producing a small amount of clear-to-yellow sputum, without coughing blood. She denies chest pain but reports a sense of chest tightness and difficulty taking a full breath. She has noticed slightly more fatigue with routine activity over the past several days but had continued working. She denies recent fever, vomiting, or known sick contacts. Her history is notable for seasonal allergies; she takes an over-the-counter allergy medicine as needed. She works as a home health aide and arrived still wearing her work badge.

Symptoms: Palpitations; tachycardia; lightheadedness; fatigue; sweating

Symptoms: headache; visual change; tingling in one arm and hand; difficulty finding words; dizziness; sensitivity to light; low feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: I am a 42-year-old man and work as a graphic designer. I have had occasional headaches before, and my brother has migraines. My only regular medication is an oral contraceptive prescribed as part of a prior hormone regimen.

Symptoms: headache; shimmering visual change; limb tingling; brief word-finding difficulty; dizziness; stiff, sore neck; feverish feeling
Case_History_Text: Triage: 23-year-old woman, farmer, brought to ED by coworker for sudden headache over the past 45 min with shimmering visual changes, tingling in one limb, dizziness, and difficulty finding words for about 1 min. Family history includes headaches in a parent and migraines in a sibling. No further history obtained at triage; symptoms ongoing but fluctuating.

Symptoms: Headache; visual change; tingling in one arm and hand; brief trouble finding words; dizziness; low feverish feeling; recent viral illness
Case_History_Text: I brought my 58-year-old brother to the emergency department after EMS was called to our apartment. He became dizzy while standing and, for about a minute, struggled to find the words he wanted, though he seemed to understand me. The speech problem improved before EMS arrived, but he still felt unsteady and complained that his head hurt. He also described feeling mildly feverish, although we did not check his temperature at home. He came alone in the ambulance, and I met him here.

Symptoms: headache; visual change; tingling in an arm and hand; speech difficulty; dizziness; light sensitivity; vomiting; stiff, sore neck

She was independent before this started, but she is frightened and feels the symptoms have not fully gone away.

Symptoms: headache; visual shimmering; intermittent visual change; limb tingling; brief trouble finding words; dizziness; stiff, sore neck; vomiting once
Case_History_Text: EMS brought a 42-year-old man to the emergency department after his adult daughter called for help. Symptoms: headache; visual shimmering; visual change; limb tingling; speech difficulty; dizziness; stiff, sore neck

She feels dizzy when standing and reports that her neck has been stiff and sore since yesterday. Her spouse says she seemed quieter than usual during the drive but has remained responsive and has not appeared confused. She denies a recent fall or other head injury. Her medical history includes an irregular heart rhythm treated with a daily anticoagulant; she reports taking it as prescribed. No similar episode has required emergency care. She arrives alert, accompanied by her spouse, and asks for relief of the headache and nausea.

Symptoms: progressive headache; nausea; sensitivity to light; visual shimmering; recent subtle personality change
Case_History_Text: I’m 71 and work as an accountant. Since yesterday morning, I’ve had a headache that started mildly but has steadily become more intense. My wife says I have seemed unusually impatient and forgetful over the past couple of weeks, but I had not really noticed it. She became concerned when I stayed in bed today and called EMS. I take a prescribed blood thinner for an ongoing circulation problem and brought my medication list. My wife came with me to the emergency department.

Symptoms: progressive headache; nausea; one episode of vomiting; stiff, sore neck; subjective low fever; recent viral illness

Symptoms: progressive intermittent headache since yesterday evening; nausea; one-minute episode of trouble finding words; worsening discomfort today
Case_History_Text: I brought my 51-year-old husband to the emergency department after his coworker called EMS from the welding shop. He has no known recent head injury.

Symptoms: progressive headache; nausea; one episode of vomiting; low feverish feeling; brief trouble finding words; anticoagulant use; smoking history
Case_History_Text: Hello, I’m writing from the emergency department with my neighbor, who brought me in because this headache has steadily worsened through most of today. Earlier, for about a minute, I knew what I wanted to say but could not find the words; that has resolved. I work as a nurse and usually push through headaches, but this feels different and is not easing with rest. I take a prescribed blood thinner for a separate condition and smoke several cigarettes daily. I have not had a recent injury.

Symptoms: progressive headache; nausea; one episode of vomiting; visual shimmering; brief trouble finding words; photophobia
Case_History_Text: EMS brings a 69-year-old man from home to the emergency department after his spouse called for worsening head pain over approximately two hours. Symptoms: progressive headache; nausea; photophobia; head pressure; reduced appetite
Case_History_Text: A 62-year-old woman presents to the emergency department accompanied by her adult daughter for evaluation of a progressively worsening headache that became substantially more intense over approximately six hours. She describes a steady pressure across the forehead and temples, with occasional throbbing, and says bright lights aggravate it. Nausea began soon after the headache intensified, although she has not vomited. She reports feeling tired and has had little appetite today. Her daughter states that the patient has been quieter than usual but remains conversant and recognizes family members. The patient denies recent head injury, fever, neck stiffness, fainting, or new difficulty speaking, walking, or using either arm or leg. She has a history of high blood pressure and takes a daily medication, though she is unsure whether she took it this morning. She works as a construction foreman and had continued routine duties until the headache forced her to stop.

Symptoms: progressive headache; nausea; light sensitivity; feverish feeling; morning headaches
Case_History_Text: I’m 62 and work as a postal worker. My wife came with me after she called EMS because the headache became much worse over the last three hours. It started as a pressure behind my forehead and has gradually intensified, with nausea and no appetite. Bright lights are bothering me, and I feel slightly feverish, although I have not checked my temperature. I’ve noticed milder headaches most mornings for several weeks, but this one is different because it has kept building instead of easing. I smoke several cigarettes a day. I have not had a recent head injury. I was worried when the pain became difficult to ignore, so I asked my wife to stay with me while we came to the emergency department.

Symptoms: progressive headache; nausea; vomiting x1; photophobia; dizziness
Case_History_Text: 37-year-old woman, graphic designer, arrives to ED with spouse for headache worsening over the past 45 min. Reports gradual pressure-like pain, now severe, with light sensitivity, nausea, one episode of emesis, and dizziness. States she has occasional headaches but this episode is more persistent than usual. Recent viral illness reported. Takes a prescribed anticoagulant for a prior clotting problem; denies missed doses. No recent fall or head injury reported. Awake, conversant, and uncomfortable at triage.

Symptoms: progressive headache over one day; nausea; one episode of vomiting; brief trouble finding words
Case_History_Text: I am his sister, and I brought him to the emergency department after calling EMS when his headache kept worsening through the day. About an hour before we left, he paused during a conversation and could not find a familiar word for roughly a minute, then returned to speaking normally. He seemed frightened and more tired than usual but did not faint or report a fall. He takes an anticoagulant for a longstanding circulation problem. EMS had initially found him alone at home, and I met him there before accompanying him in.

Symptoms: progressive headache since last night; nausea; visual shimmering; brief trouble finding words; morning headaches; subtle personality change noted by spouse

I have no recent head injury and would like to be evaluated.

The patient takes a prescribed anticoagulant for a prior medical condition and reports no recent medication changes or missed doses. She has no known history of a brain mass. Further symptom review is limited by her discomfort.

Symptoms: progressively worsening headache for 6 hours; nausea; one episode of vomiting; brief word-finding difficulty; shimmering vision; subjective feverish feeling

Symptoms: progressively worsening headache over three hours; nausea; intermittent visual shimmering; dizziness
Case_History_Text: I brought my 66-year-old uncle to the emergency department after his neighbor called EMS when his headache kept getting worse this afternoon.
