Symptoms: progressive headache; nausea; sensitivity to light; visual shimmering

I am worried because this feels progressively worse and would appreciate an assessment.

Symptoms: progressive headache; nausea; stiff, sore neck; low feverish feeling; visual shimmering; dizziness; recurrent morning headaches

His neighbor says he appeared uncomfortable but has not fainted or had convulsive activity. He smokes and takes a prescribed blood thinner for another medical condition. Case_History_Text: A 57-year-old woman presents to the emergency department alone with a progressively worsening headache that began approximately 45 minutes ago while she was finishing a security shift. She has experienced occasional headaches in the past, usually less severe and more familiar in character, and has not previously sought emergency care for them. She takes no newly started medications and reports no recent illness or unusual exertion. On arrival, she is awake, able to provide a clear history, and appears uncomfortable. Her coworker offered to drive her, but she preferred to come in alone.

Symptoms: Headache; feverish feeling; photophobia; visual shimmering; abrupt worsening over 45 minutes
Case_History_Text: A 44-year-old woman was brought to the emergency department by her adult daughter for a headache that became markedly more uncomfortable over the past 45 minutes. She describes a steady pressure across her forehead and behind both eyes, with intermittent shimmering in her vision when looking at bright surfaces. She feels feverish and reports sensitivity to light, keeping her eyes partly closed during conversation. She has not vomited and denies recent head injury. She is unsure whether the discomfort worsens with movement and cannot clearly describe any neck limitation, stating that she has mainly been trying to remain still because the light bothers her. Her daughter says the patient seemed well earlier while preparing for a shift as a restaurant cook, then called her home because the headache intensified. She reports cigarette use but no other significant medical history is volunteered. She has taken no medication for this episode and has not noticed a rash, fainting, or weakness.

Symptoms: Headache; feverish feeling; photophobia; dizziness; fatigue; occasional headaches
Case_History_Text: I’m 31 and work nights as a security guard. Since yesterday, I’ve had a headache that gradually became stronger, along with a feverish feeling and chills. Light bothers me, so I’ve been keeping the room dim, and I feel dizzy when I stand or walk. I’ve been more tired than usual and had little appetite, but I have not vomited. I get occasional headaches, though this feels more persistent than normal. I take an anticoagulant for another medical reason and have not missed a dose. I was at home alone today when I felt worse, so someone called EMS. I came to the emergency department alone. My neck does not feel especially stiff, but moving around makes the headache more noticeable.

Symptoms: headache; feverish feeling; photophobia; one episode of vomiting; stiff, sore neck; brief trouble finding words
Case_History_Text: 19-year-old woman, retail manager, presents to ED with coworker for headache beginning last night. Reports feeling feverish, light-sensitive, and vomited once this morning. Describes her neck as stiff and sore but can move it; denies known injury. Had approximately one minute of trouble finding words earlier today, now resolved. Smokes cigarettes. College roommate has recently had a viral illness. No prior personal history of similar episodes; sibling has migraines. Alert and answering questions appropriately at triage. Symptoms have persisted despite rest and fluids.

Symptoms: Headache; feverish feeling; photophobia; intermittent visual shimmering; symptoms on and off since yesterday evening
Case_History_Text: I brought my 33-year-old son to the emergency department after calling EMS because his headache became more intense this morning. He is a farmer and had been doing routine work yesterday, but by evening he said he felt feverish and wanted the lights turned down. Since then, the pain has come and gone, with brief episodes of shimmering in his vision. He has been resting more than usual and says bright light makes the headache worse. He has not mentioned any recent injury, and I have not noticed him struggling to move his neck, though he is clearly uncomfortable. He has no known major medical problems. His sister has migraines, but he has never had headaches quite like this. I stayed with him during the ride to the ED.

Symptoms: Headache; fever; sensitivity to light; visual shimmering; sore, somewhat stiff neck; fatigue; nausea
Case_History_Text: Hi, I’m writing about my 16-year-old coworker, who came to the emergency department with me because she has felt suddenly unwell for most of today. She developed a worsening headache with fever and says bright lights are difficult to tolerate. She has noticed shimmering around objects and feels tired and mildly nauseated. Her neck is sore and feels somewhat stiff, though she can move it and does not describe a clear injury. She has been drinking small amounts but has little appetite. She smokes occasionally. Her only regular medicine is an anticoagulant prescribed for another condition, with no recent dose changes. She is unemployed at present, and I am accompanying her as a former coworker and friend.

Symptoms: headache; feverish feeling; photophobia; vomiting once; dizziness; visual shimmering
Case_History_Text: EMS brings a 36-year-old man to the emergency department after his neighbor called for help. He reports approximately two hours of worsening headache with light sensitivity, dizziness, and shimmering in his vision. He vomited once before arrival and says he has felt feverish, though he did not measure his temperature. He is awake and answering questions appropriately, but appears uncomfortable and prefers the room dim. He denies a recent injury. His history includes high blood pressure, cigarette smoking, and prescribed anticoagulant use for another condition. The neighbor accompanies him and provides additional reassurance about the timeline.

Symptoms: headache; fever; photophobia; nausea; dizziness
Case_History_Text: A 34-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by a neighbor for approximately six hours of worsening headache and fever. She describes the pain as diffuse and throbbing, with intermittent waves of nausea and a sense that the room is moving when she stands or turns quickly. Bright lights markedly increase her discomfort, so she has been keeping her eyes closed during the ride. She reports feeling chilled earlier but has not measured her temperature at home. She denies vomiting, diarrhea, cough, congestion, chest discomfort, shortness of breath, recent injury, or known sick contacts. Her neck feels generally sore, though she does not describe definite stiffness and says she can turn her head. She has had no fainting, confusion, focal weakness, numbness, or trouble speaking. She works as a postal worker and continued her route earlier today before leaving because of the symptoms. She smokes cigarettes and reports no regular medications or significant prior medical history. Her neighbor notes that she has been tired but answering questions appropriately.

Symptoms: Headache; fever; photophobia; shimmering vision; mildly stiff, sore neck; recent sick contacts
Case_History_Text: I am 27 and work as a bus driver. About three hours ago, while I was at home, I developed a strong headache and started feeling feverish. Light bothers my eyes, and I have noticed shimmering around objects when I look at them. My neck feels sore and somewhat stiff, but I can still move it. My adult daughter called EMS and came with me to the emergency department. I have not had this kind of headache before. Several people I know, including someone in my household, recently had a sore throat. I take a prescribed anticoagulant for a separate medical reason and have not missed a dose. I feel tired and uncomfortable but have not fainted or had trouble speaking.

Symptoms: Headache; fever; photophobia; nausea; brief trouble finding words; stiff, sore neck
Case_History_Text: 35-year-old woman, graphic designer, arrived to ED with spouse for sudden worsening headache over the past 45 min, with reported fever, nausea, and marked sensitivity to light. Spouse noticed she had trouble finding words for about 1 min, now resolved. Pt describes her neck as stiff and sore but denies a clear injury. Takes an anticoagulant for a chronic non-cardiac condition. Several household contacts recently had sore throats. Reports sibling history of migraines; no personal migraine history documented. Awake and answering questions at triage.

Symptoms: headache; fever; photophobia; nausea; fatigue; reduced appetite
Case_History_Text: I am his older sister, and I came to the emergency department after EMS brought him in alone. He is a 30-year-old farmer who had been working normally yesterday morning but began complaining of a steadily worsening headache by afternoon. Overnight he developed a fever, nausea, and marked sensitivity to light, so he stayed in a dark room and drank very little. This morning he seemed exhausted and said the headache was unlike his usual occasional headaches. He has not mentioned any recent injury, rash, vomiting, or unusual exposures that I know of. He takes a prescribed anticoagulant for a longstanding blood-clot problem and otherwise has been fairly healthy. He was awake and answering questions when EMS left him, though he appeared uncomfortable and wanted the lights turned off.

Symptoms: headache; fever; sensitivity to light; visual shimmering; dizziness
Case_History_Text: Hello, I’m a 29-year-old mechanic and came to the emergency department with my neighbor because I have felt increasingly unwell since last night. I developed a fever and a strong, steady headache that makes it difficult to concentrate. Bright lights are uncomfortable, and I have noticed brief shimmering in my vision when I look around or stand up. I also feel dizzy and tired, with less appetite than usual. My college roommate has been home with what sounds like a viral illness this week. My sibling gets migraines, although I have never had this combination of symptoms before. I have not taken anything besides water and one dose of acetaminophen, and I’m worried because the headache and fever have continued.

Symptoms: headache; fever; photophobia; intermittent vomiting; visual shimmering; dizziness; stiff, sore neck
Case_History_Text: EMS brings a 27-year-old man to the emergency department with his spouse after being called for worsening episodes of headache and fever that began yesterday evening. He is a high school coach and reports light sensitivity, brief shimmering in his vision, dizziness, and one episode of vomiting. He describes his neck as stiff and sore but is able to move it, though movement increases discomfort. His spouse says he has had occasional headaches before but this episode seems different. He has a history of high blood pressure, and several recent contacts had sore throats. He is awake and answering questions appropriately.

Symptoms: headache; fever; photophobia; visual shimmering; vomiting once
Case_History_Text: A 32-year-old woman, a college student, presents to the emergency department with a coworker for headache and fever that began earlier today. She describes the headache as gradually increasing over several hours, with pressure across her forehead and behind both eyes. Bright lights worsen the discomfort, and she noticed intermittent shimmering in her peripheral vision while walking across campus. She vomited once this afternoon but has been able to sip water since then. She reports feeling unusually warm, chilled, tired, and generally unwell. Several classmates and coworkers have recently had sore throats, though she is not sure whether any were formally evaluated. She denies recent head injury and says she has not had similar symptoms recently. Her coworker reports that she was speaking normally and walking without assistance before arrival. She is concerned because the headache feels more intense than her usual headaches. No additional history is available at the time of triage.

Symptoms: headache; feverish feeling; photophobia; sore, somewhat stiff neck; one episode of vomiting
Case_History_Text: I’m 36 and work as a pharmacist. About two hours ago, while finishing my shift, I developed a strong headache that came on fairly quickly and became worse under the bright lights. I felt hot and chilled at the same time, though I have not checked my temperature. My neck feels sore and a little stiff when I turn it, but I can still move it. I vomited once before EMS arrived. A coworker called EMS because I looked pale and was covering my eyes. I’ve had occasional headaches before, but this feels more intense than usual. Several people around me recently had sore throats. I came to the emergency department with my coworker and feel tired and uncomfortable.

Symptoms: headache; feverish feeling; photophobia; nausea; dizziness
Case_History_Text: 24-year-old woman, accountant, presents to ED with her neighbor for approx. 6 hrs of worsening diffuse headache and feeling feverish. Reports marked sensitivity to light, nausea without vomiting, and intermittent dizziness. No reported neck stiffness; movement is uncomfortable but she remains able to turn her head. Several coworkers and a roommate recently had sore throats. Smokes cigarettes. Takes an anticoagulant for a pre-existing condition; medication and timing to be verified. No known recent injury reported. Appears uncomfortable in triage but awake and answering appropriately. Neighbor says symptoms began during the afternoon and progressed over the evening.

Symptoms: Headache; fever; sensitivity to light; brief trouble finding words; recent viral illness
Case_History_Text: I brought my coworker to the emergency department after EMS was called from the farm. He is 35 and had been recovering from what seemed like a viral illness over the past few days, with fatigue and a sore throat. About three hours ago, he developed a worsening headache and felt hot, then became very uncomfortable under the bright lights in the equipment shed. For roughly a minute, he struggled to find the words he wanted, though his speech returned to normal before EMS arrived. He has been tired and quieter than usual but is answering me appropriately. He has not mentioned an injury, vomiting, or a stiff neck. I am worried because the headache and fever came on more strongly this afternoon.

Symptoms: headache; feverish feeling; photophobia; nausea; one episode of vomiting
Case_History_Text: Hello, I’m writing about my mother, a 39-year-old woman who came to the emergency department with me today. She works as a welder and was feeling generally unwell, warm, and slightly nauseated before developing a headache over the past 45 minutes. Bright lights are bothering her, and she vomited once on the way here. She describes the headache as steady and unusual for her, but she has not reported any injury. Her medical history includes high blood pressure, and she smokes cigarettes. She has not mentioned other new symptoms, and I do not know of any recent medication changes. She is awake and answering questions, though she looks uncomfortable and wants the lights dimmed.

Symptoms: headache; fever; photophobia; visual shimmering; brief trouble finding words; sore neck
Case_History_Text: EMS handoff: We brought a 25-year-old unemployed man from his apartment after his coworker called 911. He reports about one day of fever and a worsening headache with sensitivity to light. He noticed shimmering in his vision and had approximately one minute of trouble finding words, which resolved before our arrival. He describes his neck as sore and somewhat stiff but can move it. He had a viral illness recently. Past history includes high blood pressure; he reports that a sibling has migraines. He remained awake and conversational during transport, with no reported injury or substance use.

Symptoms: Headache; fever; photophobia; one episode of vomiting; visual shimmering; recent exposure to coworkers with sore throat
Case_History_Text: An 18-year-old woman who works as a retail manager presents to the emergency department with a coworker for headache and fever that began last night. She describes a gradually worsening, diffuse pressure with intermittent throbbing, accompanied by sensitivity to overhead lights and brief episodes of shimmering in her vision. She vomited once early this morning but has been able to sip fluids since then. She reports feeling chilled and unusually tired, though she has remained alert and able to walk without assistance. Several coworkers and a household contact have recently complained of sore throat symptoms. She denies recent head injury, new medications, recreational drug use, or known chronic medical conditions. She is unsure whether turning or flexing her neck changes the headache and does not volunteer marked neck discomfort. Her coworker says she seemed quieter than usual today but has been answering questions appropriately. She has not noticed a rash, weakness, numbness, or difficulty speaking.

Symptoms: headache; feverish feeling; photophobia; stiff, sore neck; vomiting once; fatigue
Case_History_Text: I’m 38 and nonbinary, and I work as an accountant. Since yesterday evening, I’ve had a headache that comes and goes, with a low feverish feeling and a strong dislike of bright light. My neck feels stiff and sore, although I can still move it. I vomited once earlier today and have felt washed out since then. A few people I was around recently had sore throats, and I had what seemed like a mild viral illness last week. The headache became more bothersome this afternoon, so my neighbor called EMS and came with me to the emergency department. I haven’t had anything like this recently, and I’m worried because the light makes the pain worse.

Symptoms: headache; feverish feeling; photophobia; dizziness; sore, somewhat stiff neck; fatigue
Case_History_Text: 43-year-old woman, home health aide, brought to ED by spouse for headache beginning earlier today and gradually worsening. Reports feeling feverish, dizzy, and unusually sensitive to light. Neck feels sore and somewhat stiff, though she can move it. Denies known injury. Has occasional headaches; sister has migraines. Smokes cigarettes. No recent travel or sick contacts reported. Awake and answering appropriately at triage, appears uncomfortable in bright light. Spouse says she has been resting more than usual but has had no witnessed confusion or fainting. Further evaluation pending.

Symptoms: headache; fever; sensitivity to light; visual shimmering; malaise
Case_History_Text: I brought my 25-year-old son to the emergency department after his adult daughter called EMS because he suddenly became much worse this afternoon. He had seemed tired earlier, but over about two hours he developed a strong, constant headache and said the room felt painfully bright. He kept covering his eyes and described shimmering patterns in his vision, even when they were closed. He felt hot to me and complained of chills and general achiness. He has not mentioned any recent injury, and he has been eating and drinking less than usual today. He smokes cigarettes but has no known ongoing medical problems that I am aware of. He is awake and answering questions, although he seems uncomfortable and wants to lie still in the dimmest area.

Symptoms: headache; feverish feeling; photophobia; visual shimmering; dizziness; occasional prior headaches; high blood pressure
Case_History_Text: Hello, I’m a 29-year-old woman and I came to the emergency department with my neighbor because of a headache that began about six hours ago. It has gradually become intense, and ordinary lights make it worse, so I have been keeping my eyes partly closed. I have also noticed shimmering in my vision and feel dizzy when I stand or walk. I feel feverish, though I have not measured my temperature at home. I have had occasional headaches before, but this feels more persistent than usual. I work as a mechanic and was unable to finish my shift. I have a history of high blood pressure. I can move my neck, but I feel generally unwell and would like to be evaluated.

Symptoms: headache; feverish feeling; photophobia; visual shimmering; one episode of vomiting; malaise
Case_History_Text: EMS brings a 36-year-old man to the emergency department after a neighbor called for assistance. He reports that a diffuse headache began about three hours ago and has steadily worsened, with a low feverish feeling, sensitivity to light, and shimmering in his vision. He vomited once before EMS arrival and says he feels generally unwell. He is unemployed and lives alone nearby; a college roommate from years ago recently told him about a viral illness. He smokes cigarettes and reports that his sibling has migraines. He arrived awake and answering questions appropriately, accompanied by his neighbor.

Symptoms: headache; fever; photophobia; nausea; sore, mildly stiff neck
Case_History_Text: A 35-year-old woman presents alone to the emergency department with a headache and fever that began approximately 45 minutes ago while she was finishing a bus route. She describes the pain as diffuse and steadily worsening, with sensitivity to overhead lights and mild nausea but no vomiting. She reports that her neck feels sore and somewhat stiff, although she can turn her head and denies a sudden loss of movement. She has not noticed a rash, weakness, numbness, confusion, fainting, or difficulty speaking. She reports feeling chilled earlier and says she has had less appetite today, but provides no clear preceding illness. She has been working her usual schedule and denies recent travel or known sick contacts. Her medical history includes high blood pressure; she is unsure whether she took her usual medication this morning. She arrived walking independently and is answering questions appropriately.

Symptoms: dizziness; vertigo; nausea; imbalance; blurred vision; fatigue
Case_History_Text: A 46-year-old woman was brought to the emergency department by a neighbor for sudden-onset dizziness that began approximately 45 minutes before arrival. She describes a spinning sensation that becomes more noticeable when she turns her head or attempts to sit or stand. Since the onset, she has felt unsteady and has needed her neighbor’s support while walking. She reports nausea without vomiting and intermittent blurred vision, which she says is difficult to characterize because of the spinning sensation. She denies chest discomfort, shortness of breath, headache, recent fainting, or known injury. She feels unusually fatigued but remained awake and able to answer questions throughout the episode. She works as a rideshare driver and had been preparing to leave for an afternoon shift when symptoms began. Her neighbor reports no similar prior episode. Her medical history includes diabetes; she reports taking her usual medications and denies recent illness or medication changes.

Symptoms: Dizziness; vertigo; nausea; imbalance; blurred vision; trouble keeping balance
Case_History_Text: I’m a 64-year-old security guard, and this started yesterday while I was getting ready for work. The room suddenly felt like it was spinning, and I became nauseated. Since then, I’ve had waves of dizziness and my vision has seemed blurry at times. I’m having trouble keeping my balance and needed to hold onto the walls when walking. I’ve had a couple of shorter spells like this in the past, but they went away on their own. I have high blood pressure and take medicine for it. My neighbor noticed I was unsteady this morning and called EMS. They brought me to the emergency department, and my neighbor came along. I have not had chest pain or trouble breathing.

Symptoms: dizziness; vertigo; nausea; imbalance; headache; blurred vision
Case_History_Text: 74-year-old woman, works as a janitor, presents to ED alone for dizziness and room-spinning vertigo beginning last night. Reports nausea, intermittent headache, blurred vision, and trouble keeping her balance while walking. Denies recent injury. Symptoms have persisted into today and prompted her to leave work early. PMH includes diabetes and hypertension; states her father had atrial fibrillation. No medication list available at triage. Awake and answering questions, but appears uncomfortable and requests assistance when standing.

Symptoms: Dizziness; vertigo; nausea; imbalance; intermittent blurred vision
Case_History_Text: I brought my 68-year-old husband to the emergency department after calling EMS this morning. He works as a janitor and was unable to walk steadily across our kitchen when another spell began. Since yesterday evening, he has had episodes of dizziness and a spinning sensation that come and go, accompanied by nausea and occasional blurred vision. He says the room seems to move when he turns his head or gets up, and he has needed to hold onto furniture. He had a few milder spells like this several months ago that resolved on their own. Between episodes he seems more comfortable, but today he remains unsteady and worried. He has not complained of chest discomfort or headache, and I have not noticed any fainting.

Symptoms: Dizziness; vertigo; nausea; imbalance; fatigue; intermittent numbness in one arm; difficulty keeping balance
Case_History_Text: Hello, I’m writing from the emergency department with my coworker beside me. Since late this morning, I’ve had episodes of intense dizziness and a spinning sensation, along with nausea and feeling unusually fatigued. I’m having trouble walking in a straight line and need to hold onto nearby furniture or my coworker’s arm to keep my balance. I also noticed intermittent numbness in my right arm, which has made me more worried. I’ve had a few shorter spells of dizziness in the past, but today’s symptoms have lasted most of the day and feel more disruptive. I’m a 51-year-old software engineer with diabetes and no recent injury. Please let me know what information you need.

Symptoms: dizziness; vertigo; nausea; imbalance; blurred vision; transient slurred speech; headache; right arm numbness
Case_History_Text: EMS handoff: This is a 52-year-old man, a postal worker, brought in with his adult daughter after we were called for sudden dizziness and a spinning sensation that began about two hours ago. He reports nausea and difficulty walking without support, with intermittent blurred vision. His daughter noticed several minutes of slurred speech, now resolved; he also describes a headache and numbness in his right arm that has improved. He recalls having a few shorter spells like this in the past. History includes diabetes, and he has slept poorly for several nights. No reported fall or loss of consciousness.

Symptoms: dizziness; vertigo; nausea; imbalance; headache; brief slurred speech
Case_History_Text: A 67-year-old woman was brought to the emergency department by her spouse after developing sudden dizziness approximately six hours earlier while preparing for work. She describes a persistent sensation that the room is spinning, worsened by turning her head or attempting to stand. She has felt unsteady and has needed her spouse’s arm to walk. Nausea began soon after the dizziness, though she has not vomited. She also reports a mild pressure-like headache that developed during the episode. According to her spouse, her speech sounded slurred for several minutes near the onset, then returned to normal before arrival. She denies chest discomfort, shortness of breath, fainting, or recent head injury. She has noticed no hearing change or ear pain. Her medical history includes high blood pressure, and she takes a daily medication but is unsure of its name. She works as an office administrator and was independent with daily activities before this event.

Symptoms: Dizziness; spinning vertigo; nausea; imbalance; blurred vision; trouble keeping balance
Case_History_Text: I am 59 and work as a mechanic. About three hours ago, while I was at home getting ready for work, the room suddenly started spinning. I felt nauseated but have not vomited. Since then, I have had trouble keeping my balance and needed my spouse to help me walk. My vision has seemed blurry at times, especially when I try to look around. The spinning gets worse when I move, though I still feel unsteady when sitting still. My spouse called EMS because I was afraid of falling, and they brought me to the emergency department. I have diabetes and have smoked for many years. I have not had an episode this intense before.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute posterior circulation ischemic stroke (cerebellar infarction)

Symptoms: Dizziness; room-spinning vertigo; nausea; imbalance; fatigue; transient slurred speech; blurred vision; headache
Case_History_Text: 51-year-old woman, janitor, presents alone to ED for sudden dizziness and room-spinning vertigo beginning 45 min ago while preparing for work. Reports nausea, marked imbalance, fatigue, blurred vision, and a headache. States speech sounded slurred for several minutes, now improved. Denies recent injury. History includes diabetes and high blood pressure. Reports sleeping poorly for several nights. Appears worried and requests assistance when walking. No home medication list available at triage.

Symptoms: dizziness; room-spinning vertigo; nausea; imbalance; brief slurred speech; headache
Case_History_Text: I am his daughter, and I called EMS after my 59-year-old father became suddenly dizzy yesterday afternoon. He described the room spinning and had trouble walking without holding onto furniture. He felt nauseated but did not vomit. For several minutes, his speech sounded slurred, then returned to normal. He has also complained of a dull headache since the episode began. My father works as an accountant and is usually steady and independent. He has a history of high blood pressure and takes medication, though I am not sure whether he took it today. He arrived at the emergency department by EMS alone while I followed behind and met him there. He remains dizzy, particularly when trying to sit up or walk, and says he feels off balance.

Symptoms: Dizziness; vertigo; nausea; imbalance; brief slurred speech; blurred vision
Case_History_Text: Hello, I am a 75-year-old retired nurse who came to the emergency department alone because I have felt dizzy and unsteady since last night. The room seems to spin when I turn or sit up, and I have been nauseated but have not vomited. For a few minutes this morning, my speech sounded slurred to me, and my vision was blurred; both improved before I arrived. I still feel off balance when walking and am holding onto furniture for support. I slept very little over the past several nights while helping a neighbor, so I initially thought exhaustion might explain this. My parent had atrial fibrillation. I have not had this exact combination of symptoms before.

Symptoms: dizziness; vertigo; nausea; imbalance; blurred vision; headache; trouble keeping balance; brief slurred speech
Case_History_Text: EMS brings a 54-year-old man to the emergency department with his adult daughter after she called for help at home. He reports episodes of dizziness and room-spinning vertigo beginning yesterday evening, occurring on and off with nausea and increasing trouble keeping his balance. He noticed blurred vision and a mild headache during some episodes. His daughter says his speech sounded slurred for several minutes earlier today, then returned to normal before EMS arrival. He works at a daycare and has had several nights of poor sleep. He smokes, and reports that a parent had atrial fibrillation. No recent injury was reported.

Symptoms: dizziness; vertigo; nausea; imbalance; difficulty keeping balance
Case_History_Text: A 49-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with a coworker for dizziness that began earlier today and has persisted for most of the day. She describes a spinning sensation occurring in waves, with nausea and a feeling that the floor is unsteady beneath her. She has needed to hold onto furniture while walking and asked her coworker to accompany her after feeling unsafe traveling home alone. She denies fainting, recent head injury, chest discomfort, shortness of breath, or palpitations. She reports no prior similar episode and is unsure whether the sensation changes with position or movement. She has not noticed hearing loss or ringing in her ears. She denies severe headache, fever, or recent illness. The patient works as an office administrator and was able to communicate clearly during the interview, though she prefers to remain seated because standing worsens her imbalance. Her mother has a history of atrial fibrillation.

Symptoms: dizziness; vertigo; nausea; imbalance; intermittent numbness in one arm; blurred vision; fatigue
Case_History_Text: I am a 49-year-old man and work as a pharmacist. About two hours ago, while getting ready for work, the room suddenly began spinning. I became nauseated and had trouble walking straight, so I sat on the floor and called for help. My spouse stayed with me and EMS brought me to the emergency department. The spinning worsens when I move my head or try to stand, although I still feel unsteady when sitting still. I have also noticed intermittent numbness in my right arm and brief blurred vision. I feel unusually tired. I have smoked for years, and lately I have been sleeping only a few hours a night because of extra shifts. I have not had this exact episode before.

Symptoms: dizziness; vertigo; nausea; imbalance; fatigue; brief slurred speech; headache; blurred vision
Case_History_Text: 75-year-old woman, retired mechanic, brought to ED by neighbor for ~6 hrs of dizziness and room-spinning vertigo with nausea and marked imbalance. Reports fatigue, headache, and intermittent blurred vision. Neighbor noticed slurred speech for several minutes earlier, now resolved. Patient describes prior similar spells but says today feels more persistent. Denies recent injury. History significant for diabetes. Awake and conversational at triage, requesting assistance to stand because she feels unsteady. No medications or food triggers identified. Neighbor remains at bedside.

Symptoms: dizziness; vertigo; nausea; imbalance; fatigue
Case_History_Text: I brought my 41-year-old father to the emergency department after calling EMS because he suddenly became very dizzy about three hours ago. He says the room feels as though it is spinning, especially when he tries to sit up or walk. He has been unsteady on his feet and needed me to hold his arm, but he has not fallen. He feels nauseated and has vomited once. He works as a security guard and had been unusually tired earlier today, though he was able to finish his shift. He has not mentioned chest discomfort or trouble breathing. I am worried because his own parent had atrial fibrillation, although he has never told me that he has it. He arrived with EMS and is still visibly uncomfortable.

Symptoms: dizziness; vertigo; nausea; imbalance; trouble keeping balance; numbness in one arm
Case_History_Text: Hello, I’m writing about my coworker, a 58-year-old woman who needs help in the emergency department. She is a graphic designer and developed sudden dizziness and a spinning sensation about 45 minutes ago while working at her desk. She feels nauseated and says she cannot keep her balance when standing or walking. She also reports numbness in one arm, though she is able to speak with us and answer questions. She recalls having a few shorter spells of dizziness in the past that went away on their own. Her medical history includes diabetes. A coworker brought her in, and she is seated safely while we wait. She has not reported an injury or recent illness.

Symptoms: dizziness; vertigo; nausea; imbalance; intermittent arm numbness; headache; blurred vision
Case_History_Text: EMS bringing a 41-year-old man from his apartment to the emergency department after his coworker called for assistance. He reports about one day of episodic dizziness and a spinning sensation, with nausea and difficulty walking steadily. He also describes a headache, blurred vision, and intermittent numbness in one arm, though he is unsure when each symptom began relative to the others. He works as an office administrator and arrived alone before EMS transport. History includes diabetes and high blood pressure. He reports several nights of poor sleep recently. No injury was reported, and he remained awake and able to answer questions during transport.

Symptoms: dizziness; vertigo; nausea; imbalance; intermittent numbness in the right arm; blurred vision
Case_History_Text: A 72-year-old woman was brought to the emergency department by a neighbor for dizziness and a spinning sensation that began last night. She reports associated nausea and difficulty maintaining her balance while walking, requiring her to hold onto furniture at home. She also noticed intermittent blurred vision and tingling involving the right arm, though she has had difficulty describing the exact timing of these symptoms. She denies fainting, chest pain, shortness of breath, fever, or recent head injury. The symptoms have persisted into today with variable intensity and are worse when she attempts to move about, although she has not identified one consistent trigger. She has not vomited. The patient works as a home health aide and reports several nights of poor sleep while helping cover extra shifts. Her neighbor states that she seemed worried and unsteady this morning but was able to answer questions and walk with assistance. She takes her usual medications and has no known recent illness.

Symptoms: dizziness; vertigo; nausea; imbalance; intermittent one-arm numbness; blurred vision; headache
Case_History_Text: I am a 50-year-old nonbinary nurse, and my spouse brought me to the emergency department after calling EMS. Since yesterday evening, I have had episodes of dizziness and a spinning sensation that come and go. I feel nauseated during the episodes and have trouble walking steadily, so I have been holding onto furniture. At times, my right arm has felt numb, and my vision has seemed blurred. I also have a headache, which is unusual for me but not severe. Between episodes I feel somewhat better, though I do not feel back to normal. I have diabetes and take my prescribed medications. I have not had a recent injury or illness, and I cannot identify a clear trigger.

Symptoms: dizziness; vertigo; nausea; imbalance; fatigue; trouble keeping balance; headache; numbness in one arm
Case_History_Text: 40F postal worker brought to ED by adult daughter for dizziness and room-spinning vertigo present most of today. Reports nausea, fatigue, trouble keeping balance, and needing support while walking. Also notes a headache and intermittent numbness in one arm. Denies known injury. Daughter says pt has slept poorly for several nights due to extra work shifts. PMH includes diabetes; smokes cigarettes. Pt is awake and speaking clearly but appears uncomfortable and cautious with movement. No medications or recent illness documented at triage.

Symptoms: dizziness; vertigo; nausea; imbalance; blurred vision
Case_History_Text: I came to the emergency department with my 69-year-old brother after EMS was called from the community college where he is taking classes. His coworker said he suddenly began feeling dizzy about two hours ago and described the room as spinning. He became unsteady when trying to walk and needed help staying upright. He has also complained of nausea and intermittent blurred vision, but he has not vomited or passed out. He says the symptoms worsen when he turns his head or tries to move. He has diabetes and takes medication for it, though I do not know whether he took today’s dose. He has not mentioned chest discomfort, shortness of breath, headache, fever, or recent injury.

Symptoms: dizziness; vertigo; nausea; imbalance; trouble keeping balance; headache
Case_History_Text: Hello, I am a 78-year-old woman who works as an accountant. About six hours ago, while at work, I developed a strong spinning sensation with nausea. I have had trouble keeping my balance and needed my coworker to walk with me to the emergency department. The dizziness is worse when I move my head or try to stand, and I have a mild headache that began around the same time. I have experienced a few shorter spells like this in the past, but they usually settled more quickly. My mother had atrial fibrillation. I have not fainted, and I am not having chest discomfort or shortness of breath. Please let the team know I still feel unsteady.

Symptoms: dizziness; vertigo; nausea; imbalance; trouble keeping balance; numbness in one arm; blurred vision
Case_History_Text: EMS brings a 73-year-old man from a high school athletic field after a coworker called for help. He reports three hours of sudden dizziness and a spinning sensation with nausea, worsening whenever he tries to stand or walk. He has had trouble keeping his balance and says his vision has seemed blurred. During transport, he also described numbness in one arm, though he was unsure when that began. He is a high school coach with a history of diabetes and smoking. His parent had atrial fibrillation. He remains concerned and mildly uncomfortable but is able to answer questions.

Symptoms: dizziness; vertigo; nausea; imbalance; headache; fatigue
Case_History_Text: A 44-year-old woman was brought to the emergency department by her spouse for approximately 45 minutes of persistent dizziness described as a spinning sensation. She reports that the symptoms began while she was moving around her home and have continued at rest, with worsening when she attempts to walk. She feels markedly off balance and has required her spouse’s support to reach the bathroom. Nausea is present without vomiting. She also notes a mild, diffuse headache and unusual fatigue that began around the same time. She denies chest discomfort, shortness of breath, fever, recent head injury, or loss of consciousness. Her spouse has not noticed confusion, facial asymmetry, or difficulty understanding her, although he says she has been cautious and unsteady when speaking and walking. She has a history of diabetes managed through regular outpatient care. She is unemployed and lives with her spouse. She reports no similar episode of this duration previously.

Symptoms: transient weakness; numbness; confusion; loss of consciousness; headache; fatigue
Case_History_Text: A 50-year-old woman was brought to the emergency department by a neighbor for an episode beginning approximately 45 minutes before arrival. She had been working from home on accounting paperwork when she suddenly complained of a headache and feeling unusually tired. Her neighbor reported that she then became briefly unresponsive while seated, with her head turning slightly to one side and one hand appearing weak. The episode lasted less than two minutes, after which she was awake but confused and repeatedly asked what had happened. She described lingering tingling and heaviness affecting one side of her body, though these symptoms had largely improved by arrival. She denied recent head injury, fever, or substance use. She had no known history of similar events. The neighbor noted that her speech sounded briefly unusual but returned to baseline. She remained fatigued and mildly disoriented during the initial interview. Her mother had atrial fibrillation; the patient herself reported no known heart rhythm disorder.

Symptoms: transient weakness; numbness in one arm; confusion; brief loss of consciousness; blurred vision; slurred speech; poor sleep
Case_History_Text: I’m a 33-year-old man and work as a warehouse supervisor. Over the past day, I’ve had episodes where my vision became blurry, my speech sounded slurred, and one arm felt numb and weak. I also became confused and had trouble following what people were saying. Earlier today, I briefly lost consciousness; my neighbor found me and called EMS. I felt tired and foggy afterward, but the symptoms improved before we arrived. I’ve been sleeping poorly for several nights because of extra shifts and stress. I don’t remember exactly what happened during the episode, and my neighbor noticed I seemed briefly unsteady afterward. My parent has atrial fibrillation. I have not had anything like this before.
Model_Diagnosis: Focal seizure with postictal neurologic deficits

Symptoms: transient weakness; numbness in one arm; confusion; loss of consciousness; blurred vision; nausea; fatigue
Case_History_Text: 18-year-old woman, retail manager, brought to ED by neighbor for episodes since last night. Neighbor reports brief loss of consciousness followed by confusion and fatigue; patient recalls intermittent weakness and numbness affecting one arm, with blurred vision and nausea. Symptoms improved but have recurred briefly, and she feels not fully back to baseline. Reports marked sleep deprivation from several late work shifts and similar spells in the past, never fully evaluated. History of diabetes. No reported injury, fever, or recent illness. Triage note: alert, cooperative, mildly slowed responses, speech understandable; subtle asymmetry of arm strength noted during brief effort.
Model_Diagnosis: Focal-onset seizure with postictal Todd paralysis

Symptoms: Transient weakness; numbness; confusion; brief loss of consciousness; trouble keeping balance; slurred speech; intermittent episodes since yesterday evening
Case_History_Text: I brought my husband to the emergency department after calling EMS this morning. He is 69 and still takes a few college classes, and yesterday evening he suddenly complained that one hand felt numb and seemed unsteady when walking. For several minutes his speech sounded slurred, and he had trouble following our conversation. He then briefly lost consciousness while seated, though he woke up on his own. Since then, he has had several shorter spells of confusion and weakness that seemed to come and go. He has not returned completely to his usual self, especially with his balance. He has diabetes, but was otherwise doing his normal activities before yesterday. I have not noticed a persistent severe headache or recent injury.

Symptoms: transient weakness; numbness; confusion; loss of consciousness; trouble keeping balance; blurred vision; fatigue
Case_History_Text: I’m sending this for my wife, who has had several concerning episodes since late morning. She is 59 and currently attends college while working part-time from home. She first complained that one side felt weak and tingly, then became unsteady and said her vision was blurred. At one point she lost consciousness briefly while seated; afterward she seemed confused and very tired for about 20 minutes. Her strength and speech appeared closer to normal before another shorter spell of numbness and difficulty focusing. She has had trouble keeping her balance most of today. She has high blood pressure and smokes, but no recent injury. We arrived together at the emergency department because the symptoms keep coming and going.

Symptoms: transient weakness; numbness; confusion; loss of consciousness; nausea; fatigue; trouble keeping balance; blurred vision
Case_History_Text: EMS handoff: This is a 39-year-old man, a nurse, brought from home after a coworker called EMS for an episode of confusion followed by loss of consciousness. The event began about two hours ago, with nausea, blurred vision, numbness, and heaviness affecting one side, then difficulty standing and keeping his balance. He gradually became more alert but remains tired and says his thinking feels slowed. He reports poor sleep during several recent shifts, smokes cigarettes, and has had two shorter, similar spells in the past without evaluation. No family member accompanied him, and he arrived alone at the emergency department.

Symptoms: transient weakness; numbness; confusion; loss of consciousness; blurred vision; nausea
Case_History_Text: A 78-year-old retired teacher was brought to the emergency department by her adult daughter approximately six hours after an abrupt episode at home. While preparing tea, she complained that her vision had become blurred and that she felt nauseated, then appeared briefly unresponsive and slumped against the counter. Her daughter noticed diminished movement of one arm and intermittent tingling involving the opposite hand, though she was unable to describe a clear pattern. The episode lasted several minutes, followed by confusion and slowed responses. She gradually returned to her usual conversation but remained tired and had difficulty recalling the event. By arrival, the weakness and numbness had largely resolved, although she reported mild lightheadedness and a vague pressure in her head. The daughter denied any recent injury. The patient has slept poorly for the past several nights while helping a neighbor with morning childcare. She has no known prior similar episode, and both patient and daughter provide somewhat differing timelines.

Symptoms: transient weakness; numbness; confusion; loss of consciousness; blurred vision; nausea; trouble keeping balance
Case_History_Text: I am 66 and work as a graphic designer. About three hours ago, while I was at home reviewing a design, my vision became blurry and I felt nauseated. I remember trying to stand, then losing consciousness. My neighbor says I was unresponsive briefly and seemed confused when I woke up. For a short time, one side felt weak and numb, and I had trouble using my hand, though that has mostly improved. I was unsteady walking and kept asking what had happened. I have had two somewhat similar spells over the past year but never this unsettling. I have diabetes and take medication for it. My neighbor called EMS and came with me to the emergency department. I still feel tired and slightly off balance.

Symptoms: transient weakness; numbness; confusion; brief loss of consciousness; fatigue; blurred vision; trouble keeping balance; several minutes of slurred speech
Case_History_Text: 35F, warehouse supervisor, arrived alone to ED. Reports sudden fatigue followed by blurred vision, tingling and weakness affecting one side, trouble keeping balance, and several minutes of slurred speech. She then briefly lost consciousness; on waking, felt confused and had difficulty recalling the event. Symptoms began about 45 min ago and have mostly improved, though she feels tired and mildly unsteady. Hx high blood pressure and sleep deprivation from several consecutive early shifts. Reports two similar brief spells in the past without a clear explanation. Denies recent injury. Triage note.
Model_Diagnosis: Focal seizure with postictal Todd paralysis

Symptoms: transient weakness; numbness; confusion; loss of consciousness; headache; trouble keeping balance; poor sleep
Case_History_Text: I brought my 21-year-old son to the emergency department after EMS was called this afternoon. He works at a daycare and had slept poorly for several nights because of an unpredictable schedule. Earlier today, he complained of a headache and said he felt unsteady while walking. A short time later, he suddenly became quiet, seemed confused, and briefly lost consciousness. When he woke, he was slow to answer and reported numbness with weakness that came and went, though he could move both sides by the time we arrived. He still seems tired and occasionally has trouble finding his words and keeping his balance. I have not seen anything like this happen to him before.
Model_Diagnosis: New-onset focal seizure with postictal Todd paralysis

Symptoms: transient loss of consciousness; confusion afterward; brief weakness; intermittent numbness; slurred speech for several minutes; headache; nausea; recent sleep deprivation
Case_History_Text: Hello, I’m a 69-year-old software engineer who was brought to the emergency department by my coworker. Since last night, I have had several unusual episodes. I briefly lost consciousness while sitting at home and woke feeling confused and unusually tired. I noticed temporary weakness and numbness, more noticeable on one side, but these symptoms improved before arrival. This morning, my coworker observed that my speech sounded slurred for a few minutes, and I had trouble following the conversation. I have also had a headache and nausea without vomiting. I have been sleeping poorly while completing a software project. My medical history includes diabetes. I do not recall any recent injury, fever, or new medication.

Symptoms: transient weakness; numbness; confusion; loss of consciousness; trouble keeping balance; headache; blurred vision; nausea
Case_History_Text: EMS handoff: We brought a 23-year-old man from his apartment after his adult daughter called for intermittent episodes beginning yesterday evening. He works as a security guard and reports several nights of very poor sleep and regular cigarette use. He describes numbness and weakness that have come and gone, with occasional trouble keeping his balance, blurred vision, nausea, and a headache. His daughter witnessed him briefly lose consciousness this morning; afterward he was confused and slow to answer for several minutes. She noticed his left hand seemed clumsy during one episode, though he is moving all extremities on arrival. No 12-lead interpretation available.

Symptoms: transient weakness; numbness; confusion; loss of consciousness; trouble keeping balance; fatigue
Case_History_Text: A 27-year-old woman who works on a nearby farm arrived alone to the emergency department after feeling unwell for most of the day. She reports that she became unusually tired in the morning, then developed tingling and a sense of weakness affecting one side of her body, though she is unsure which side and says it resolved before arrival. While outside the farmhouse, she became unsteady, had difficulty keeping her balance, and briefly lost consciousness. She has limited memory of the event and describes several minutes afterward when she felt confused and had trouble organizing her thoughts. By the time of evaluation, her strength and sensation subjectively felt nearly normal, but she continued to feel fatigued and mildly “foggy.” She denies a persistent headache, chest discomfort, or recent fever. She has smoked cigarettes for several years and takes no regular medications. No similar episode is clearly documented, and she is unable to provide a witness account because she came to the department by herself.

Symptoms: transient weakness; numbness; confusion; loss of consciousness; headache; fatigue; nausea
Case_History_Text: I’m 47 and drive a city bus. About two hours ago, while getting ready for work, I suddenly felt weak and had tingling in one hand. My spouse says I became unresponsive for a short time, though I don’t remember that part. When I came around, I was confused about where I was and had trouble finding the right words, but that improved before EMS arrived. I still feel tired, mildly nauseated, and have a dull headache. I may have been slower with my left side, although I’m not sure. I’ve had a couple of similar spells in the past that resolved on their own. I have been sleeping poorly because of extra shifts. My spouse came with me to the emergency department.
Model_Diagnosis: Focal seizure with postictal confusion (possible Todd paralysis)

Symptoms: transient weakness; numbness; confusion; brief loss of consciousness; blurred vision; slurred speech; nausea; fatigue
Case_History_Text: 49-year-old woman, librarian, arrived alone to ED. Reports episode beginning about 6 hrs ago while shelving books: sudden fatigue, blurred vision, nausea, and brief slurred speech, followed by numbness and heaviness affecting one side, then loss of consciousness witnessed by a coworker. On waking, she was confused and had difficulty recalling several minutes; weakness and numbness gradually improved. She describes a second brief period of disorientation en route and ongoing tiredness, without clear persistent deficit. Has slept poorly for several nights and smokes. Denies recent injury. Triage note: awake, conversant, mildly slow to answer, ambulatory.
Model_Diagnosis: Focal seizure with postictal Todd paralysis

Symptoms: transient weakness; numbness; confusion; loss of consciousness; headache; brief slurred speech
Case_History_Text: I brought my 74-year-old husband to the emergency department after calling EMS this afternoon. Over the past three hours, he has had several brief changes from his usual self. He first complained of a dull headache and tingling in one hand, then became unsteady and seemed unable to use that hand normally for a short time. His speech sounded slurred for a few minutes. Later, while sitting at the kitchen table, he stopped responding and briefly lost consciousness. When he awakened, he was confused and asked the same questions repeatedly, although his strength and sensation gradually seemed to improve. He has been awake much of the night caring for our dog and has slept poorly for several days. He is a retired nurse and has no known similar episode.
Model_Diagnosis: Focal-onset seizure with postictal confusion (Todd paralysis)

Symptoms: transient weakness; numbness; confusion; brief loss of consciousness; nausea; blurred vision; headache
Case_History_Text: Hello, I am writing for my coworker, a 73-year-old woman who works with me at a daycare and has just arrived in the emergency department. About 45 minutes ago, while helping with lunch, she suddenly complained of a headache, nausea, and blurred vision. She became confused, seemed briefly weak and numb on one side, and then lost consciousness for a short time. She was awake again within minutes but initially had trouble answering simple questions and appeared very tired. Her strength and sensation have improved, though she is not quite herself yet. She has slept poorly for several nights, smokes, and had no recent illness or injury that we know of. I am staying with her and can provide more details.

Symptoms: transient weakness; numbness; confusion; loss of consciousness; nausea; impaired balance; brief slurred speech; blurred vision; fatigue after poor sleep
Case_History_Text: EMS reports a 61-year-old man, a retail manager, brought from home after his partner called for assistance. He had been sleeping poorly for several nights and experienced nausea, blurred vision, and trouble keeping his balance during the day. This evening he briefly lost consciousness, followed by confusion and weakness with numbness that seemed slightly more noticeable in one hand. His speech sounded slurred for a few minutes, then improved before arrival. He remains tired and intermittently slow to answer but follows conversation. He reports no similar prior episode. His father had atrial fibrillation. He arrived alone in the ambulance.
Model_Diagnosis: Acute ischemic stroke (transient ischemic attack with persistent neurologic symptoms)

Symptoms: transient weakness; numbness; confusion; loss of consciousness; nausea; headache
Case_History_Text: A 50-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by a neighbor for an episode that began last night. She is an accountant and had reportedly been sleeping poorly for several days while finishing work. According to the neighbor, she was standing in her kitchen when she became quiet, appeared briefly unresponsive, and slumped to the floor. Afterward, she was confused and slow to answer questions, with intermittent difficulty describing numbness and weakness that seemed more noticeable on one side but was not consistently reproduced. The neighbor did not observe clear shaking, though the event was partly obscured by the fall. The patient recalls feeling nauseated and developing a headache earlier in the evening but has limited memory of the episode itself. She reports that the weakness and numbness improved before arrival, although she still feels “foggy” and mildly fatigued. She denies recent head injury, fever, chest discomfort, or shortness of breath. Her neighbor states that her speech has sounded normal during transport.
Model_Diagnosis: Focal-onset seizure with postictal confusion and Todd paralysis

Symptoms: transient weakness; numbness in one arm; confusion; brief loss of consciousness; blurred vision; headache; intermittent episodes since yesterday evening
Case_History_Text: I am 76 and retired from teaching. Since yesterday evening, I have had spells that come and go. My right arm felt numb and weak at times, and my vision became blurry. I also developed a headache and felt confused about where I was for a few minutes. This morning, I briefly lost consciousness while talking with a former coworker. When I woke up, I was tired and had trouble finding the right words, but that improved before EMS arrived. My coworker called for help and came with me to the emergency department. I have slept poorly for several nights and feel worn out. My parent had atrial fibrillation, but I have not had similar episodes before.

Symptoms: transient weakness; numbness in one arm; confusion; brief loss of consciousness; nausea; fatigue; slurred speech for several minutes
Case_History_Text: 28-year-old woman, software engineer, brought to ED by spouse after several episodes of feeling unwell over most of today. Spouse reports she briefly lost consciousness, then appeared confused and had slurred speech for a few minutes. Patient describes transient weakness and numbness in one arm, now largely resolved, with persistent fatigue and nausea. She has slept poorly for several nights. PMH includes high blood pressure; no known prior similar events. Her parent has atrial fibrillation. Arrived ambulatory with spouse, answering questions but needing occasional clarification about the sequence of events.

Symptoms: transient weakness; numbness in one hand; confusion; brief loss of consciousness; fatigue; headache; prior similar spells
Case_History_Text: I brought my 21-year-old nephew to the emergency department after his adult son called EMS from their apartment. About two hours ago, while studying for a college exam, he complained of a sudden headache and feeling unusually tired. He then became quiet, seemed confused, and briefly lost consciousness in his chair. When he woke, he said one hand felt numb and appeared briefly unsteady, though the weakness improved before EMS arrived. He could answer questions but needed extra time and repeatedly asked what had happened. He has had a few shorter spells like this over the past year, involving tiredness, a headache, and temporary confusion, but has never been evaluated during one. He denies recent injury, and his son says he had been well earlier today.

Symptoms: transient weakness; numbness; confusion; loss of consciousness; brief slurred speech; blurred vision; fatigue
Case_History_Text: Hello, I am 71 and came to the emergency department by myself. About six hours ago, while making coffee, I suddenly felt weak and numb, with one arm seeming clumsy and my vision becoming blurred. I remember trying to sit down, then losing consciousness briefly. When I became aware again, I was confused and very tired. My speech sounded slurred for a few minutes, according to a neighbor I called afterward, but it returned to normal. I still feel drained and occasionally have trouble finding the right words, though I can walk. I have slept poorly for several nights and smoke regularly. I am a retired mechanic and do not usually have episodes like this.

Symptoms: transient weakness; numbness in one arm; confusion; brief loss of consciousness; nausea; fatigue; headache; several nights of poor sleep
Case_History_Text: EMS handoff: This is a 56-year-old man, a construction foreman, brought in by his adult daughter after we were called to their home. She reports that over the past three hours he complained of a headache, nausea, and unusual fatigue, then became briefly unresponsive while seated. On waking, he was confused and had trouble moving and feeling one arm, though those symptoms improved before arrival. He has been sleeping poorly for several nights and has diabetes. He denies known recent injury. He is now awake, speaking clearly, and following directions, with mild residual tiredness.

Symptoms: transient weakness; numbness; confusion; loss of consciousness; blurred vision; nausea
Case_History_Text: A 50-year-old woman who works as a librarian was brought to the emergency department by a neighbor after an abrupt episode at home approximately 45 minutes before arrival. The neighbor reports that she had been speaking normally when she complained of blurred vision and nausea, then became briefly unresponsive while seated. On waking, she appeared confused and had difficulty describing what had happened. She reported heaviness and reduced sensation affecting one side of her body, though the exact distribution was unclear and symptoms improved during transport. By the time of evaluation, she was able to follow conversation but remained mildly slow to answer and intermittently repeated questions. She denied recent trauma. The neighbor was unsure whether there had been any unusual movements during the brief period of unresponsiveness. Her symptoms had largely resolved, aside from mild queasiness and subjective tingling. Her history includes diabetes managed through routine outpatient care. She lives alone and had been preparing to leave for work when the event occurred.

Symptoms: left-sided arm and leg weakness; tingling of the left face and hand; blurred vision; difficulty finding words; nausea; fatigue
Case_History_Text: A 27-year-old woman who works as a rideshare driver presents to the emergency department with a coworker for 45 minutes of sudden neurologic symptoms. She reports that while waiting for a passenger, her left hand began tingling, followed by a sensation of heaviness in the left arm and leg. She noticed blurred vision affecting one side of her view and felt that her speech was slowed, with difficulty finding familiar words. Her coworker says she remained awake and understood questions but sounded different than usual. She describes mild nausea and marked fatigue without vomiting. She denies a severe headache, recent injury, chest discomfort, shortness of breath, or loss of consciousness. Her history includes high blood pressure, though she is unsure of the names of her medications and may have missed a dose today. She reports no prior episodes of similar symptoms and no known neurologic disorder. She arrived walking with assistance from her coworker.

Symptoms: left-sided arm and leg weakness; tingling on the left side of the face; intermittent blurred vision; brief slurred speech; fatigue; nausea
Case_History_Text: I’m 42 and a college student, and my spouse came with me after calling EMS today. Since yesterday, my left hand and leg have felt weak and intermittently tingly, with a strange numb feeling along the left side of my face. My vision has been blurred at times, mostly in one eye, and I had a few minutes when my speech sounded slurred. That passed, but I still feel like I’m not speaking normally. I’ve also been unusually tired and mildly nauseated. I have been sleeping very little while finishing a major assignment and assumed that was catching up with me. I do not usually have medical problems. My parent has atrial fibrillation, which worries me, but I have never been told I have it.

Symptoms: left arm numbness and weakness; blurred vision; brief slurred speech; nausea; symptoms began last night
Case_History_Text: 23-year-old woman, welder, presents to ED with coworker for intermittent left arm numbness and subjective weakness beginning last night. Reports blurred vision and nausea, with a few minutes of slurred speech earlier today that resolved before arrival. She continues to notice visual blurring and clumsiness using the left hand. Denies recent injury. Smokes cigarettes; history notable for diabetes. Her parent has atrial fibrillation. No prior similar episodes reported. Awake and conversant at triage, but describes symptoms as fluctuating since onset.

Symptoms: intermittent right-sided weakness and numbness; blurred vision; trouble finding words; fatigue; unsteady balance
Case_History_Text: I brought my 28-year-old husband to the emergency department after calling EMS this morning. He works as a retail manager and first complained yesterday evening that his right hand and leg felt heavy and numb. He also said his vision was blurry in one eye and that he was having trouble getting words out. The symptoms eased after a while but returned several times overnight and again while we were getting ready to leave. He has been unusually tired and has stumbled when walking, needing to hold onto furniture. He had two shorter spells like this over the past year, but they resolved before we sought care, and he has never been given a clear explanation. He remained awake and understood what was happening throughout.

Symptoms: left-sided arm and leg weakness; tingling on the left side; blurred vision; trouble finding words; nausea; unsteady balance
Case_History_Text: I’m a 26-year-old software engineer and came to the emergency department alone because I’ve felt increasingly unwell for most of today. It started with tingling in my left hand, then my arm and leg felt weak and awkward. My vision has been blurred, mostly on the left, and I’ve had trouble finding words even though I know what I want to say. I feel nauseated and have been unsteady when walking. I had a similar episode of visual blurring several years ago that resolved, but I was never given a clear explanation. My parent has atrial fibrillation. I take no regular medications and have not had any recent illness or injury.

Symptoms: left-sided arm numbness and weakness; blurred vision; difficulty speaking; headache; trouble keeping balance; symptom onset about two hours ago
Case_History_Text: EMS brings a 25-year-old man from an auto repair shop to the emergency department with his coworker, who reports symptoms began roughly two hours ago while they were working. The patient describes sudden blurred vision, a headache, trouble keeping his balance, and numbness with weakness in his left arm. His speech has been difficult for the coworker to understand, though he remains able to answer simple questions. He recalls a similar episode of visual disturbance several years ago that resolved without a clear explanation and says heat commonly makes him unusually fatigued. His father has atrial fibrillation. No known neurologic diagnosis is reported.

Symptoms: left-sided arm and leg weakness with tingling; blurred vision in the right eye; difficulty finding words; unsteady balance; fatigue
Case_History_Text: A 43-year-old woman who works as an auto mechanic was brought to the emergency department by a neighbor for approximately six hours of left-sided arm and leg weakness with tingling. She reports that the symptoms began while she was at home after finishing an early shift, initially as clumsiness in her left hand, followed by trouble walking steadily. She has also noticed intermittent blurring of vision in her right eye and difficulty getting words out clearly, though she understands what others are saying. She describes feeling unusually fatigued but denies fainting. Her neighbor says she seemed slower to respond than usual but remained awake and cooperative. She has a history of high blood pressure and takes a daily medication, although she is unsure whether she took it this morning. She reports no recent injury and no similar prior episode. On arrival, she is able to provide the history but pauses occasionally while speaking.

Symptoms: left-sided weakness and numbness; blurred vision; trouble finding words; headache; difficulty keeping balance
Case_History_Text: I’m 24 and coach at a high school. About three hours ago, while getting ready for practice, my left hand and leg started feeling numb and weak. My vision became blurry, and I had trouble getting words out clearly when I called my neighbor. I’ve also had a headache and feel unsteady when I walk, like I might veer to one side. I was up late several nights this week preparing for games, so I’m exhausted. I’ve had a couple of shorter spells in the past where my vision or sensation felt unusual, but they went away and I never found out why. My neighbor stayed with me and called EMS, and I came to the emergency department.

Symptoms: left-sided arm and leg weakness with numbness; transient slurred speech; blurred vision; headache; nausea; fatigue
Case_History_Text: 44-year-old woman, bus driver, brought to ED by adult daughter for sudden left arm and leg heaviness with tingling and blurred vision beginning 45 min PTA. Daughter reports speech sounded slurred for several minutes, now improved. Pt notes a dull headache, nausea, and marked fatigue after several nights of poor sleep. Hx of high blood pressure; no known prior neurologic diagnosis. Reports an episode of visual disturbance in one eye several years ago that resolved without explanation. Awake and cooperative, speaking in short clear phrases at triage, with persistent subjective left-sided weakness and numbness.

Symptoms: left arm numbness and weakness; blurred vision in the right eye; trouble finding words; headache; symptoms progressing over the past day
Case_History_Text: I brought my 30-year-old husband to the emergency department after calling EMS this evening. He works as a librarian and was shelving books yesterday when he mentioned tingling in his left hand. Over the day, the numbness seemed to spread up his arm, and he began having trouble using it normally. He also complained of a headache and said the vision in his right eye looked blurred. This afternoon, he struggled to find ordinary words during a conversation, though he seemed to understand what I was saying. He has not had anything like this before. He takes no regular medications, and his father has atrial fibrillation. He remained awake and able to walk with me to the ambulance.

Symptoms: Left-sided arm numbness and weakness; intermittent blurred vision; trouble getting words out; headache; nausea; fatigue worsened by heat
Case_History_Text: Hello, I am a 23-year-old woman and work as a security guard. Since last night, my left arm has felt numb and weaker than usual, and I have had episodes of blurred vision. My daughter noticed that I was pausing and having trouble getting some words out this morning, so she brought me to the emergency department. I also have a headache and feel nauseated, though I have not vomited. I have diabetes and often become unusually tired when I am overheated, but this feels different and has not fully gone away after resting. I am worried because the symptoms have continued since they began last night.

Symptoms: intermittent left-sided weakness and numbness; blurred vision; episodes of slowed or unclear speech; fatigue; nausea; headache
Case_History_Text: EMS handoff: We were called for a 46-year-old man, an accountant, whose spouse noticed intermittent left-sided weakness and numbness beginning yesterday evening. He reports several episodes of blurred vision and difficulty getting words out, with symptoms improving and then returning. He also describes fatigue, mild nausea, and a headache. He has had very little sleep recently and says heat has caused pronounced fatigue in the past. His spouse recalls one or two similar, shorter spells over the last year, though he has never received a firm explanation. He arrived with his spouse for further evaluation.

Symptoms: left-sided arm and leg weakness; tingling of the left hand; blurred vision; brief slurred speech; fatigue
Case_History_Text: A 22-year-old unemployed woman was brought to the emergency department by a neighbor after developing neurologic symptoms over most of today. She first noticed tingling in her left fingertips while preparing breakfast, followed by a heavy sensation and weakness involving the left arm and leg. She has been walking slowly but has not fallen. Around midday, she experienced blurred vision, which she describes as difficulty bringing objects into focus rather than complete loss of sight. Her neighbor reports that her speech sounded slurred for several minutes during a phone conversation; the patient recalls knowing what she wanted to say but having trouble speaking clearly. The speech change resolved before arrival, while the weakness and altered sensation have persisted with some fluctuation. She denies recent injury, loss of consciousness, or seizure-like activity. She smokes cigarettes and takes no daily medications. Her neighbor says she has seemed tired and mildly anxious today.

Symptoms: left-sided arm and leg weakness; numbness around the left hand and cheek; blurred vision; brief slurred speech; trouble keeping balance; fatigue
Case_History_Text: I’m 48 and work as a pharmacist. About two hours ago, while getting ready for work, my left hand started feeling numb, and then my left leg felt weak and unsteady. I noticed blurred vision and had trouble focusing on the words in front of me. For a few minutes, my speech sounded slurred, although I knew what I wanted to say. I had to hold onto the counter because I was having trouble keeping my balance. I feel unusually tired now, but I do not have severe pain. I have been sleeping poorly for the past week and have a history of high blood pressure. I called EMS and came to the emergency department alone.

Symptoms: left arm numbness and weakness; blurred vision; brief slurred speech; unsteady gait; fatigue
Case_History_Text: 36F software engineer brought to ED by coworker for approx 6 hrs of intermittent neurologic symptoms. Reports left arm numbness with mild weakness, blurred vision, and trouble keeping balance. Had several minutes of slurred speech earlier, now resolved. Symptoms began after several nights of poor sleep and worsened while working in a hot office; fatigue noted. Denies recent injury. Coworker states she appeared unsteady but remained awake and able to follow conversation. PMH notable for intermittently high BP; no prior similar episode reported. Triage note: alert, speaking clearly at present, ambulatory with assistance.

Symptoms: right-sided arm and leg weakness; numbness on the right side; blurred vision; brief slurred speech; difficulty speaking clearly
Case_History_Text: I brought my 26-year-old brother to the emergency department after calling EMS from his apartment. He drives for a rideshare service and had been getting ready for work when he said the right side of his body felt numb and weak. Over the next three hours, he had trouble using his right hand and walking normally. He also complained that his vision was blurry. At one point, his speech sounded slurred for several minutes, and he seemed frustrated when trying to explain what he meant. The symptoms have fluctuated but have not completely gone away. He has a history of high blood pressure but is usually independent and active. His adult daughter came with us and helped provide the timeline.

Symptoms: right arm numbness and weakness; blurred vision; difficulty finding words; sudden fatigue
Case_History_Text: Hello, I’m a 44-year-old woman and a college student. My spouse is bringing me to the emergency department because about 45 minutes ago my right hand and arm began feeling numb and weak.
